definition_zh: 条件化过程；使刺激与反应逐步建立联结的训练程序
definition_en: the procedure through which a response becomes attached to a stimulus or to its consequences by repeated pairing or reinforcement
core_image: 隔音实验房里，铃声与食物按同一次序反复出现，笼中的动物从漠然转为听到铃声就转向食盘，记录纸带上的曲线一天天变陡。
scene: 隔音实验房里，研究者把铃声与食物按固定次序反复呈现，笼中的动物从最初的漠然转为听到铃声就转向食盘，纸带上的曲线一天天变陡。The conditioning process turned a random pairing into a reliable habit within three weeks.
sceneCN: 这里指把刺激与反应反复配对、使联结逐渐稳固的那一整套程序（第 1 个义项：作为整体程序）；句意为条件化过程在三个星期内把随机的配对变成了可靠的习惯。

pos.zh: 条件化过程；条件作用程序（心理学术语）
（作定语）条件化训练的，如条件化过程研究

collocations.phrase: a conditioning process in animal training
collocations.zh: 动物训练中的条件化过程

derivatives.zh: 条件；使形成条件反射（拉丁 condicio「约定、状况」，由「约定之事」转指「前提」，动词义再转指「设定反应的条件」）
已形成条件反射的；受条件限制的（在「条件」后加表被动的分词词尾，由「设定条件」转指「已被塑造」）
条件作用；条件化（在动词后加表动作的名词词尾，由动作转指该过程本身）
有条件的（加拉丁关系形容词词尾，由「约定」转指「以约定为前提的」）
调节剂；护发素（加表施事或工具的词尾，由「调节」转指「起调节作用之物」）
先决条件（在前加一个表「预先」的成分，由「条件」转指「须先满足者」）

senses.title: The programme that builds the link
senses.definition: the whole procedure by which a response is made to depend on a particular signal
senses.definitionCN: 使某个反应依赖于特定信号的一整套操作程序
senses.example: The conditioning process took three weeks before the bell alone produced the turn.
senses.exampleCN: 条件化过程用了三个星期，才做到只响铃就引起转身。
senses.why: The phrase names the procedure as a whole, not one step of it, so the article the is usual.
senses.whyCN: 这个词组把整套操作当作一个对象来命名，而不是指其中某一步，因此通常带定冠词。

senses.title: Classical pairing of two stimuli
senses.titleCN: 经典条件化：两个刺激反复同时出现
senses.definition: the procedure in which a neutral stimulus is presented together with a second stimulus until it alone calls up the response
senses.definitionCN: 把中性刺激与另一个刺激反复同时呈现，直到前者单独就能唤起反应的程序
senses.example: In the classical conditioning process the light is paired with food on every trial.
senses.exampleCN: 在经典条件化过程里，每一次试验都把灯光与食物配对。
senses.why: Pairing works because the two events arrive together often enough for one to stand in for the other.
senses.whyCN: 配对之所以有效，是因为两个事件同时到来的次数足够多，其中一个便可代表另一个。

senses.title: Operant shaping by consequences
senses.titleCN: 操作性条件化：由后果塑造反应
senses.definition: the procedure in which a response is made more or less frequent by what follows it
senses.definitionCN: 由反应之后出现的结果来增减该反应发生频率的程序
senses.example: In the operant conditioning process the reward follows the lever press, not the bell.
senses.exampleCN: 在操作性条件化过程里，跟着拉杆动作的是奖励，而不是铃声。
senses.why: Here the shaping force is the consequence, which is why the route is called operant rather than classical.
senses.whyCN: 此处的塑造力量是后果，所以这条路线称操作性路线，而不是经典路线。

senses.title: The course as it unfolds in time
senses.titleCN: 过程义：随时间逐步展开的历程
senses.definition: the gradual course over which the link strengthens, from the first pairing to a settled response
senses.definitionCN: 联结由最初配对到稳定反应所经历的渐次历程
senses.example: The conditioning process shows a slow rise at first and a steep climb after the tenth trial.
senses.exampleCN: 条件化过程起初上升缓慢，第十次试验之后才陡然变陡。
senses.why: The word process contributes exactly this meaning: an interval with stages, not a single act.
senses.whyCN: 过程一词带来的正是这层意思：有阶段的时段，而非一次完成的动作。

senses.title: Animal training in practice
senses.definition: the practical routine by which a trainer teaches an animal to answer a cue
senses.definitionCN: 训练者教会动物对某个提示作出反应的实务流程
senses.example: Keepers shorten the conditioning process by using the same whistle before every feed.
senses.exampleCN: 饲养员在每次投食前都吹同一个哨子，以此缩短条件化过程。
senses.why: Zoos and laboratories inherited the laboratory procedure and kept the name for the daily routine.
senses.whyCN: 动物园与实验室继承了这套实验程序，也把这个名称留给了日常操作。

senses.title: Habit formation in everyday life
senses.titleCN: 日常生活中的习惯养成
senses.definition: the repeated arrangement by which an ordinary cue comes to trigger a habitual act
senses.definitionCN: 通过反复安排，使日常线索自动引起习惯性动作的过程
senses.example: Advertising relies on the conditioning process, showing the same tune beside the same product for years.
senses.exampleCN: 广告依靠条件化过程，多年如一日地把同一段旋律与同一件商品并置。
senses.why: Outside the laboratory the pairing is done by repetition of daily life rather than by a controlled schedule.
senses.whyCN: 出了实验室，配对由日常生活的重复完成，而不是由受控的时间表完成。

senses.title: A laboratory protocol
senses.definition: the written sequence of steps a laboratory follows to produce the link reliably
senses.definitionCN: 实验室为稳定地产生该联结而遵循的书面步骤序列
senses.example: The manual describes the conditioning process step by step, with the inter-trial interval fixed.
senses.exampleCN: 手册逐步写明条件化过程，并把试次之间的间隔固定下来。
senses.why: Once the procedure is written down it becomes a protocol, and the phrase shifts from behaviour to method.
senses.whyCN: 程序一旦写成文字便成为规程，这个词组也就从描述行为转为描述方法。

senses.title: Adaptation to repeated conditions
senses.titleCN: 对反复环境条件的适应
senses.definition: the gradual adjustment of a body to repeated heat, cold, altitude or effort
senses.definitionCN: 身体对反复出现的炎热、寒冷、高海拔或负荷所作的渐次调整
senses.example: Athletes use a conditioning process in the heat chamber before competing in the tropics.
senses.exampleCN: 运动员在奔赴热带比赛之前，会在热舱里进行一段条件化过程。
senses.why: Physiology borrowed the phrase because repeated exposure produces a stable response, just as pairing does.
senses.whyCN: 生理学借用这个词组，因为反复暴露也会产生稳定反应，与配对的作用相同。

intro.en: Conditioning is English condition plus the noun suffix -ing, and condition goes back through Old French to Latin condicio 'agreement, situation', from condicere 'to agree upon'. Process comes from Latin processus 'a going forward', from procedere. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: conditioning 是英语 condition 加表动作的名词词尾构成，condition 经古法语上溯拉丁 condicio「约定、状况」，来自 condicere「共同说定」。process 来自拉丁 processus「向前行进」，出自 procedere。年代均为约数。

items.en: Condicere meant 'to say together, agree upon', built from com- 'together' plus dicere 'to say, point out'. The deeper origin of dicere is reconstructed as a root meaning 'to show', and that root is a reconstruction rather than a recorded form.
items.cn: condicere 意为「一起说定、约定」，由表「共同」的前缀加 dicere「说、指出」构成。dicere 的更早来源被重构为一个意为「显示」的词根，那只是重构形式，并非有记录的形式。

items.en: Condicio named an agreement, a stipulation, and by extension the situation in which something stands. The sense of 'state something is in' is the one English condition first took over.
items.cn: condicio 指约定、条款，并引申为某物所处的状况。英语 condition 最先接手的正是「某物所处的状态」这一义。

items.en: Old French condicion carried the word into English in the twelfth century, where it named both a stipulation and a state of affairs.
items.cn: 古法语 condicion 在十二世纪把这个词带入英语，既指条款，也指事态。

items.en: Processus 'a going forward, an advance' came from procedere, built from pro- 'forward' plus cedere 'to go, yield'. The deeper origin of cedere is a reconstruction, often given as a root meaning 'to go'.
items.cn: processus「向前行进、推进」出自 procedere，由表「向前」的前缀加 cedere「走、让」构成。cedere 的更早来源属重构形式，常被写作一个意为「走」的词根。

items.en: Twentieth-century psychology gave conditioning its technical sense, first for the pairing of stimuli and then for shaping by consequences. The full phrase conditioning process names the procedure rather than a single trial.
items.cn: 二十世纪心理学赋予 conditioning 技术含义，先指刺激配对，后指由后果塑造反应。完整词组 conditioning process 指整套程序，而非单次试验。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper origin): no exact first citation is recorded for the compound, and the pre-Latin origins of dicere and cedere are reconstructions, so any older form offered for them is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：这个词组没有确切的最早书证；dicere 与 cedere 在拉丁语之前的来源均属重构形式，凡为其给出的更早形式都是重构。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same Latin verb and the same noun of stating; group two holds words from the study of learning that sit close but are not synonyms.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁动词与「陈述」名词的词；第二组是学习研究中含义相近但并不等同的词。

entries.definition: The noun for a state or a stipulation and the verb for making something depend on a factor; it lacks the sense of a course of training.
entries.definitionCN: 指状态或条款的名词，也指使某物取决于某因素的动作；不含「一段训练历程」之义。

entries.definition: An adjective for a response or a person already shaped by training; it describes the result, while the phrase names the working procedure.
entries.definitionCN: 指已被训练塑成的反应或人；它描述结果，而词组描述正在运行的程序。

entries.definition: Means depending on a stated term, as in a conditional offer; it belongs to grammar and law rather than to learning.
entries.definitionCN: 意为以某项说明的条件为前提，如有条件录用；属语法与法律用语，与学习过程无关。

entries.definition: Something that must be true before anything else can start, or to prepare someone in advance; it stresses what comes first.
entries.definitionCN: 指必须先成立的前提，或预先使人做好准备；强调「在先」。

entries.definition: The everyday word for teaching a skill by practice; it covers drills, coaching and instruction, of which conditioning is one narrow method.
entries.definitionCN: 指通过练习传授技能的日常用词，涵盖操练、辅导与讲授，条件化只是其中一种狭窄方法。

entries.definition: The weakening of a response after mere repeated exposure, with no reward and no paired stimulus; it is non-associative, so it is not conditioning.
entries.definitionCN: 指仅因反复暴露而使反应减弱，既无奖励也无配对刺激；它属非联想学习，因此不是条件化。

entries.definition: The consequence that raises the frequency of a response; it is a part of the operant procedure, not the whole course.
entries.definitionCN: 指提高反应频率的后果；它是操作性程序的一个组成部分，而非整段历程。

entries.definition: The body's adjustment to heat, cold or altitude; it overlaps the physiological sense of the phrase but implies no signal and no response.
entries.definitionCN: 指身体对炎热、寒冷或海拔的适应；与词组的生理义重叠，但不含信号与反应。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: 'condition' plus 'process': a state made to depend on a signal, run again and again until it holds.
normal.cn: 「条件」加「过程」：让状态取决于某个信号，一遍遍跑到它站住为止。

normal.en: Latin condicere is 'to say together': the bell and the food are said together until the bell alone speaks.
normal.cn: 拉丁 condicere 是「一起说定」：铃声与食物被说定要一起出现，直到铃声单独也能说话。

normal.en: The family splits in two: condition, conditional and precondition speak of terms, while conditioning and conditioned speak of being shaped.
normal.cn: 同族词分成两路：condition、conditional、precondition 说「前提」，conditioning 与 conditioned 说「被塑成」。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the two laboratory routes: the classical conditioning process and the operant conditioning process.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出两条实验室路线：经典条件化过程与操作性条件化过程。

normal.en: The head noun is process, so the phrase always carries the idea of stages rather than of one act.
normal.cn: 中心词是「过程」，因此这个词组始终带「有阶段」的意思，而不是一次完成的动作。

abstract.en: Picture a path worn into grass by the same feet: the first walk needs looking, the hundredth turns itself.
abstract.cn: 想象一条被同一双脚踩进草地的小径：第一次还得找路，第一百次脚自己就拐弯。

abstract.en: Picture a bell and a door tied by one string: pull either end and the other must move.
abstract.cn: 想象铃与门被一根绳系住：拉任何一头，另一头必动。

abstract.en: Picture clay pressed by the same hand on a wheel until the shape arrives without being watched.
abstract.cn: 想象转盘上的陶土被同一只手反复按压，最后不看也知道形状该往哪里去。

examples.en: The conditioning process took three weeks before the bell alone produced the turn.
examples.cn: 条件化过程用了三个星期，才做到只响铃就引起转身。

examples.en: Researchers shortened the conditioning process by pairing the light with food on every trial.
examples.cn: 研究者每一次试验都把灯光与食物配对，从而缩短了条件化过程。

examples.en: In operant terms the conditioning process is driven by consequences rather than by pairing.
examples.cn: 就操作性路线而言，条件化过程由后果推动，而不是由配对推动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「条件」+「过程」——把「反应取决于某个信号」这件事反复跑成固定流程；经典路线靠配对，操作路线靠后果。

root: conditioning：英语 condition 加表动作的名词词尾；condition 出自拉丁 condicio「约定、状况」，来自 condicere「共同说定」= 表「共同」的前缀 + dicere「说」。process：拉丁 processus「向前行进」，来自 procedere「向前走」= 表「向前」的前缀 + cedere「走」。两词在拉丁语之前的更深来源均为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one gesture: an arbitrary signal is repeated beside a real event until the signal alone carries the response. The gesture is then read as a whole programme, as two laboratory routes, as a course in time, as animal routine, as everyday habit, as a written protocol, and finally as a body adjusting to its climate.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：把一个任意信号与一个真实事件反复并置，直到信号单独就能带出反应。这个动作再依次读作整套程序、两条实验室路线、一段时间历程、动物日常操作、生活里的习惯、书面规程，最后是身体对环境的适应。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bell and a bowl brought side by side often enough that the bell begins to do the bowl's work.
core.cn: 核心意象：铃与食盆被并置得足够多次，最后铃开始干食盆的活。

branches.en: THE PROGRAMME AND ITS CLOCK: first the whole procedure, then the same procedure seen as a span with stages.
branches.cn: 整套程序与它的时钟：先看整套操作，再把它看作有阶段的一段时间。

branches.en: TWO LABORATORY ROUTES: pairing two stimuli, and shaping by what follows the act.
branches.cn: 两条实验室路线：把两个刺激配对，以及由动作之后的后果来塑造。

branches.en: THE DAILY ROUTINE: the procedure becomes a keeper's morning whistle.
branches.cn: 日常操作：程序变成饲养员早晨的那声哨。

branches.en: PAIRING OUTSIDE THE LAB: the same arrangement is run by ordinary life and by advertising.
branches.cn: 实验室之外的配对：同样的安排由日常生活与广告来完成。

branches.en: FROM METHOD TO BODY: written steps first, then a body adjusting to heat or altitude.
branches.cn: 从方法到身体：先是写下来的步骤，再是身体对炎热或海拔的适应。

intro.en: Both halves of the phrase can be read morpheme by morpheme: a Latin verb of agreeing plus a Latin verb of going forward, each with its own English family.
intro.cn: 词组的两个部分都可按语素读出：一个表「约定」的拉丁动词与一个表「向前走」的拉丁动词，各自带出一串英语同族词。

latinIntro.en: Latin condicere gives condition, conditional, conditioned and precondition; Latin procedere gives proceed, process, procedure and procedural.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 condicere 衍生 condition、conditional、conditioned、precondition；拉丁 procedere 衍生 proceed、process、procedure、procedural。

items.example: The verb named the act of settling terms before the ritual began.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指仪式开始前把条款说定的那个动作。

items.meaning: an agreement, a stipulation, a situation
items.example: Condicio covered both the terms and the state that followed from them.
items.exampleCN: condicio 同时指条款与由条款形成的状态。

items.meaning: a state; to make something depend on a factor
items.example: The test conditions were held constant.
items.exampleCN: 测试条件保持恒定。

items.meaning: the act or process of shaping a response
items.meaningCN: 塑造反应的动作或过程
items.example: Conditioning was run in a soundproof room.
items.exampleCN: 条件化在隔音室里进行。

items.example: The conditioned animal turned at the bell.
items.exampleCN: 已被条件化的动物听到铃声就转身。

items.meaningCN: 以说明的条件为前提的
items.example: The offer was conditional on a medical check.
items.exampleCN: 这份录用以体检合格为前提。

items.example: The verb described a body moving forward through an opening.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词描述身体穿过开口向前移动。

items.example: Processus named the movement before it named the method.
items.exampleCN: processus 先指行进，后指方法。

items.meaning: a course of stages; a method
items.example: The process has four stages.
items.exampleCN: 这个过程有四个阶段。

items.meaning: an established way of doing something
items.example: The procedure was written into the manual.
items.exampleCN: 这套程序被写进手册。

definition_en: a link formed in the mind, or a body of people joined for a shared purpose
core_image: 一张卡片上写着一个名字，名字四周牵出许多细线，连到气味、地点、面孔与一首歌；卡片下方另有一枚圆章，上面刻着一群人的共同名义。
scene: 老式教室里，老师刚说出一个地名，学生脑中立刻浮起那条河的气味、夏日的蝉声和同行者的面孔，几段记忆自己连成一片。The name triggered an association with a river, a summer sound and a familiar face.
sceneCN: 这里指由某个词或景象在脑中牵出的连带记忆（第 1 个义项：心理联想）；句意为这个地名唤起与河流、夏日声响和熟面孔相连的联想。

pos.zh: 联想；协会；关联；联合（心理义可数，指具体联想；结交义不可数）

collocations.zh: 因交往而受牵连的推断

derivatives.zh: 联系；交往 / 同事；准会员 / 副的（拉丁 associare「结伴」，由「结伴」转指「把人或事连在一起」，再转指「同伴」与「次级身份」）
联想的；结合的（加拉丁形容词词尾，由「联结」转指「具有联结性质的」）
社团的；联想性的（在 associative 之后再加关系形容词词尾，由「联结」转指「属于社团或联想活动的」）
使分离；声明与……无关（加表「分开」的前缀，由「联结」转指「解除联结」）
以联想的方式（加副词词尾，由形容词转指动作方式）

senses.title: A link formed in the mind
senses.definition: a mental connection by which one idea brings another to mind
senses.definitionCN: 一种心理联结，由一个念头带出另一个念头
senses.example: The smell of chalk dust carries an association with primary school.
senses.exampleCN: 粉笔灰的气味带着一段与小学相连的联想。
senses.why: The word names the joined pair itself, which is why one speaks of an association rather than of associating.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名的是被连起来的那一对本身，所以说「一个联想」，而不说「一次联想动作」。

senses.title: An organized body of members
senses.definition: a society of people who have joined to pursue a shared interest
senses.definitionCN: 为共同兴趣而联合起来的人的团体
senses.example: The historical association meets on the first Monday of each month.
senses.exampleCN: 这个历史学会每月第一个星期一聚会。
senses.why: A group joined for one purpose is the same joining seen as an institution, so the mental and the social readings share one form.
senses.whyCN: 为同一目的联合起来的群体，就是把「联结」看作一个机构，因此心理义与社会义共用同一个词形。

senses.title: A working partnership
senses.definition: a lasting working relationship between two people or bodies
senses.definitionCN: 两个个人或机构之间长期的工作关系
senses.example: The two clinics announced an association to share laboratory staff.
senses.exampleCN: 两家诊所宣布建立合作，以共用实验室人员。
senses.why: Partnership is a link between parties, which extends the core image from ideas to institutions.
senses.whyCN: 合作是各方之间的一条联结，把核心意象从观念扩展到了机构。

senses.title: Measured dependence between variables
senses.titleCN: 变量之间可测量的相依
senses.definition: a statistical relation in which one variable tends to change with another
senses.definitionCN: 一种统计关系：一个变量倾向于随另一个变量变化
senses.example: The survey reports a strong association between sleep length and mood.
senses.exampleCN: 该调查报告称睡眠时长与情绪之间有很强的相关。
senses.why: Statistics kept the idea of a link but stripped it of meaning: the link is counted, not explained.
senses.whyCN: 统计学保留了「联结」这个想法，却把它抽空：联结只被计数，不被解释。

senses.title: A link learned by pairing
senses.definition: the connection a learner forms between a stimulus and a response or between two events
senses.definitionCN: 学习者在刺激与反应之间、或在两个事件之间形成的联结
senses.example: Repeated pairing builds an association between the sound and the reward.
senses.exampleCN: 反复配对会在声音与奖励之间建立联想。
senses.why: Psychology names the link a learner forms, which keeps the mental sense but adds a subject who acquires it.
senses.whyCN: 心理学指学习者形成的联结，保留心理义，另加「习得者」这一层。

senses.title: Recollection by contiguity
senses.titleCN: 由邻近共现引起的追忆
senses.definition: the way one remembered item brings back another because they were met together
senses.definitionCN: 一个记住的事物因曾与另一事物同时出现而把它带回心头
senses.example: She recalled the harbour by association with the smell of tar.
senses.exampleCN: 她由柏油的气味联想到那个港口。
senses.why: Memory works by nearness: things stored side by side come back side by side, and the word for the pair becomes the word for the route.
senses.whyCN: 记忆靠邻近运作：存放在一起的东西会一起回来，指「那一对」的词于是变成指「那条通路」的词。

senses.title: An inferred link used as evidence
senses.titleCN: 被当作证据的推断性关联
senses.definition: a connection assumed from someone's company or surroundings rather than from proof
senses.definitionCN: 由某人的交往对象或所处环境推定、而非由证据证明的关联
senses.example: The case against him rested on association rather than on evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 对他不利的论证靠的是交往关系，而不是证据。
senses.why: Here the link is treated as if it proved something, which is exactly what the phrase guilt by association warns against.
senses.whyCN: 此处把联结当作已经证明的东西，而这正是「因交往受牵连」一语所要警惕的。

senses.title: A community of species
senses.definition: a recurring group of plants or animals that grow or live together in one habitat
senses.definitionCN: 在同一生境中反复共同生长的植物或动物组合
senses.example: The ecologist mapped the association of oaks and hazel along the slope.
senses.exampleCN: 生态学家标出了坡地上橡树与榛树的群落分布。
senses.why: Ecology borrowed the social sense: species that regularly appear together are read as a body with members.
senses.whyCN: 生态学借用了社会义：经常同时出现的物种被读作一个有成员的团体。

senses.title: The act of joining together
senses.definition: the act of uniting two bodies or interests into one arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 把两个团体或利益合成一项安排的行为
senses.example: The association of the two guilds took three years of negotiation.
senses.exampleCN: 两个行会的联合谈了三年。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer: the bare act of joining, before either the mental link or the club exists.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的一层：单纯的联合动作，在心理联结与俱乐部出现之前。

intro.en: Association comes through French from Latin associare 'to unite with', built on ad- 'to' plus sociare 'to join, share', from socius 'companion, ally'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: association 经法语来自拉丁 associare「与……联合」，由表「朝向」的前缀加 sociare「结伴、共享」构成，后者出自 socius「同伴、盟友」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Socius meant 'companion, ally, partner'. Its deeper origin is not established; the explanation often repeated, that it came from a verb meaning 'to follow', is a hypothesis rather than a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: socius 意为「同伴、盟友、合伙人」。其更深来源未得到证明；常被重复的一种解释是它出自一个意为「跟随」的动词，那只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Sociare meant 'to join, to share, to unite', formed on socius. The verb keeps the sense of making two parties share one arrangement.
items.cn: sociare 意为「联合、共享、使成为一体」，由 socius 构成。这个动词保留「让两方共享一项安排」的意思。

items.en: Ad- 'to, toward' plus sociare produced associare 'to unite with, join to oneself', the direct source of the English noun.
items.cn: 表「朝向」的前缀加 sociare 构成 associare「与……联合、把……结为同伴」，是英语名词的直接来源。

items.en: Old French association entered English in the fourteenth century, first naming a confederation or a society rather than a mental link.
items.cn: 古法语 association 在十四世纪进入英语，最初指同盟或社团，而非心理联结。

items.en: From the seventeenth century the word named the linking of ideas, a theme taken up by the associationist school; the statistical sense of a measured dependence is a nineteenth- and twentieth-century growth.
items.cn: 从十七世纪起，这个词指观念的联结，这一主题由联想主义学派接手；指可测量相依的统计义则是十九至二十世纪的扩展。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper origin): the earliest citation for the psychological sense is not fixed, and the pre-Latin source of socius is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：心理义的最早书证无法确定；socius 在拉丁语之前的来源属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same Latin stock of companionship; group two holds near neighbours that name a link, a membership or a statistical relation.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁「结伴」词干的词；第二组是表示联结、成员身份或统计关系的近义词。

entries.definition: The verb for joining things in the mind or in business, and the noun for a partner or a junior member; the noun association names the link or the body instead.
entries.definitionCN: 指在脑中或业务上把事物连起来的动词，也指同伴或准成员的名称；名词 association 则指那条联结或那个团体。

entries.definition: The adjective for anything that works by linking, as in associative memory; it describes the property, while association names the thing.
entries.definitionCN: 指以联结方式运作的形容词，如联想记忆；它描述性质，而 association 指事物本身。

entries.definition: Means belonging to or organized through associations, as in associational life; it adds the institutional layer only.
entries.definitionCN: 意为属于社团的或经由社团组织的，如社团生活；只加上了机构这一层。

entries.definition: To declare or cause separation, especially from a person or a scandal; it is the exact opposite of joining.
entries.definitionCN: 指声明或造成分离，尤指与某人或某丑闻划清界限；与「联合」正好相反。

entries.definition: The ordinary word for anything joined, from wires to people; it says nothing about memory or membership.
entries.definitionCN: 指被连起来的任何东西，从电线到人；不含记忆或成员身份之义。

entries.definition: The state of being formally attached to a party, church or university; association can be looser and need not be recorded.
entries.definitionCN: 指正式隶属于某党、教会或大学的状态；association 可以更松散，也不必登记。

entries.definition: A formal organization of members, usually with rules and officers; it is one kind of association, not the whole range.
entries.definitionCN: 指有章程与负责人的正式成员组织；它只是 association 的一种，而非全部。

entries.definition: A statistical measure of how two variables move together; the statistical sense of association names the relation, while correlation names its strength.
entries.definitionCN: 指衡量两个变量共同变化的统计量；association 的统计义指那种关系，correlation 指其强度。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin socius 'companion': an association is what companions make when they join.
normal.cn: 拉丁 socius「同伴」：联想与协会都是同伴联合起来的产物。

normal.en: The family runs associate, associative, associational and disassociate, all from one verb of joining.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 associate、associative、associational、disassociate，全出同一个表「联合」的动词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the senses: an association with a person, in association with a partner, a trade association.
normal.cn: 固定搭配分出各义：与某人的关联、与伙伴合作、行业协会。

normal.en: Psychology pairs the word with ideas and with learning: the association of ideas, associative learning.
normal.cn: 心理学把这个词与观念、学习并置：观念的联想、联想学习。

normal.en: The statistical use always asks for a between: a strong association between two variables.
normal.cn: 统计用法总要问「两者之间」：两个变量之间的强相关。

abstract.en: Picture a board where every pin is joined to the next by a thread, and touching one shakes the others.
abstract.cn: 想象一块板，每枚钉子都用线连着下一枚，碰一下这头，那头也动。

abstract.en: Picture a club room where the same name is written on every chair.
abstract.cn: 想象一间社团活动室，每把椅子都写着同一个名字。

abstract.en: Picture two strangers walking in step because they once shared an umbrella.
abstract.cn: 想象两个陌生人步伐一致，只因当年同撑过一把伞。

examples.en: The scent of tar still carries an association with the harbour.
examples.cn: 柏油的气味至今带着与那个港口相连的联想。

examples.en: The association publishes a quarterly journal for its members.
examples.cn: 该协会为会员出版一份季刊。

examples.en: Researchers found an association between noise levels and reading speed.
examples.cn: 研究者发现噪声水平与阅读速度之间存在关联。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「朝向」+「结伴」——把两样东西结到一起：在脑中结是联想，在人之间结是协会，在数据里结是相关。

root: 拉丁 associare「与……联合」= 表「朝向」的前缀 + sociare「结伴、共享」，sociare 出自 socius「同伴、盟友」；socius 更深来源不确定，与「跟随」的联系仅为假说。英语 association 经法语。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one gesture: two things are joined. Joined in the mind gives recall; joined in learning gives a stimulus-response pair; joined often enough gives a measured dependence; joined people give a body, a partnership and an act of union; joined species give an ecological community; and a link assumed rather than proved gives the evidential sense.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿同一个动作展开：把两样东西结在一起。在脑中结，得到联想与追忆；在学习中结，得到刺激与反应的配对；结得足够多，得到可测量的相关；把人结起来，得到团体、合作与联合行为；把物种结起来，得到生态群落；把未经证明的联结当作证据，得到推断义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one name on a card with threads running out to smells, places and faces, and a seal beneath it bearing a shared name.
core.cn: 核心意象：卡片上一个名字牵出通往气味、地点与面孔的细线，卡片下方是一枚刻着共同名义的圆章。

branches.en: THE MENTAL LINK AND ITS RETURN: one idea brings another, and nearness in storage becomes nearness in recall.
branches.cn: 心念中的联结与它的回返：一个念头带出另一个，存放时的邻近变成回想时的邻近。

branches.en: LEARNED THEN COUNTED: pairing builds the link, and statistics measures how closely two variables move.
branches.cn: 先习得再计数：配对建立联结，统计学则量出两个变量一起变动的紧密度。

branches.en: PARTNERS AND THE ACT OF UNION: a lasting working tie, and the bare deed of joining two bodies.
branches.cn: 伙伴与联合之举：长期的工作纽带，以及把两个团体合成一体的那个动作。

branches.en: BODIES WITH MEMBERS: a society of people and a recurring community of species are both read as one body.
branches.cn: 有成员的团体：人的社团与反复共生的物种组合，都被读作一个整体。

branches.en: THE LINK AS EVIDENCE: company is treated as proof, which is the one sense that warns against itself.
branches.cn: 把联结当证据：交往被当作证明，这是唯一自带警告的义项。

intro.en: Association is a Latin verb of joining with a prefix and a suffix around one root, so the whole family reads morpheme by morpheme.
intro.cn: association 是由一个表「结伴」的词根加若干词缀构成的拉丁动词的后代，整个词族都可按语素读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin socius and sociare give social, society, sociable and associate; the prefix ad- adds direction toward.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 socius 与 sociare 衍生 social、society、sociable、associate；表「朝向」的前缀增添方向。

items.example: Socius named the person one joined with.
items.exampleCN: socius 指与自己结伴的那个人。

items.example: The verb described merchants putting their funds into one pool.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词描述商人把资金合成一池。

items.example: Associare bound one party to another.
items.exampleCN: associare 把一方与另一方绑在一起。

items.meaning: the act of joining; a body so formed
items.meaningCN: 联合的行为；由此形成的团体
items.example: The association elected its first chair.
items.exampleCN: 该协会选出了第一任主席。

items.example: She was made an associate of the firm.
items.exampleCN: 她被聘为该公司准合伙人。

items.example: Associative memory groups items by context.
items.exampleCN: 联想记忆按情境把条目分组。

items.meaningCN: 属于社团的；与联结有关的
items.example: Associational life revived after the war.
items.exampleCN: 战后社团生活复苏。

items.example: He disassociated himself from the report.
items.exampleCN: 他声明自己与那份报告无关。

definition_zh: 联想的；结合性的；（数学）结合的
definition_en: relating to the linking of ideas, or, of an operation, giving the same result however its parts are grouped
core_image: 三只箱子按不同次序摞在一起，无论先摞哪两只，最后堆出的形状都一样；旁边另一张纸上，一个词正牵出五六个不相干的词。
scene: 编辑把几个不相干的词写在同一页上，读者读到这里，脑中自动浮起童年厨房的气味和一段旧旋律，词与词之间没有论证，只有牵连。Associative writing trusts the links a reader's mind will make on its own.
sceneCN: 这里指以自由联想的方式牵连意象、不靠论证推进的（第 4 个义项：自由联想的、跳跃的）；句意为联想式写作信赖读者自己在心里做出的那些联结。

pos.zh: 联想的；结合性的；（数学）结合的；由社团组成的

derivatives.zh: 联想；协会；关联（由形容词回到拉丁动词所派生的动作名词，指联结本身或由联结形成的团体）
联系；交往 / 同伴 / 副的（同族动词，由「结伴」转指「把事物连起来」）
以联想的方式（加副词词尾，由形容词转指动作方式）
结合性；可结合性（加表性质的名词词尾，由形容词转指该性质本身）
解除联结（加表「分开」的前缀，由「联结」转指「拆开」）

senses.title: Working by mental links
senses.definition: describing thought or memory that proceeds by one idea calling up another
senses.definitionCN: 描述思维或记忆靠一个念头带出另一个念头而推进
senses.example: Associative thinking linked the smell of rain to a childhood street.
senses.exampleCN: 联想式思维把雨的气味连到童年的一条街。
senses.why: The adjective describes the manner of working, while the noun names the link itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词描述运作方式，名词则指那条联结本身。

senses.title: Of an operation whose grouping does not matter
senses.titleCN: 运算的分组不影响结果
senses.definition: of an operation in which the grouping of three or more elements leaves the result unchanged
senses.definitionCN: 指三个以上元素无论怎样分组，运算结果都不变的性质
senses.example: Addition is associative, so the sum is the same whichever pair is added first.
senses.exampleCN: 加法满足结合律，先加哪一对，总和都一样。
senses.why: Mathematics took the everyday idea of joining and precise it into a rule about grouping.
senses.whyCN: 数学把日常「连起来」的想法精确化为一条关于分组的规则。

senses.title: Of learning by pairing
senses.definition: describing learning in which one item becomes attached to another through repeated exposure
senses.definitionCN: 描述通过反复接触使一项与另一项建立联结的学习
senses.example: Associative learning explains why the bell alone came to calm the dog.
senses.exampleCN: 联想学习解释了为什么单靠铃声就能让狗安静下来。
senses.why: Learning by pairing is the mental link put to work: one item comes to stand for another.
senses.whyCN: 由配对进行的学习，就是把心理联结投入使用：一项开始代表另一项。

senses.title: Loose, free-flowing linkage
senses.definition: describing writing or speech that moves by resemblance and memory rather than by argument
senses.definitionCN: 描述写作或言谈靠相似与记忆推进，而非靠论证
senses.example: The essay proceeds by associative jumps rather than by steps.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章靠联想跳跃推进，而不是一步一步来。
senses.why: When links are not checked, they become a style: the adjective turns from a description of memory into a description of method.
senses.whyCN: 当联结不被检验，它就成了一种风格：这个形容词从描述记忆转为描述方法。

senses.title: Of lookup by content rather than address
senses.titleCN: 按内容而非按地址查找的
senses.definition: describing a store that returns a record by matching its content instead of by a fixed location
senses.definitionCN: 描述一种存储：按内容匹配取回记录，而不是按固定位置取回
senses.example: An associative memory returns the record that best matches the key.
senses.exampleCN: 相联存储器返回与检索键最匹配的那条记录。
senses.why: Storage addressed by content keeps the mental idea of likeness, applied to records rather than to ideas.
senses.whyCN: 按内容寻址的存储保留了「相似」这一心理想法，只是把记录代替了念头。

senses.title: Of a body based on voluntary membership
senses.definition: describing organizations or activity built on people joining freely rather than on kinship or decree
senses.definitionCN: 描述靠人们自愿加入、而非靠血缘或命令建立的组织或活动
senses.example: Associative clubs pooled their dues to rent a hall.
senses.exampleCN: 各社团把会费凑起来租下礼堂。
senses.why: Here the Latin noun's social sense returns as an adjective: what is built out of joining.
senses.whyCN: 此处拉丁名词的社会义回到形容词上：凡是由「加入」构成的东西。

senses.title: Of word links that share a context
senses.titleCN: 指共享语境的词间关系
senses.definition: describing relations between words that may replace one another in a context, as against those that combine in sequence
senses.definitionCN: 描述可在同一语境中互相替换的词之间的关系，与按顺序组合的关系相对
senses.example: Associative relations group salt with pepper rather than with sprinkle.
senses.exampleCN: 联想关系把盐与胡椒归在一起，而不是把盐与「撒」这个动作归在一起。
senses.why: Linguistics borrowed the psychological term for the links stored in the mind alongside grammar.
senses.whyCN: 语言学借用了这个心理学术语，指与语法并存、存放在心里的那些联结。

senses.title: Linked by resemblance, not by cause
senses.titleCN: 靠相似而非因果相连的
senses.definition: describing connections made because things look or feel alike rather than because one produced the other
senses.definitionCN: 描述因外观或感觉相似、而非因因果相生而形成的连接
senses.example: The film works through associative images rather than through argument.
senses.exampleCN: 这部影片靠意象的相似牵连起作用，而不是靠论证。
senses.why: When no proof joins them, resemblance alone remains, and the adjective describes that weaker link.
senses.whyCN: 当没有证明把两者连起，只剩相似，这个形容词便描述那种更弱的联结。

intro.en: Associative is associate plus the Latin adjective suffix -ivus 'tending to'. Associate comes from Latin associare 'to unite with'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: associative 是 associate 加拉丁形容词词尾（意为「倾向于……」）构成；associate 出自拉丁 associare「与……联合」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Socius meant 'companion, ally'. Its deeper origin is not established; the link sometimes proposed to a verb of following is a hypothesis.
items.cn: socius 意为「同伴、盟友」。其更深来源未得到证明；有人提出它与一个表「跟随」的动词有关，那只是假说。

items.en: Ad- 'to' plus sociare 'to join' produced associare 'to unite with', the verb behind the whole English family.
items.cn: 表「朝向」的前缀加 sociare「结伴」构成 associare「与……联合」，是整个英语词族背后的动词。

items.en: The suffix -ivus formed adjectives meaning 'tending to, serving to', and it reached English through French as -ive.
items.cn: 拉丁词尾 -ivus 构成意为「倾向于、用于」的形容词，经法语进入英语。

items.en: Associative is recorded in English from the seventeenth century in the philosophy of ideas; the mathematical rule of grouping is named in the nineteenth century, and the psychological and computing uses follow in the twentieth.
items.cn: associative 在十七世纪已见于英语的观念哲学；指分组规则的数学用法在十九世纪得名，心理学与计算技术的用法随后于二十世纪出现。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper origin): no exact first citation is fixed for the adjective, and the pre-Latin source of socius remains a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：这个形容词没有确切的最早书证；socius 在拉丁语之前的来源仍属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds forms of the same Latin verb; group two holds adjectives that also describe how things are linked.
note.cn: 第一组是同一个拉丁动词的各词形；第二组是同样描述「如何相连」的形容词。

entries.definition: Names the link or the body of members; the adjective names the property of working by such links.
entries.definitionCN: 指那条联结或成员团体；形容词则指「以这种联结运作」的性质。

entries.definition: The verb for linking and the noun for a partner; it never carries the mathematical sense of grouping.
entries.definitionCN: 指联结的动词与同伴的名词；它从未带上数学分组义。

entries.definition: The adverb for doing something by association, as in thinking associatively; the adjective modifies the thing, not the act.
entries.definitionCN: 指以联想方式做某事的副词，如「以联想方式思考」；形容词修饰事物，而非动作。

entries.definition: Describes separation rather than joining, as in a dissociative disorder; it is built with a prefix of apartness.
entries.definitionCN: 描述分离而非联结，如解离性障碍；它由表「分开」的前缀构成。

entries.definition: The everyday adjective for anything joined, by wire, by road or by logic; it does not say how the joining is made.
entries.definitionCN: 指被连起来的任何东西，靠电线、道路或逻辑；不说明联结如何形成。

entries.definition: Describing what concerns relations between things, often in databases or grammar; it is broader and more technical than associative.
entries.definitionCN: 描述涉及事物之间关系者，常见于数据库或语法；比 associative 更宽泛也更技术化。

entries.definition: Describing two things that regularly occur together by rule, as in correlative conjunctions; the pairing is grammatical, not mental.
entries.definitionCN: 描述按规则经常同时出现的两项，如关联连词；这种配对是语法性的，而非心理性的。

entries.definition: Describing a device deliberately built to fix something in memory; it may use associations, but its purpose is recall.
entries.definitionCN: 描述为把某物钉在记忆中而特意造出的手段；它可以用联想，但目的是记住。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The Latin suffix -ivus means 'tending to': associative is 'tending to link'.
normal.cn: 拉丁词尾意为「倾向于」：associative 就是「倾向于联结的」。

normal.en: The family runs associate, association, associatively and associativity, all from one verb of joining.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 associate、association、associatively、associativity，全出同一个表「联合」的动词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the fields: associative learning in psychology, associative memory in computing, the associative property in algebra.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各领域：心理学的联想学习、计算技术的相联存储、代数的结合律。

normal.en: The mathematical sense is a rule about brackets: change the grouping, keep the answer.
normal.cn: 数学义是一条关于括号的规则：改分组，不改答案。

normal.en: The noun keeps the social sense, so association can still mean a club, while the adjective rarely does.
normal.cn: 名词保留社会义，因此 association 仍可指社团，而形容词很少这样用。

abstract.en: Picture three boxes stacked in any order that still makes one tower.
abstract.cn: 想象三只箱子无论先摞哪两只，堆出来仍是同一座塔。

abstract.en: Picture a page where one word pulls five unrelated words out of the air.
abstract.cn: 想象一页纸上，一个词把五个不相干的词从空气里拽出来。

abstract.en: Picture a library shelf that finds a book by what it is about, not by where it sits.
abstract.cn: 想象一排书架，靠书的内容而不是靠位置找到它。

examples.en: Associative memory in the model is addressed by content rather than by location.
examples.cn: 该模型中的联想记忆按内容而非按位置寻址。

examples.en: String concatenation is associative, but subtraction is not.
examples.cn: 字符串拼接满足结合律，而减法不满足。

examples.en: Her associative style of lecturing leaves the connections for the listener to finish.
examples.cn: 她联想式的讲授把联结留给听者自己去补完。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「朝向」+「结伴」+「倾向于」——倾向于把东西结在一起：心里结是联想，括号里结是结合律。

root: 拉丁 associare「与……联合」加拉丁形容词词尾（意为「倾向于」）；associare = 表「朝向」的前缀 + sociare「结伴」，sociare 出自 socius「同伴」；socius 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe a way of linking: ideas calling ideas, brackets that change nothing, pairs learned by exposure, jumps that skip argument, records found by content, bodies built from voluntary joining, words sharing a context, and images joined by resemblance.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在描述一种「连起来」的方式：念头带出念头、括号改了结果不变、反复接触学成的配对、跳过论证的跳跃、按内容取回记录、由自愿加入组成的团体、共享语境的词、靠相似相连的意象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: three boxes stacked in any order into the same tower, beside a page where one word pulls five others out of the air.
core.cn: 核心意象：三只箱子无论先摞哪两只都堆成同一座塔，旁边一页纸上一个词把五个词从空气里拽出来。

branches.en: THE LOOSE CHAIN: a mind that links freely, and a style that lets the links stand unchecked.
branches.cn: 松散的链：自由联结的心，以及任由联结不经检验的风格。

branches.en: THE LEARNED PAIR: repeated exposure welds one item to another.
branches.cn: 学成的配对：反复接触把一项焊在另一项上。

branches.en: THE RULE OF BRACKETS: regrouping changes nothing, which is joining made exact.
branches.cn: 括号的规则：改了分组也不改结果，这是被精确化的「连起来」。

branches.en: TWO KINDS OF STORE: records found by content, and people joined by choice.
branches.cn: 两种「库」：按内容取回的记录，与凭自愿加入的人。

branches.en: JOINED BY CONTEXT OR LIKENESS: words that share a setting, and images that resemble each other.
branches.cn: 靠语境或相似相连：共享场景的词，以及彼此相似的意象。

intro.en: The adjective is one root, two prefixes and one suffix: a Latin noun of companionship, a prefix of direction, and a suffix of tendency.
intro.cn: 这个形容词是一个词根、两个前缀与一个后缀的组合：拉丁的「同伴」名词、表方向的前缀、表倾向的后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin socius gives social, society and sociable; sociare with ad- gives associate and association; -ivus gives the tending-to adjectives of English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 socius 衍生 social、society、sociable；sociare 加表方向的前缀衍生 associate 与 association；拉丁词尾 -ivus 构成英语中表「倾向于」的形容词。

items.example: Socius is the person one joins.
items.exampleCN: socius 是与自己结伴的人。

items.example: The verb described two towns sharing one market.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词描述两座城镇共用一个市集。

items.example: Associare joined one party to another.
items.exampleCN: associare 把一方与另一方连起。

items.example: They associate the tune with summer.
items.exampleCN: 他们把那支曲子与夏天联系起来。

items.example: Associative habits build quickly.
items.exampleCN: 联结性的习惯形成得很快。

items.example: She thinks associatively under time pressure.
items.exampleCN: 她在时间压力下以联想方式思考。

items.example: Associativity fails for subtraction.
items.exampleCN: 减法不满足结合性。

items.example: Dissociative symptoms followed the shock.
items.exampleCN: 休克之后出现了解离症状。

definition_zh: 学习者；初学者；学车的人
definition_en: a person who is learning a subject, a skill or a trade
core_image: 清晨的驾驶练习场上，一辆车顶立着醒目的标记牌，方向盘后的人手心出汗，副驾的教练把同一句话说了第三遍。
scene: 清晨的练车场上，车顶立着醒目的标记牌，方向盘后的人手心出汗，副驾的教练把同一句话又说了一遍。The learner stalled again at the same junction and laughed at herself.
sceneCN: 这里指正在学开车、尚未取得正式驾照的人（第 3 个义项：学车者）；句意为这位学车者在同一个路口又熄了火，自己也笑了。

pos.zh: 学习者；初学者；学车者（可数）

collocations.zh: 以学习者为中心的教学

derivatives.zh: 学习；得知（古英语 leornian「获得知识」，由「获得知识」转指「学习」这一动作）
学习；学问（在动词后加表动作或结果的名词词尾，由动作转指过程与所得）
有学问的；博学的（加表「已具备」的分词词尾，由「学到」转指「学有所成」；注意与表「被学到」的读音不同）
忘掉（旧习惯、旧知识）（加表「相反」的前缀，由「学得」转指「把学到的去掉」）
可学会的（加表「能够」的形容词词尾，由「学习」转指「可被学会」）

senses.title: A person who is learning
senses.definition: anyone in the act of acquiring knowledge or a skill
senses.definitionCN: 任何正在获取知识或技能的人
senses.example: Every learner in the room had already read the first chapter.
senses.exampleCN: 教室里每个学习者都已经读过第一章。
senses.why: The bare role: whoever is in the act, whatever the subject and whatever the age.
senses.whyCN: 最素朴的角色义：不论学科、不论年龄，谁在学就是谁。

senses.title: A beginner, often a fast one
senses.titleCN: 初学者，常指学得快的人
senses.definition: a person new to a subject, especially when judged by how quickly they pick it up
senses.definitionCN: 刚接触某学科的人，尤指就其上手快慢而言
senses.example: She is a quick learner and finished the induction in a week.
senses.exampleCN: 她学得很快，一周就完成了入职培训。
senses.why: The word can name not only the role but the speed of the person in it, which is why quick learner is such a common phrase.
senses.whyCN: 这个词不仅能指角色，也能指处于该角色者的速度，所以「学得快的人」成了极常见的说法。

senses.title: A learner driver
senses.definition: a person learning to drive who has not yet passed the test
senses.definitionCN: 尚未通过考试、正在学开车的人
senses.example: The learner braked too late at the junction.
senses.exampleCN: 这位学车者在路口刹车太晚。
senses.why: British usage makes the word a formal status marked by a plate on the car.
senses.whyCN: 英式用法把这个词变成一个正式身份，以车上的牌子标出。

senses.title: A language learner
senses.definition: a person studying a second or foreign language
senses.definitionCN: 正在学习第二语言或外语的人
senses.example: The course pairs each learner with a native speaker.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课为每位语言学习者配一位母语者。
senses.why: Language teaching made the word a category: learner language, learner errors, learner autonomy.
senses.whyCN: 语言教学把这个词变成一个类别：学习者语言、学习者错误、学习者自主。

senses.title: The centre of teaching
senses.definition: the person whose needs teaching is organized around, in contrast to the teacher
senses.definitionCN: 教学据其需要来安排的一方，与教师相对
senses.example: The syllabus was rewritten to be learner-centred.
senses.exampleCN: 教学大纲被改写为以学习者为中心。
senses.why: Here the word names a position in a relationship rather than an individual.
senses.whyCN: 此处这个词命名的是关系中的一方，而不是某个个人。

senses.title: An organism that acquires responses
senses.definition: in psychology, the animal or person whose behaviour is being shaped in an experiment
senses.definitionCN: 心理学中指行为正在实验中受到塑造的动物或人
senses.example: The learner in the maze was a rat, not a student.
senses.exampleCN: 迷宫里的学习者是一只老鼠，而不是学生。
senses.why: Psychology needs a word for the party whose behaviour changes, and the everyday word is borrowed unchanged.
senses.whyCN: 心理学需要一个指「行为被改变的一方」的词，于是把这个日常词原样借去。

senses.title: A machine that improves with data
senses.definition: in computing, a model or algorithm that adjusts its parameters from examples
senses.definitionCN: 计算领域指从样例中调整参数的模型或算法
senses.example: The learner reached ninety per cent accuracy after ten thousand examples.
senses.exampleCN: 这个学习器在看过一万个样例后达到九成准确率。
senses.why: The machine is said to learn because its parameters change with examples, so the human word is extended to it.
senses.whyCN: 机器被称为学习，是因为参数随样例改变，人的词便延伸到它身上。

senses.title: An apprentice under a master
senses.definition: a person bound to a master to learn a trade by working in it
senses.definitionCN: 为学手艺而跟随师傅、在实际劳作中学习的人
senses.example: The learner spent two years in the workshop before touching the lathe.
senses.exampleCN: 这名学徒在作坊里待了两年才被允许碰车床。
senses.why: The oldest layer of the word: learning a trade by living inside it, which no classroom reproduces.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的一层：靠着身在行当里学手艺，任何课堂都无法复制。

intro.en: Learner is the Old English verb leornian 'to get knowledge' plus the agent suffix -ere. There is no Latin element in the word. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: learner 由古英语动词 leornian「获得知识」加表施事者的古英语后缀构成，词中不含拉丁成分。年代均为约数。

items.en: Leornian meant 'to learn, to get knowledge, to be taught'. Its deeper origin is not established; the usual reconstruction is a Germanic verb meaning 'to learn', and that form is a reconstruction.
items.cn: leornian 意为「学习、获得知识、受教」。其更深来源未得到证明；通常重构为一个日耳曼语中意为「学习」的动词，那只是重构形式。

items.en: The agent suffix -ere formed nouns for people who do a thing, as in baker and writer; it is Germanic, and its resemblance to the Latin agent suffix is a common inheritance rather than a borrowing.
items.cn: 表施事者的后缀构成指「做某事之人」的名词，如烤面包者与写作者；它属日耳曼语，与拉丁同类后缀的相似来自共同渊源，而非借用。

items.en: Learner is recorded in Middle English as 'one who learns', a plain agent noun with no special status attached.
items.cn: learner 在中古英语中即已记录，意为「学习的人」，是一个普通的施事名词，并未附带特殊身份。

items.en: From the nineteenth century the word was attached to particular roles, and in the twentieth it became a technical term in education, in psychology and in computing.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，这个词被系在特定角色上；到二十世纪，它成为教育学、心理学与计算技术中的术语。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Germanic source of leornian is not established, and the reconstructed Germanic verb is a reconstruction, not a recorded form.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：leornian 在日耳曼语之前的来源未得到证明，所重构的日耳曼语动词属重构形式，并非有记录的形式。

note.en: Group one holds forms of the same Old English verb; group two holds words for people who are in some stage of study.
note.cn: 第一组是同一个古英语动词的各词形；第二组是指处于某一学习阶段之人的词。

entries.definition: The verb for getting knowledge or skill; the noun adds the person who is in the middle of doing it.
entries.definitionCN: 指获得知识或技能的动词；名词则加上「正在做这件事的人」。

entries.definition: An adjective for someone who has acquired much knowledge, or for what has been acquired; it marks the end state, not the ongoing role.
entries.definitionCN: 形容已获得大量知识的人或已习得之物；标出的是终点状态，而非进行中的角色。

entries.definition: Names the process or the body of knowledge, as in machine learning or a learning curve.
entries.definitionCN: 指过程或知识总体，如机器学习、学习曲线。

entries.definition: To drop a habit or a belief one already holds; it is learning run backwards.
entries.definitionCN: 指丢掉已持有的习惯或看法；是倒着走的「学」。

entries.definition: A person registered in a school or university; the status is institutional, whereas learner describes the act.
entries.definitionCN: 指在学校或大学注册的人；其身份是制度性的，而 learner 描述的是行为。

entries.definition: A child at school, or someone taught by a particular teacher; it is narrower in age and setting.
entries.definitionCN: 指在校儿童，或由某位老师教授的人；在年龄与场合上更窄。

entries.definition: A person legally bound to a master for a term to learn a trade; it is the formal version of one sense of learner.
entries.definitionCN: 指按契约在期限内随师傅学手艺的人；是 learner 某一义项的正式说法。

entries.definition: A person being trained for a particular post, usually inside an organization; the focus is the job, not the knowledge.
entries.definitionCN: 指为某一岗位受训的人，通常在企业内部；重心是岗位，而非知识。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: A verb of getting knowledge plus the old suffix for the person doing it: the one who learns.
normal.cn: 一个表「获得知识」的动词加古英语中表施事者的后缀：正在学的那个人。

normal.en: The family runs learn, learning, learned and unlearn; learned splits off as an adjective for the finished state.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 learn、learning、learned、unlearn；learned 分出作形容词，指已完成的状态。

normal.en: Fixed phrases place the word in a setting: a quick learner, a language learner, learner-centred teaching.
normal.cn: 固定搭配把词放进具体场合：学得快的人、语言学习者、以学习者为中心的教学。

normal.en: British road signs make one sense official: the learner plate marks a driver who has not passed.
normal.cn: 英国路牌把其中一个义项制度化了：学车牌标出尚未通过考试的驾驶者。

normal.en: The word carries no Latin element, so every attempt to read it as a Latin derivative is a false friend.
normal.cn: 这个词不含拉丁成分，凡把它读作拉丁派生词的做法都是误认。

abstract.en: Picture a hand holding a pencil the wrong way until the fingers find their own grip.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手起初把笔握错，后来指头自己找到了握法。

abstract.en: Picture a car with a bright plate on the roof, announcing that mistakes are allowed.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆车顶立着亮牌子的车，宣告犯错是被允许的。

abstract.en: Picture a rat in a maze learning a route it will never describe.
abstract.cn: 想象迷宫里的老鼠学会一条它永远说不出的路线。

examples.en: The learner repeated the phrase until the stress fell in the right place.
examples.cn: 这位学习者反复念那句话，直到重音落在正确的位置。

examples.en: A learner driver must be accompanied by a qualified driver.
examples.cn: 学车者必须由持证驾驶者陪同。

examples.en: The software adapts to each learner's pace.
examples.cn: 这款软件会适应每位学习者的进度。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「学」+ 表施事者的古英语后缀——正在学的那个人；学车者、语言学习者、学习器都是它的分身。

root: 古英语 leornian「获得知识、受教」加古英语表施事者的后缀；leornian 更深来源未得到证明，通常重构为一个日耳曼语动词，属重构形式。词中无拉丁成分。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one role: the person in the middle of acquiring something. The role is then fixed to a beginner's speed, to a driver without a licence, to a language student, to the centre of a method, to an animal in a maze, to a model fed with examples, and back to the oldest setting, the apprentice in a workshop.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个角色展开：正处于「习得某事」之中的人。这个角色再依次系到初学者的快慢、无证的学车者、语言学生、某种教学法的中心、迷宫里的动物、被样例喂养的模型，最后回到最古老的场景：作坊里的学徒。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand learning a grip, a car marked as not yet passed, and a rat that will never describe its route.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只正在学会握法的手、一辆标明尚未通过考试的车、一只永远说不出路线的老鼠。

branches.en: THE ROLE AND THE POSITION: a person learning, and the same person as the pole a syllabus is built around.
branches.cn: 角色与位置：正在学习的人，以及被当作大纲轴心的同一个。

branches.en: TWO BEGINNINGS: the newcomer judged by speed, and the apprentice bound to a master.
branches.cn: 两种开头：以快慢衡量的新手，与随师傅受契约约束的学徒。

branches.en: THE MARKED CAR: a legal status, visible from outside.
branches.cn: 带标记的车：一种从外面看得见的法定身份。

branches.en: THE SECOND TONGUE: the word becomes a category in language teaching.
branches.cn: 第二门语言：这个词在语言教学中成为一个类别。

branches.en: TWO NON-HUMAN LEARNERS: the animal in the maze and the model fed with examples.
branches.cn: 两种非人的学习者：迷宫里的动物，与用样例喂养的模型。

intro.en: Learner is Germanic through and through: one Old English verb plus one Old English agent suffix, with no Latin layer to read.
intro.cn: learner 通体属日耳曼语：一个古英语动词加一个古英语施事后缀，没有拉丁层可读。

latinIntro.en: This word has no Latin element, so the Latin list is left empty; the older strata are Germanic only.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词不含拉丁成分，因此拉丁条目留空；更早的层次纯属日耳曼语。

items.structure: leornian (Old English verb, weak class two)
items.example: Leornian named the act before anyone named the actor.
items.exampleCN: leornian 先命名动作，后才有指人的词。

items.example: The suffix turned verbs of doing into names of doers.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把表动作的动词变成指施事者的名词。

items.example: Children learn the alphabet by song.
items.exampleCN: 孩子们靠歌曲学字母。

items.example: The learner asked for a slower tape.
items.exampleCN: 这位学习者要了一盘更慢的录音。

items.meaning: the process or the knowledge gained
items.example: Learning continues after school.
items.exampleCN: 学习在学校之后继续。

items.example: A learned judge cited an old case.
items.exampleCN: 一位博学的法官引了旧判例。

items.example: He had to unlearn his first method.
items.exampleCN: 他不得不丢掉最初学到的方法。

items.example: The skill is learnable in a term.
items.exampleCN: 这项技能一学期可学会。

definition_en: to learn something so exactly that it can be produced from memory without the text
core_image: 书桌上一本翻旧的书被合上，书页里夹着的纸条写着开头两个字；背诵的人在屋里踱步，眼睛不看任何东西。
scene: 夜里，学生把书合上放到桌角，只留一张写着开头两个字的纸条，然后在屋里来回踱步，让整段文字从记忆里一句句浮出来。She had memorized the whole speech and could start from any line.
sceneCN: 这里指把整段文字逐字记住、离开书本也能复现（第 2 个义项：逐字背熟）；句意为她已把整篇演讲背熟，从任何一句都能接下去。

derivatives.zh: 记忆；记忆力（拉丁 memoria「记忆」，由「记忆」转指「记忆能力」与「被记住之事」）
值得记住的；难忘的（加拉丁形容词词尾，由「记忆」转指「值得被记住」）
记住；背诵（在动词后加拉丁动作名词词尾，由动作转指该过程）
备忘录（拉丁 memorandum「应被记住之事」，由「须记住」转指「备忘的字条」）
纪念（加表「共同」的前缀，由「记住」转指「众人共同记住」）

senses.title: Commit facts to memory by study
senses.titleCN: 靠反复研习把事实记牢
senses.definition: to fix facts in the mind through repeated study until they can be recalled
senses.definitionCN: 通过反复研习把事实固定在脑中，直到能回想起来
senses.example: She memorized the names of every bone before the practical exam.
senses.exampleCN: 在实操考试前，她记住了每一块骨头的名称。
senses.why: The general sense: information is put in, but nothing is said about how exactly it must come out.
senses.whyCN: 泛指的义项：信息被装进去，但不说出来时必须多精确。

senses.title: Learn a text word for word
senses.definition: to learn a passage so exactly that every word can be reproduced
senses.definitionCN: 把一段文字学到能一字不差复现的程度
senses.example: He memorized the opening paragraph of the treaty.
senses.exampleCN: 他背熟了条约的第一段。
senses.why: The adverb test is simple: if a paraphrase would fail, the word is this sense rather than the general one.
senses.whyCN: 检验很简单：若换个说法就不合格，那就是这个义项，而不是泛指的「记住」。

senses.title: Fix a route or a sequence in mind
senses.titleCN: 把路线或次序记在脑中
senses.definition: to learn the order of places or steps well enough to follow them without a guide
senses.definitionCN: 把地点或步骤的次序学到无须引导也能照做的程度
senses.example: The driver memorized the route before the signposts were removed.
senses.exampleCN: 在路牌被撤走之前，司机先记住了路线。
senses.why: A route is a sequence, and a sequence is remembered by order rather than by words.
senses.whyCN: 路线是一个次序，而次序靠顺序记住，不靠字句。

senses.title: Store data in a device
senses.definition: in computing, to write information into a store so that it can be read later
senses.definitionCN: 计算领域指把信息写入存储器，以便之后读取
senses.example: The program memorizes the result so the next call is quick.
senses.exampleCN: 程序把结果存起来，下一次调用就很快。
senses.why: A device stores what it is given, so the human verb is applied to writing into memory.
senses.whyCN: 设备把给它的东西存起来，于是人的动词被用于「写入记忆」。

senses.title: Drill by rote
senses.titleCN: 以重复操练的方式硬记
senses.definition: to learn by repetition in a drill, often without understanding the material
senses.definitionCN: 在操练中靠重复学习，常常并不理解材料
senses.example: The class memorized the conjugation tables twice a week.
senses.exampleCN: 这个班每周两次把变位表背两遍。
senses.why: The word itself is neutral, but in schooling it often carries the criticism of rote work.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本身中性，但在学校语境里常带「死记」的批评色彩。

senses.title: Play or speak from memory
senses.definition: to learn a piece or a speech so well that it can be performed without the score or notes
senses.definitionCN: 把乐曲或讲稿学到无须看谱或看稿也能表演的程度
senses.example: The pianist had memorized the sonata before the tour began.
senses.exampleCN: 巡演开始前，这位钢琴家已把奏鸣曲背了下来。
senses.why: Performance without the score is the proof that the text is held exactly, which separates this sense from general study.
senses.whyCN: 无谱演奏是「文字被精确持有」的证明，这一义项由此与泛泛的学习分开。

senses.title: Cram for an examination
senses.definition: to put material into memory for a short period, often to be forgotten soon after
senses.definitionCN: 把材料短时间塞进记忆，常常很快又忘掉
senses.example: They memorized a hundred dates the night before and forgot half by noon.
senses.exampleCN: 他们考前一晚记了一百个年代，到中午就忘了一半。
senses.why: The purpose is the examination rather than durable knowledge, so the act is narrowed by its deadline.
senses.whyCN: 目的是考试而非长久知识，这个动作便被截止日期收窄。

senses.title: Register a face or a name on purpose
senses.titleCN: 刻意把面孔或姓名记住
senses.definition: to make a deliberate effort to keep a face, a name or a detail available for later use
senses.definitionCN: 刻意努力把面孔、姓名或细节留在脑中，以备后用
senses.example: The officer memorized the visitor's face at the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 警官在门口把来访者的面孔记了下来。
senses.why: Here the act is deliberate attention rather than rehearsal, which shows how wide the verb's range is.
senses.whyCN: 这里的动作是有意的注意而非复述，可见这个动词的范围有多宽。

intro.en: Memorize is Latin memoria 'memory' plus the verb suffix -ize, which came to English through French from Latin -izare and Greek -izein. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: memorize 是拉丁 memoria「记忆」加动词后缀构成；这个后缀经法语、拉丁 -izare，上溯希腊 -izein 进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Memor meant 'mindful, remembering'. Its deeper origin is not established; the connection often cited to a root meaning 'to remember' is a reconstruction, not a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: memor 意为「留心的、记得的」。其更深来源未得到证明；常被引用的一个意为「记住」的词根联系属于重构形式，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Memoria named memory both as the faculty and as the thing remembered, a double sense English keeps in memory.
items.cn: memoria 既指记忆能力，也指被记住之事，英语 memory 保留了这双重含义。

items.en: The verb suffix reached English through Latin -izare and French -iser, from Greek -izein, which formed verbs of making or doing.
items.cn: 这个动词后缀经拉丁 -izare 与法语 -iser，上溯希腊 -izein 进入英语；后者构成表「使成为」或「做」的动词。

items.en: Memorize is recorded in the sixteenth century first in the sense of putting something into writing, and the sense 'learn by heart' is recorded from the nineteenth century.
items.cn: memorize 在十六世纪已有记录，最初指「把某事写下来」；「背诵记住」这一义项自十九世纪起才有记录。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper origin): the exact first citation is not fixed, and any pre-Latin form offered for memor is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：确切的最早书证无法确定；凡为 memor 给出的拉丁语之前的形式都是重构。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Latin noun of memory; group two holds verbs that also put something into the mind but differ in method or purpose.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁「记忆」名词的词；第二组是同样把东西放进头脑、但方法或目的不同的动词。

entries.definition: The faculty of remembering or the store of what is remembered; it names the capacity, while the verb names the act of filling it.
entries.definitionCN: 指记忆能力或被记住之事的总体；它指能力，而动词指填充这一能力的动作。

entries.definition: Describes what deserves to be remembered; it says nothing about anyone's effort.
entries.definitionCN: 形容值得被记住者；不涉及任何人的努力。

entries.definition: To honour a person or event by a public act of remembrance; the prefix adds the sense of many people remembering at once.
entries.definitionCN: 指以公开的纪念行为致敬某人或某事；前缀增添了「众人同时记住」的意思。

entries.definition: A written note for later use, literally 'a thing to be remembered'; it is a document, not an act of learning.
entries.definitionCN: 指留待后用的字条，字面是「应被记住之事」；它是文件，而非学习动作。

entries.definition: The general verb for gaining knowledge or skill, including understanding; memorize is the narrower act of fixing the exact form.
entries.definitionCN: 指获得知识或技能的泛用动词，含理解；memorize 则是把确切形式固定下来的较窄动作。

entries.definition: To continue to hold information or heat without losing it; it describes keeping, not the first effort of putting in.
entries.definitionCN: 指持续保有信息或热量而不丢失；描述的是保持，而非最初装入的努力。

entries.definition: To force facts into memory in a short burst before an examination, usually with little understanding; it is memorizing at its most temporary.
entries.definitionCN: 指考前短时间强行塞入事实，通常理解很少；是 memorize 最临时的一种。

entries.definition: To say a memorized text aloud before an audience or a teacher; it is the performance that follows the memorizing.
entries.definitionCN: 指在听众或老师面前把背熟的文字说出来；是记住之后的表演。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin memoria 'memory' plus the verb suffix of making: to make something into memory.
normal.cn: 拉丁 memoria「记忆」加表「使成为」的动词后缀：把某物做成记忆。

normal.en: The family runs memory, memorable, memorandum, commemorate and memorization, all from one noun of remembering.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 memory、memorable、memorandum、commemorate、memorization，全出同一个表「记住」的名词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the objects: memorize a poem, memorize lines, memorize a route, memorize for an exam.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出对象：背诗、背台词、记路线、为考试强记。

normal.en: The sixteenth-century sense was to put in writing, which is why a memorandum is literally a thing to be remembered.
normal.cn: 十六世纪的义项是「写下来」，所以备忘录字面上就是「应被记住之事」。

normal.en: The word names the putting in, not the holding: retaining is what happens after memorizing.
normal.cn: 这个词指「装进去」，不指「保持」；记住之后才是保有。

abstract.en: Picture a book closed on the table with only two words left on a slip of paper.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上合起的书，只剩一张写着两个词的纸条。

abstract.en: Picture a room walked in circles until the floor knows the route.
abstract.cn: 想象在一间屋里绕圈，绕到地板都认得这条路线。

abstract.en: Picture a drawer labelled in a script only the owner can read.
abstract.cn: 想象一只抽屉，标签上的字只有主人认得。

examples.en: He memorized the list of irregular verbs in a single evening.
examples.cn: 他用一个晚上背下了不规则动词表。

examples.en: The actor had memorized every line before the first rehearsal.
examples.cn: 演员在第一次排练之前就把每句台词记熟了。

examples.en: Do not memorize the formula; derive it once and it stays.
examples.cn: 别死记公式；自己推一遍，它才留得住。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「记忆」+「使成为」——把材料做成记忆：逐字背、记路线、存进机器，都是同一个动作的不同落点。

root: 拉丁 memoria「记忆」加动词后缀（经拉丁 -izare、法语 -iser，上溯希腊 -izein，表「使成为」）；memoria 出自 memor「留心的、记得的」，memor 更深来源不确定，常引的词根联系属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one act: putting something into memory on purpose. The act is then fixed to facts, to an exact text, to a route, to a device's store, to drill, to a performance without the score, to a night of cramming, and to the deliberate registering of a face.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：有意把某物装进记忆。这个动作再依次落到事实、逐字的文本、一条路线、设备的存储、课堂操练、无谱的演奏、考前的突击，以及刻意记住一张面孔。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a book closed on the table, a slip with two words on it, and a body walking the room until the text comes out by itself.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上合起的书、写着两个词的纸条，以及一个在屋里踱步直到文字自己浮出的人。

branches.en: FACTS AND DRILL: the general act of fixing facts, and the schoolroom form that repeats them.
branches.cn: 事实与操练：把事实固定的泛称，与教室里反复重复的那种做法。

branches.en: THE EXACT FORM: a text word for word, then a piece performed without the score.
branches.cn: 确切的形式：逐字的一段文字，再到无谱演奏的一支曲子。

branches.en: HELD FOR LATER USE: a route kept in mind, and a face registered on purpose.
branches.cn: 留待后用：记住的一条路线，与刻意记下的一张面孔。

branches.en: THE DEVICE'S STORE: the same verb applied to writing into a machine's memory.
branches.cn: 设备的存储：同一个动词用在把数据写进机器记忆。

branches.en: THE NIGHT BEFORE: memory filled for one day and lost by noon.
branches.cn: 考前一晚：为一天而填满，到中午已漏掉一半。

intro.en: Memorize joins a Latin noun of memory to a Greek verb suffix that reached English through Latin and French, so both halves are readable.
intro.cn: memorize 把拉丁的「记忆」名词与一个经拉丁、法语进入英语的希腊动词后缀接在一起，两半都可读。

latinIntro.en: Latin memor and memoria give memory, memorable, memorandum and commemorate; the -ize suffix gives organize, realize and modernize.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 memor 与 memoria 衍生 memory、memorable、memorandum、commemorate；表「使成为」的后缀衍生 organize、realize、modernize。

items.example: Memor described the person who keeps something in mind.
items.exampleCN: memor 形容把某事留在心里的人。

items.example: Memoria covered both the faculty and the remembered thing.
items.exampleCN: memoria 兼指记忆能力与被记住之事。

items.example: They memorize the names in pairs.
items.exampleCN: 他们成对地记这些名字。

items.meaning: the act of committing to memory
items.example: Memorization without use fades quickly.
items.exampleCN: 不加运用的背诵很快消退。

items.example: Her memory for faces is unusually good.
items.exampleCN: 她对面孔的记忆力特别好。

items.example: It was a memorable afternoon.
items.exampleCN: 那是一个难忘的下午。

items.example: The office issued a short memorandum.
items.exampleCN: 办公室发出了一份简短备忘录。

items.example: The town commemorates the flood every spring.
items.exampleCN: 这座镇每年春天纪念那场洪水。

latinEntries.structure: memorandum (gerundive, 'that which is to be remembered')

definition_zh: 回想；召回；撤回（缺陷产品）；罢免
definition_en: to bring something back to mind, or to call a person or thing back
core_image: 一只旧箱子的盖子被掀开，里面的信件按年份叠着；同一只手在另一张桌上把已经发出的通知一张张收回。
scene: 老屋阁楼上，她掀开箱盖，按年份叠着的信件让整个夏天忽然回到眼前，连纸页的干味都清晰起来。She could recall the smell of that attic whenever it rained.
sceneCN: 这里指把过去的经验重新带回意识（第 1 个义项：回想）；句意为每逢下雨，她都能回想起那座阁楼的气味。

pos.zh: 记忆力；召回令；罢免（可数或不可数）

derivatives.zh: 可召回的；可想起的（在动词后加表「能够」的形容词词尾，由动作转指「可被唤回」）
未被想起的；未被召回的（加表否定的前缀，由「被唤回」转指「未被唤回」）
回忆；记忆（同义近邻，出自拉丁「聚集」一路，与本词不同源，见形近组）

senses.title: Bring something back to mind
senses.definition: to bring a past experience or a fact back into conscious thought
senses.definitionCN: 把过去的经验或事实重新带入意识
senses.example: She could recall the smell of that attic whenever it rained.
senses.exampleCN: 每逢下雨，她都能回想起那座阁楼的气味。
senses.why: The prefix of return plus a verb of calling gives the core: something is called back to where it was.
senses.whyCN: 表「返回」的前缀加表「喊」的动词给出核心：把某物叫回它原来的地方。

senses.title: Recover an item from memory
senses.definition: in psychology, to retrieve a stored item in order to report it
senses.definitionCN: 心理学指把存着的条目提取出来以便报告
senses.example: In the test, subjects recalled six of the ten words.
senses.exampleCN: 在测试中，受试者回想起十个词里的六个。
senses.why: Laboratory use measures the retrieval rather than the feeling, so the word becomes a technical term with a score.
senses.whyCN: 实验室用法测量的是提取本身而非感受，于是这个词成了带分数的术语。

senses.title: Summon a person back
senses.definition: to order a person, especially an official, to return from a post
senses.definitionCN: 命令某人，尤指官员，从任所返回
senses.example: The ministry recalled its ambassador for consultations.
senses.exampleCN: 该部召回大使回国磋商。
senses.why: The oldest sense is literal: a person is ordered back, with no memory involved.
senses.whyCN: 最老的义项是字面的：人被命令回来，与记忆无关。

senses.title: Take a defective product back
senses.definition: to ask buyers to return a batch of goods because of a fault
senses.definitionCN: 因存在缺陷而要求购买者退回一批货物
senses.example: The company recalled two thousand bottles of the syrup.
senses.exampleCN: 该公司召回了两千瓶糖浆。
senses.why: The manufacturing sense is recent: the maker calls the goods back, exactly as a voice would call a person.
senses.whyCN: 制造义出现得晚：制造者把货物叫回去，正像一声呼喊把一个人叫回来。

senses.title: Remove an official by vote
senses.definition: to remove an elected official before the end of the term by a direct vote
senses.definitionCN: 在任期结束前以直接投票解除民选官员的职务
senses.example: Voters recalled the mayor after the audit was published.
senses.exampleCN: 审计报告公布后，选民罢免了市长。
senses.why: A vote is the voice of the electorate calling an official back out of office.
senses.whyCN: 投票是选民的声音，把官员从职位上叫回来。

senses.title: Call a player back to the squad
senses.definition: to bring a player back into a team after a period away
senses.definitionCN: 把离队一段时间的球员重新召入队中
senses.example: The club recalled the winger from his loan spell.
senses.exampleCN: 俱乐部把这位边锋从租借期召回。
senses.why: A club calls a player back from loan, the same summoning applied to a contract.
senses.whyCN: 俱乐部把球员从租借中叫回，是同一种召唤用在合同上。

senses.title: Ask a system for stored data
senses.definition: in computing, to fetch a stored record or to resume a suspended task
senses.definitionCN: 计算领域指取回已存的记录，或恢复被挂起的任务
senses.example: The interface recalls the last search when the window reopens.
senses.exampleCN: 窗口重新打开时，界面会取回上一次的检索。
senses.why: Machines are said to recall because they return what was put in, without any experience of remembering.
senses.whyCN: 机器被说成「回想」，是因为它把放进去的东西取出来，却没有任何记得的经验。

senses.title: The power to remember
senses.definition: the ability to remember things, especially when tested at speed
senses.definitionCN: 记住事物的能力，尤指在被快速测试时
senses.example: Her recall of dates is better than her recall of faces.
senses.exampleCN: 她对年代的记忆好过对面孔的记忆。
senses.why: The noun turns the act into a capacity, which is why one speaks of good or poor recall.
senses.whyCN: 名词把动作变成能力，所以人们说记性好或记性差。

senses.title: An order to return
senses.definition: an official notice or instruction that something must come back
senses.definitionCN: 要求某物必须返回的正式通知或指令
senses.example: A recall was issued for the faulty chargers.
senses.exampleCN: 针对有故障的充电器发布了召回令。
senses.why: The notice is the act turned into a document, the last step of the same calling-back.
senses.whyCN: 通知是动作变成文件，是同一次叫回的最后一步。

intro.en: Recall is the prefix of return, from Latin re-, joined to the English verb call, which comes from Old Norse kalla 'to cry out'. The word has no Latin root in its second element. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: recall 是表「返回」的前缀（源自拉丁 re-）加英语动词 call 构成，call 出自古诺斯语 kalla「大声喊」。第二个成分不含拉丁词根。年代均为约数。

items.en: Kalla meant 'to cry out, call loudly, summon by voice'. Its deeper origin is not established; no secure older form can be given for it.
items.cn: kalla 意为「大声喊、呼喊、以声召唤」。其更深来源未得到证明，无法给出可靠更早形式。

items.en: English took the verb in the Middle English period, where it named summoning a person or naming a thing aloud.
items.cn: 英语在中古英语时期借入这个动词，指把某人叫来，或大声念出某物的名字。

items.en: The prefix re- came into English formations from Latin, where it meant 'back, again'; in recall it adds the direction of return to a verb of calling.
items.cn: 表「返回」的前缀经拉丁进入英语构词，意为「向后、再次」；在 recall 中，它给「喊」这个动词加上返回的方向。

items.en: Recall first meant 'to call back, summon back'; the sense 'remember' is recorded from the late sixteenth century, as if memory were a place one calls a thing back from.
items.cn: recall 最初意为「叫回、召回」；「记得」这一义项自十六世纪晚期才有记录，仿佛记忆是一个可以把东西叫回来的地方。

items.en: The nineteenth and twentieth centuries added the political removal by vote, the return of defective goods, and the computing sense of fetching stored data.
items.cn: 十九与二十世纪增添了经投票罢免、收回缺陷产品，以及计算技术中取回已存数据的义项。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin and first date): the pre-Germanic source of kalla is not established, and no exact first citation is recorded for the mental sense.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源与首见年代）：kalla 在日耳曼语之前的来源未得到证明；心理义没有确切的最早书证。

note.en: Group one holds words that look like recall but come from other roots or add another layer; group two holds near neighbours of remembering and of calling back.
note.cn: 第一组是外形近似 recall、但词根不同或另加层次的词；第二组是「记得」与「叫回」两路的近义词。

entries.definition: The plain verb for summoning or naming; recall is that verb with a direction of return attached.
entries.definitionCN: 指召唤或命名的单纯动词；recall 是给它加上了返回的方向。

entries.definition: Built from Latin re- plus colligere 'to gather', so it means gathering memories up again by effort; it shares meaning with recall but not a root.
entries.definitionCN: 由拉丁表「返回」的前缀加 colligere「聚集」构成，意为费力把记忆重新聚拢；与 recall 义近而词根无关。

entries.definition: From Latin re- plus vocare 'to call', so it means calling a grant or a right back; the sense is close, the root is Latin, not Germanic.
entries.definitionCN: 由拉丁表「返回」的前缀加 vocare「呼叫」构成，意为把授予之物或权利收回；义近而词根属拉丁，不属日耳曼语。

entries.definition: An adjective for what can be summoned back or remembered; it describes a possibility, not an act.
entries.definitionCN: 指可被召回或可被想起的形容词；描述可能性，而非动作。

entries.definition: The general verb for having something come back to mind, with no sense of calling or of effort; recall is its more formal and more technical counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 指某事回到心头的泛用动词，不含「召唤」或「用力」之意；recall 是它更正式、更技术化的对应词。

entries.definition: To get something back from where it is stored, including from memory or from a disk; it stresses the fetching, not the calling.
entries.definitionCN: 指从存放处取回，包括从记忆或磁盘中取回；强调「取」，而非「叫」。

entries.definition: To order a person to come, often with authority; it is the person sense of recall without the return prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 指命令某人前来，常带权威意味；是 recall 指人那一义去掉「返回」的版本。

entries.definition: To take something back or pull it out of use, as a statement or a product; it names the removal, while recall names the calling back.
entries.definitionCN: 指把某物收回或停止使用，如声明或产品；它指「撤除」，recall 指「叫回」。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: A verb of calling plus a prefix of return: to call something back, whether a memory, an envoy or a bottle.
normal.cn: 一个表「喊」的动词加表「返回」的前缀：把某物叫回来，无论是记忆、使节还是瓶子。

normal.en: The mental sense is a metaphor made ordinary: memory is treated as a place a thing can be called back from.
normal.cn: 心理义是变成日常的比喻：记忆被当作一个可以把东西叫回来的地方。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark each sense: recall a name, recall an ambassador, recall a product, a recall election.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义：想起名字、召回大使、召回产品、罢免选举。

normal.en: The noun takes the same form, so a recall is both an act and the notice that orders it.
normal.cn: 名词与动词同形，因此同一个词既指动作，也指下令执行该动作的通知。

normal.en: Recall is not recollect: recollect gathers memories by effort, recall calls them back.
normal.cn: recall 不同于 recollect：后者靠用力把记忆聚拢，前者是把它们叫回来。

abstract.en: Picture a hand reaching into a dark box and finding the letter by its date.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手伸进暗箱，按年份摸到那封信。

abstract.en: Picture a whistle blown at the far end of a field, and everyone turns back.
abstract.cn: 想象田野尽头一声哨响，所有人转身往回走。

abstract.en: Picture a shop shelf emptied because the same bottle on every label was wrong.
abstract.cn: 想象货架被清空，因为每个标签上的同一瓶东西都不对。

examples.en: I cannot recall where I left the key, though I remember putting it down.
examples.cn: 我想不起钥匙放在哪里，虽然记得自己放下过。

examples.en: The government recalled its ambassador after the border incident.
examples.cn: 边境事件之后，政府召回大使。

examples.en: The manufacturer recalled the lot after two reports of leakage.
examples.cn: 接到两起渗漏报告后，制造商召回了那一批货。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「返回」+「喊」——把东西喊回来：记忆里喊回是回想，任所上喊回是召回，货架上喊回是收回。

root: 表「返回」的前缀（源自拉丁 re-）加英语动词 call；call 出自古诺斯语 kalla「大声喊」，kalla 更深来源未得到证明。第二个成分无拉丁词根。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one gesture: a thing is called back. Called back from the past it is memory; from a post, an envoy; from the market, a faulty batch; from office, a mayor; from a loan, a player; from a disk, a record; and the noun names either the capacity or the notice.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿同一个动作展开：把某物叫回来。从过去叫回是记忆，从任所叫回是使节，从市场叫回是缺陷批次，从职位叫回是市长，从租借叫回是球员，从磁盘叫回是记录；名词则指这种能力，或那份通知。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lid lifted on a box of dated letters, and the same hand taking back notices already sent.
core.cn: 核心意象：掀开一只装着按年份叠放信件的箱子，同一只手又把已发出的通知收回。

branches.en: THE CALL AND THE PERSON: a memory brought back, and an official ordered home.
branches.cn: 喊回与唤人：被带回的记忆，与被命令回国的官员。

branches.en: THE MEASURED CAPACITY: retrieval under test, and the noun for how good that capacity is.
branches.cn: 被测量的能力：测试中的提取，与衡量该能力强弱的名词。

branches.en: FROM GOODS TO NOTICE: the batch ordered back, and the paper that orders it.
branches.cn: 从货物到通知：被命令退回的批次，与下令的那张纸。

branches.en: THE VOTE THAT ENDS A TERM: removal by direct ballot rather than by appointment.
branches.cn: 终结任期的投票：以直接投票解职，而非由上级免职。

branches.en: TWO TEAMS AND A MACHINE: a player brought back from loan, and a record fetched from storage.
branches.cn: 两队与一台机器：从租借召回的球员，与从存储取回的记录。

intro.en: Recall is a Germanic verb under a Latin prefix, one of the many English words built by adding re- to a native verb.
intro.cn: recall 是拉丁前缀加日耳曼语动词的产物，属于英语中把「返回」前缀加在本族动词上的一大批词。

latinIntro.en: The prefix re- 'back, again' is Latin; call itself is Germanic, so any Latin list here can hold only the prefix and the later formations.
latinIntro.cn: 表「向后、再次」的前缀 re- 属拉丁；call 本身属日耳曼语，因此此处的拉丁条目只能收录该前缀与后起的构词。

items.example: The prefix reverses the direction of the verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把动词的方向倒转。

items.example: The verb named a voice raised to bring someone near.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指抬高声音把人叫近。

items.example: They called the dog from the yard.
items.exampleCN: 他们从院子里把狗叫回来。

items.example: The chair recalled the motion for a second vote.
items.exampleCN: 主席把动议叫回重投一次。

items.example: Only part of the batch is recallable.
items.exampleCN: 这批货只有一部分可召回。

items.example: The envoy remained unrecalled for a year.
items.exampleCN: 这位使节一年未被召回。

items.example: Recollection took her an hour.
items.exampleCN: 回忆花了她一小时。

items.meaning: a return call, or a request that something be returned
items.example: The helpline promises a callback within a day.
items.exampleCN: 服务热线承诺一天内回电。

definition_zh: 认出；承认；认可；外交承认；识别
definition_en: the act of identifying something as known, or of formally accepting it as real or valid
core_image: 门口的名册上写着许多名字，守门人只看一眼便把来人放进去；同一栋楼里，另一张桌上正把一枚印章按在证书上。
scene: 会场门口，接待员只看了来人一眼就说出他的名字，随即在名册上打了个钩，让他不必排队。Recognition came before any word was exchanged.
sceneCN: 这里指把眼前的人认作先前认识的那一个（第 1 个义项：认出）；句意为在开口之前，认出就已经发生了。

pos.zh: 认出；承认；认可；外交承认；识别（可数或不可数）

derivatives.zh: 认出；承认（拉丁 recognoscere「重新认识」，由「再看一眼而认识」转指「认出」与「正式承认」）
可认出的（加表「能够」的形容词词尾，由「认出」转指「可被认出」）
具结；保证金（法律术语，由「承认」转指「向法庭作出的承认」）
与识别有关的（加拉丁形容词词尾，由「认识」转指「涉及识别活动」）
未被认出的；未获承认的（加表否定的前缀，由「被承认」转指「未被承认」）

senses.title: Identifying something as known
senses.definition: the act of seeing or hearing something and knowing that one has met it before
senses.definitionCN: 看到或听到某物时，知道从前遇见过它
senses.example: Recognition came before any word was exchanged at the door.
senses.exampleCN: 在门口，认出发生在交谈之前。
senses.why: The prefix of 'again' plus a verb of knowing gives exactly this: knowing again what is in front of one.
senses.whyCN: 表「再次」的前缀加表「认识」的动词，正好给出这层意思：把眼前之物再认识一次。

senses.title: Recognition memory
senses.definition: in psychology, the form of memory in which a presented item is judged as old or new
senses.definitionCN: 心理学指对所呈现条目判断其是否曾出现过的那类记忆
senses.example: The recognition test asked whether each word had appeared in the list.
senses.exampleCN: 再认测试问每个词是否在词表中出现过。
senses.why: The laboratory split memory into recall and recognition: one produces the item, the other only accepts it.
senses.whyCN: 实验室把记忆分成回想与再认：前者产出条目，后者只负责认可。

senses.title: Credit for merit
senses.definition: the acknowledgement of someone's work or achievement, often publicly
senses.definitionCN: 对某人工作或成就的肯定，常为公开的
senses.example: She received recognition for twenty years of teaching.
senses.exampleCN: 她因二十年的教学获得表彰。
senses.why: Credit is recognition in its social form: the work is known again by those who did not do it.
senses.whyCN: 表彰是 recognition 的社会形态：工作被没做它的人重新认识。

senses.title: Diplomatic acceptance
senses.definition: the formal acceptance by one state of another state or government as legitimate
senses.definitionCN: 一国对另一国或其政府的合法地位的正式接受
senses.example: Recognition of the new government came after the ceasefire.
senses.exampleCN: 停火之后，对新政府的承认才到来。
senses.why: Here the knowing-again is institutional: a state says it now accepts what exists as legitimate.
senses.whyCN: 此处的「再认识」是制度性的：国家宣布它现在接受既存者为合法。

senses.title: Machine identification
senses.definition: the automatic identification of patterns, speech or objects by a system
senses.definitionCN: 系统对图案、语音或物体的自动辨识
senses.example: Speech recognition still fails in a noisy kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 语音识别在嘈杂的厨房里仍会失败。
senses.why: A system repeats the perceptual act at scale: it matches input against what it has stored.
senses.whyCN: 系统把知觉动作规模化重复：把输入与已存内容匹配。

senses.title: The chair's acknowledgement
senses.definition: in a formal meeting, the act by which the chair allows a member to speak
senses.definitionCN: 正式会议中，主席准许某位成员发言的行为
senses.example: The delegate waited ten minutes for recognition.
senses.exampleCN: 那位代表等了十分钟才被准许发言。
senses.why: A chair recognises a speaker in the formal sense of accepting that the member now has the floor.
senses.whyCN: 主席「承认」发言者，用的是「接受该成员现在取得发言权」的正式含义。

senses.title: Legal acceptance of a foreign act
senses.titleCN: 对他国法律行为的承认
senses.definition: the acceptance by a court of another jurisdiction's judgment or right
senses.definitionCN: 法院对另一辖区判决或权利的接受
senses.example: Recognition of the foreign award allowed enforcement.
senses.exampleCN: 承认该外国裁决之后才得以执行。
senses.why: Law keeps the formal sense: to recognize is to accept as valid, not merely to notice.
senses.whyCN: 法律保留正式义：承认即接受为有效，而不只是注意到。

senses.title: Immune identification
senses.definition: the ability of a body's defences to tell its own tissue from a foreign one
senses.definitionCN: 机体防御系统分辨自身组织与外来物的能力
senses.example: Recognition of the graft as foreign triggered rejection.
senses.exampleCN: 移植物被识别为外来物，从而引发排斥。
senses.why: The body must know its own tissue again and again, and rejection follows a failed recognition.
senses.whyCN: 身体必须一遍遍重新认出自身组织，识别失败便引发排斥。

senses.title: Public standing
senses.definition: the state of being known and respected by a wider public
senses.definitionCN: 被更广泛的公众所知并尊重的状态
senses.example: The design won recognition beyond the region.
senses.exampleCN: 这项设计赢得了本地区之外的认可。
