senses.why: The noun of an act becomes a noun of a state, which is why recognition can be won, lost and sought.
senses.whyCN: 动作的名词变成状态的名词，所以 recognition 可以被获得、赢得、失去与追求。

intro.en: Recognition comes from Latin recognitio, from recognoscere 'to know again', built on re- 'again' plus cognoscere 'to get to know'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: recognition 出自拉丁 recognitio，来自 recognoscere「重新认识」，由表「再次」的前缀加 cognoscere「得知、认识」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Cognoscere meant 'to get to know, learn, recognise', built from an intensive prefix plus gnoscere 'to know'. The root behind gnoscere is reconstructed, and that form is a reconstruction.
items.cn: cognoscere 意为「得知、了解、认出」，由表加强的前缀加 gnoscere「知道」构成。gnoscere 背后的词根属重构，只是重构形式。

items.en: Re- 'again' plus cognoscere gave recognoscere 'to know again, call to mind, examine'. The prefix does the whole work of the later English sense.
items.cn: 表「再次」的前缀加 cognoscere 构成 recognoscere「重新认识、想起、审视」。这个前缀承担了后来英语义项的全部工作。

items.en: Recognitio named the act of examining or acknowledging, and it is the direct source of the English noun.
items.cn: recognitio 指审视或承认的行为，是英语名词的直接来源。

items.en: The noun entered English in the fifteenth century through French, first naming an examination or a formal acknowledgement.
items.cn: 这个名词在十五世纪经法语进入英语，最初指审视或正式的承认。

items.en: Diplomatic recognition took shape in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries; recognition memory in psychology and pattern recognition in computing belong to the nineteenth and twentieth.
items.cn: 外交承认在十八至十九世纪成形；心理学的再认记忆与计算技术的模式识别属十九至二十世纪。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper origin): no exact first citation is fixed, and the pre-Latin root behind gnoscere is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：没有确切的最早书证；gnoscere 背后的拉丁语之前词根属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds forms of the same verb of knowing; group two holds nouns of identification and of formal acceptance.
note.cn: 第一组是同一个表「认识」动词的各词形；第二组是表示辨识与正式接受的近义名词。

entries.definition: The verb for identifying or accepting; the noun names the act or the state that follows it.
entries.definitionCN: 指认出或承认的动词；名词指该动作或由此形成的状态。

entries.definition: An adjective for what can be identified at once; it describes a quality, not an event.
entries.definitionCN: 指可被立刻认出的形容词；描述性质，而非事件。

entries.definition: A formal acknowledgement made to a court, often a bond to appear; it is a narrow legal descendant, not the general noun.
entries.definitionCN: 指向法庭作出的正式承认，常指保证到庭的具结；是狭窄的法律后代，而非泛用名词。

entries.definition: The general term for mental processes of knowing, without the prefix of 'again'; recognition is one such process.
entries.definitionCN: 指认知过程的泛称，不含表「再次」的前缀；recognition 是其中一种。

entries.definition: The act of establishing what something is, often by checking a document or a mark; recognition may happen without any such check.
entries.definitionCN: 指确定某物是什么的行为，常靠核对证件或标记；recognition 可以不经核对就发生。

entries.definition: The act of admitting or thanking; it covers the credit sense of recognition but not the perceptual one.
entries.definitionCN: 指承认或致谢的行为；涵盖 recognition 的表彰义，但不含知觉义。

entries.definition: The act of receiving something as satisfactory or valid; the diplomatic and legal senses of recognition are a formal kind of acceptance.
entries.definitionCN: 指把某物视为合格或有效而接受；recognition 的外交与法律义是正式的一类接受。

entries.definition: The act of discovering that something is present, as with a sensor; recognition goes further and says what it is.
entries.definitionCN: 指发现某物存在，如传感器所做；recognition 更进一步，说明它是什么。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: A prefix of 'again' on a verb of knowing: to know again what is standing in front of you.
normal.cn: 表「再次」的前缀加表「认识」的动词：把眼前的东西再认识一次。

normal.en: The family runs recognize, recognizable, recognizance and unrecognized, all from the same verb of knowing.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 recognize、recognizable、recognizance、unrecognized，全出同一个表「认识」的动词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the fields: in recognition of service, diplomatic recognition, pattern recognition.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：为表彰服务、外交承认、模式识别。

normal.en: Psychology pairs the word with recall: one produces the item, the other only accepts it as old.
normal.cn: 心理学把这个词与回想并置：一个产出条目，另一个只把它认作旧的。

normal.en: The noun slides from act to state, so recognition can be received, won, lost and sought.
normal.cn: 名词从动作滑向状态，因此 recognition 可以被获得、赢得、失去与追求。

abstract.en: Picture a doorkeeper who nods before the name is spoken.
abstract.cn: 想象守门人在名字说出口之前就点了头。

abstract.en: Picture a stamp pressed on a certificate that was already true but not yet valid.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚印章按在一份本已真实、却尚未生效的证书上。

abstract.en: Picture a body's guards checking every cell at the gate and turning away the stranger.
abstract.cn: 想象身体的守卫在门口逐一查验细胞，把外来者挡回去。

examples.en: Recognition of the melody came before she could name the composer.
examples.cn: 她还没想起作曲者，就已经认出了那段旋律。

examples.en: The prize was given in recognition of his work on coastal erosion.
examples.cn: 该奖项为表彰他在海岸侵蚀方面的工作而颁发。

examples.en: Several states extended recognition to the provisional government.
examples.cn: 若干国家承认了这个临时政府。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「再次」+「认识」——再看一眼就认出来；认得出是人，也认得出是国家，认得出是旧词，也认得出是外来细胞。

root: 拉丁 recognitio，来自 recognoscere「重新认识」= 表「再次」的前缀 + cognoscere「得知、认识」，cognoscere 又由表加强的前缀加 gnoscere「知道」；gnoscere 背后的词根属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one act: knowing again. Applied to a face it is perception; to a list it is a memory test; to work it is credit; to a state it is diplomacy; to a pattern it is a machine; to a speaker it is the chair's nod; to a judgment it is law; to a graft it is immunity; and to a public it is standing.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿同一个动作展开：再认识一次。用在面孔上是知觉，用在词表上是记忆测验，用在作品上是表彰，用在国家上是外交，用在图案上是机器，用在发言者身上是主席的点头，用在判决上是法律，用在移植物上是免疫，用在公众身上是声望。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a doorkeeper who nods before the name is spoken, and a stamp pressed on a certificate already true.
core.cn: 核心意象：名字尚未出口就点头的守门人，以及按在本已真实的证书上的印章。

branches.en: SEEING AND TESTING: the everyday act of knowing a face, and the laboratory form that only says old or new.
branches.cn: 认出与测验：日常认出面孔的动作，与实验室里只判断新旧的形式。

branches.en: FROM CREDIT TO STANDING: public thanks for work, and the wider reputation it leaves behind.
branches.cn: 从表彰到声望：对工作的公开致谢，以及它留下的更广名声。

branches.en: FORMAL ACCEPTANCE: a state accepted as legitimate, and a foreign judgment accepted as valid.
branches.cn: 正式接受：被承认为合法的国家，与被承认为有效的外国判决。

branches.en: THE MACHINE'S EYE: a system that names the pattern it has been trained on.
branches.cn: 机器之眼：把受过训练的图案说出名字的系统。

branches.en: TWO KINDS OF PERMISSION: the chair's nod to speak, and a body's guards deciding what belongs.
branches.cn: 两种许可：主席准许发言的点头，与身体守卫判定何者属于自身。

intro.en: Recognition is three Latin pieces: a prefix of again, an intensive prefix, and a verb of knowing.
intro.cn: recognition 由三块拉丁成分组成：表「再次」的前缀、表加强的前缀，与一个表「知道」的动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin cognoscere gives cognition, cognitive and recognize; re- adds the repetition that makes recognition.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 cognoscere 衍生 cognition、cognitive、recognize；表「再次」的前缀加上重复，才成为 recognition。

items.structure: gnoscere (Latin verb, older form of noscere)
items.example: The verb is the oldest layer of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是词族中最老的一层。

items.example: The prefix made knowing into a process of finding out.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「知道」变成「查明」的过程。

items.example: The verb named a second look that ends in certainty.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指以确定告终的第二次查看。

items.example: The noun named both the check and the admission.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词兼指核查与承认。

items.example: She recognized the handwriting at once.
items.exampleCN: 她一眼认出了笔迹。

items.meaning: the act of identifying or accepting
items.example: Recognition of the claim took two years.
items.exampleCN: 对该主张的承认花了两年。

items.example: The tune is recognizable in three notes.
items.exampleCN: 这支曲子三个音就能认出。

items.example: Cognition covers perception and memory.
items.exampleCN: 认知涵盖知觉与记忆。

latinEntries.structure: gnoscere (older Latin verb, replaced by noscere)

definition_en: the loss of something from memory, or the act of failing to keep it in mind
core_image: 一块写满字的石板被雨水一遍遍冲刷，笔画从边缘开始变淡；旁边一把钥匙留在门内的桌上，主人已经走远。
scene: 雨夜里，写满字的石板被雨水一遍遍冲刷，靠边的笔画先淡下去，中间的字还留着，主人却已经想不起自己写过什么。Forgetting began at the edges and took the middle last.
sceneCN: 这里指记忆内容逐渐失去、变得无法提取（第 1 个义项：遗忘）；句意为遗忘从边缘开始，最后才吞掉中间。

pos.zh: 遗忘；忘记；疏忽（不可数，指过程；可数时指具体的遗忘事例）

derivatives.zh: 忘记；遗忘（基础词加表「离开、错失」的古英语前缀，再加表「抓住」的动词，由「抓不住」转指「记不住」）
健忘的（加表「充满」的形容词词尾，由「忘记」转指「易于忘记」）
健忘地（加副词词尾，由形容词转指行为方式）
难忘的（加表否定与「能够」的两重成分，由「被忘记」转指「不可能被忘记」）
健忘（加表性质的名词词尾，由形容词转指该性质）

senses.title: Loss of what was in memory
senses.definition: the state or process in which something once known can no longer be brought to mind
senses.definitionCN: 曾知道的事物不再能被带回意识的状态或过程
senses.example: Forgetting began at the edges and took the middle last.
senses.exampleCN: 遗忘从边缘开始，最后才吞掉中间。
senses.why: The core is a lost grip: what was once held in mind is no longer held.
senses.whyCN: 核心是失去把握：曾经握在心里的东西不再被握住。

senses.title: The measured decay of retention
senses.definition: in psychology, the decline of what can be reproduced after learning, often plotted against time
senses.definitionCN: 心理学指学习后可复现内容的下降，常按时间画成曲线
senses.example: The forgetting curve fell steeply in the first hour.
senses.exampleCN: 遗忘曲线在第一个小时里陡降。
senses.why: Laboratory work turned a common experience into a measurable quantity, and the noun followed the graph.
senses.whyCN: 实验室工作把共同的经验变成可测量的量，名词便跟着那条曲线走。

senses.title: Deliberate putting out of mind
senses.definition: the conscious decision to stop dwelling on something, often a wrong or a loss
senses.definitionCN: 有意决定不再纠缠某事，常指过错或损失
senses.example: Her forgetting of the insult was a decision, not a failure.
senses.exampleCN: 她对那次侮辱的遗忘是一个决定，而不是失灵。
senses.why: The word can name an act of will, which is why forgiveness and forgetting are so often paired.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以指意志的动作，所以宽恕与遗忘常被并提。

senses.title: Neglect of a duty
senses.definition: the failure to attend to something one was obliged to remember
senses.definitionCN: 未能顾及本应记得的事
senses.example: The forgetting of the safety check was reported as a fault.
senses.exampleCN: 漏掉安全检查被记为一次过失。
senses.why: A duty one was bound to keep in mind is dropped, so the failure counts as negligence rather than as memory loss.
senses.whyCN: 本应记在心上的职责被丢掉，于是这种失灵算疏忽，而不算记忆丧失。

senses.title: Leaving something behind
senses.definition: the accidental failure to take something one meant to bring
senses.definitionCN: 本打算带走却意外没带
senses.example: The forgetting of the keys cost them an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 忘带钥匙让他们损失了一小时。
senses.why: The object is lost not from memory but from the hand, and the same word covers both.
senses.whyCN: 物件不是从记忆里丢失，而是从手上丢失，同一个词兼指两者。

senses.title: Losing oneself
senses.definition: the failure to keep one's own conduct in mind, as in losing restraint
senses.definitionCN: 未能看住自己的举止，如失去节制
senses.example: In the noise of the crowd there was a general forgetting of manners.
senses.exampleCN: 在人声鼎沸中，众人一时忘了礼节。
senses.why: What is forgotten here is one's own restraint, the object of the verb being the self.
senses.whyCN: 这里被忘记的是自己的节制，动词的对象就是自身。

senses.title: Erasure from the record
senses.definition: the dropping of an event or a person from written or public memory
senses.definitionCN: 把某个事件或某个人从书面或公共记忆中删去
senses.example: The forgetting of the treaty in later chronicles was deliberate.
senses.exampleCN: 后来的编年史对这条约的遗忘是有意的。
senses.why: Written memory can be edited, so an event can be forgotten by a record rather than by a person.
senses.whyCN: 书面记忆可以被编辑，因此一个事件能被记录而非被人遗忘。

senses.title: Useful dropping of the outdated
senses.titleCN: 对过时信息的有效舍弃
senses.definition: the adaptive discarding of information that no longer helps, so that newer material can be used
senses.definitionCN: 主动舍弃不再有用的信息，以便使用更新的材料
senses.example: Some forgetting is useful: old passwords only get in the way.
senses.exampleCN: 有些遗忘是有益的：旧密码只会碍事。
senses.why: Modern psychology treats the noun as neutral and sometimes as a virtue, against the older view of it as pure loss.
senses.whyCN: 现代心理学把这个名词看作中性，有时甚至是优点，与旧看法视之为纯粹损失相反。

intro.en: Forgetting is the Old English verb forgietan plus the noun suffix -ing. The verb joins a prefix of loss to a verb of grasping, and there is no Latin element. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: forgetting 是古英语动词 forgietan 加表动作的名词词尾构成。这个动词把表「失去」的前缀加在一个表「抓住」的动词上，词中不含拉丁成分。年代均为约数。

items.en: The prefix for- meant 'away, amiss, wrongly', and in many verbs it marked loss or destruction, as it still does in forbid and forlorn.
items.cn: 表「离开、错失、错误」的前缀在许多动词中标记失去或毁坏，在「禁止」与「被遗弃的」两个词中至今可见。

items.en: Gietan meant 'to grasp, seize', and it is related to the modern verb get. Its deeper origin is not established.
items.cn: gietan 意为「抓住、握取」，与现代动词 get 相关。其更深来源未得到证明。

items.en: For- plus gietan produced forgietan 'to lose from the mind, fail to keep', literally to lose one's grasp on something.
items.cn: 表「失去」的前缀加 gietan 构成 forgietan「从心中失去、未能保住」，字面是「失去对某物的把握」。

items.en: The noun forgetting is recorded in Middle English, naming both the failure to remember and the state of having lost something from mind.
items.cn: 名词 forgetting 在中古英语中已有记录，既指未能记住，也指已从心中失去的状态。

items.en: From the late nineteenth century the noun was used in experiments on retention, and the forgetting curve became a standard term.
items.cn: 从十九世纪晚期起，这个名词被用于保持量的实验，遗忘曲线成为标准术语。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Germanic source of gietan is not established, and no exact first citation is recorded for the noun.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：gietan 在日耳曼语之前的来源未得到证明；这个名词没有确切的最早书证。

note.en: Group one holds words of the same native verb of losing one's grasp; group two holds near neighbours of memory loss and of neglect.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「失去把握」这一本族动词的词；第二组是记忆丧失与疏忽两路的近义词。

entries.definition: The verb for losing something from mind or leaving it behind; the noun names the process or the instance.
entries.definitionCN: 指把某事从心中失去或落在别处的动词；名词指该过程或具体事例。

entries.definition: An adjective for a person who often forgets; it describes a habit, not an event.
entries.definitionCN: 形容经常忘记的人；描述习惯，而非事件。

entries.definition: An adjective for what cannot be forgotten, usually because it was striking; it is the direct opposite of the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 形容无法被忘记者，通常因其震撼；与名词正好相反。

entries.definition: Built from the same prefix of loss but on a verb meaning 'to give', so it means to give up a claim against someone; it is not a relative of forget at the root.
entries.definitionCN: 由同一个表「失去」的前缀加一个表「给」的动词构成，意为放弃对某人的追究；词根上与 forget 并非同族。

entries.definition: A brief failure of memory or of attention, as in a lapse of concentration; it names the slip, not the long process.
entries.definitionCN: 指记忆或注意的短暂失误，如注意力的一时松懈；指那次失误，而非长期过程。

entries.definition: The medical term for loss of memory caused by injury or illness; it is a condition, while forgetting is an everyday process.
entries.definitionCN: 指因损伤或疾病造成记忆丧失的医学名词；它是一种病症，而遗忘是日常过程。

entries.definition: The act of leaving something out, often deliberately, as in an omission from a report; it need not involve memory at all.
entries.definitionCN: 指把某物遗漏，常为有意，如报告中漏掉一项；完全可以与记忆无关。

entries.definition: The failure to give proper attention to a duty or a person; it is broader than forgetting and need not be caused by memory.
entries.definitionCN: 指未对职责或人给予应有照料；比遗忘更宽，且不必由记忆造成。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: A prefix of loss on a verb of grasping: literally to lose one's grip on something.
normal.cn: 表「失去」的前缀加表「抓住」的动词：字面就是失去对某物的把握。

normal.en: The family runs forget, forgetful, forgetfulness and unforgettable; forgive shares the prefix but not the root.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 forget、forgetful、forgetfulness、unforgettable；forgive 共用前缀却不共词根。

normal.en: Fixed phrases place the word in science and in life: the forgetting curve, deliberate forgetting, the forgetting of a name.
normal.cn: 固定搭配把词放进科学与生活：遗忘曲线、刻意遗忘、忘记一个名字。

normal.en: The noun is neutral in psychology, where some forgetting is useful, and negative in ordinary speech, where it is a fault.
normal.cn: 这个名词在心理学中是中性的，有些遗忘甚至有益；在日常说法中则是负面的，视为过失。

normal.en: The word has no Latin layer, so every attempt to read it as a Latin derivative is a false lead.
normal.cn: 这个词没有拉丁层，凡把它读作拉丁派生词的做法都是歧路。

abstract.en: Picture a slate washed by rain from the edges inward.
abstract.cn: 想象一块石板被雨从边缘往里冲刷。

abstract.en: Picture keys left on a table inside a room already locked.
abstract.cn: 想象钥匙留在已经锁上的屋里桌上。

abstract.en: Picture a drawer cleared of old passwords so the new one fits.
abstract.cn: 想象抽屉清掉旧密码，才放得下新的。

examples.en: Forgetting is fastest in the first hours after learning.
examples.cn: 遗忘在学习之后的头几个小时里最快。

examples.en: The forgetting of her name at the reception embarrassed him.
examples.cn: 在招待会上忘了她的名字，让他很尴尬。

examples.en: Some forgetting keeps a mind from drowning in detail.
examples.cn: 有些遗忘使头脑不致淹没在细节里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「失去」+「抓住」——抓不住了，就是忘了；记不住、落下东西、疏忽职责，都是同一次松手。

root: 古英语 forgietan「从心中失去」= 表「离开、错失」的前缀 + gietan「抓住、握取」，gietan 与现代动词 get 相关，其更深来源未得到证明。词中无拉丁成分。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one failure: a grip is lost. Lost from memory it is forgetting; lost in a measured curve it is a laboratory quantity; given up on purpose it is a decision; lost along with a duty, a pair of keys or one's manners it becomes negligence; lost from the record it is erasure; and dropped because it no longer helps it becomes useful.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次失灵展开：把握失去了。从记忆里失去是遗忘；在可测曲线里失去是一个实验量；有意放弃是一个决定；连同职责、钥匙或礼节一起失去便成为疏忽；从记录里失去是被抹去；因不再有用而丢掉，则成了有益之举。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a slate washed by rain from the edges inward, and keys left on a table in a locked room.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块被雨从边缘往里冲刷的石板，与留在已锁房间桌上的钥匙。

branches.en: LOSS AND ITS GRAPH: the plain failure, and the same failure counted against time.
branches.cn: 失去与它的曲线：素朴的失灵，与把同一次失灵按时间计数。

branches.en: THE DECISION NOT TO DWELL: forgetting chosen rather than suffered.
branches.cn: 不再纠缠的决定：被选择而非被遭受的遗忘。

branches.en: MISSED AND LEFT: a duty not attended to, and a thing not carried away.
branches.cn: 漏掉与落下：未被顾及的职责，与未被带走的物件。

branches.en: CONDUCT FORGOTTEN: restraint itself drops out of mind.
branches.cn: 忘了举止：连节制也从心中滑落。

branches.en: TWO ERASURES: an event struck from the record, and an old detail cleared to make room.
branches.cn: 两种抹除：被从记录中删去的事件，与被清掉以腾出位置的旧细节。

intro.en: Forgetting is native English: a prefix of loss, a verb of grasping, and a suffix of action.
intro.cn: forgetting 是纯英语本族词：表「失去」的前缀、表「抓住」的动词，加表动作的后缀。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin element here, so the Latin list is left empty; the older strata are Old English only.
latinIntro.cn: 此处不含拉丁成分，因此拉丁条目留空；更早的层次纯属古英语。

items.structure: for- (Old English prefix of loss or wrongness)
items.example: The prefix marks a failure rather than a direction.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标记失败，而非方向。

items.structure: gietan (Old English verb, strong class five)
items.example: The verb is the ancestor of modern get.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是现代 get 的祖先。

items.example: The compound turned a grasp into a losing of hold.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词把「抓握」变成「失去把握」。

items.meaning: to fail to remember or to bring
items.example: I forget the address every winter.
items.exampleCN: 每年冬天我都忘记那个地址。

items.meaning: the losing of a grip on memory
items.example: Forgetting is not always a fault.
items.exampleCN: 遗忘并不总是过失。

items.example: He grew forgetful about appointments.
items.exampleCN: 他对约定越来越健忘。

items.example: Forgetfulness ran in the family.
items.exampleCN: 健忘在这个家里代代都有。

items.example: The view from the ridge was unforgettable.
items.exampleCN: 山脊上的景色令人难忘。

definition_en: the act of getting something back from where it is stored, held or lost
core_image: 一只系着绳的桶从井底被提上来，桶里是先前落下去的东西；同一双手在另一处从书架最深处抽出一本久借未还的册子。
scene: 井台上，绳子一圈圈被收上来，桶从黑水里露出，先前落下去的那只铁盒就在桶底。The retrieval took longer than the drop had.
sceneCN: 这里指把落下去的东西重新取回（第 1 个义项：取回）；句意为取回所花的时间比落下去还长。

pos.zh: 取回；检索；提取；找回（可数指一次操作，不可数指该功能）

derivatives.zh: 取回；检索；挽回（古法语 retrouver「重新找到」，由「再次」加「找到」构成，由「找回」转指「挽救」）
可取回的（加表「能够」的形容词词尾，由动作转指「可被取回」）
寻回犬（加表施事者的词尾，由「找回」转指「替人捡回猎物者」）
无法挽回的（加表否定的前缀，由「可取回」转指「不可取回」）

senses.title: Getting something back
senses.definition: the act of recovering something that had been lost, taken away or left in a place
senses.definitionCN: 把丢失、被拿走或留在某处的东西重新收回的行为
senses.example: The retrieval of the dropped box took an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 把掉落的盒子取回来花了一小时。
senses.why: The core is literal: something went away or down, and it is brought back.
senses.whyCN: 核心是字面的：某物离开或落下，再被带回。

senses.title: Bringing an item out of memory
senses.definition: in psychology, the process of locating a stored memory and bringing it into awareness
senses.definitionCN: 心理学指定位已存记忆并把它带入意识的过程
senses.example: Retrieval failed at the tip of the tongue.
senses.exampleCN: 提取在「话到嘴边」的地方失败了。
senses.why: Memory is treated as a store, so getting something out of it takes the same verb as getting something out of a well.
senses.whyCN: 记忆被当作仓库，所以从里面取出东西，与从井里取出东西用同一个动词。

senses.title: Finding relevant documents
senses.definition: in information science, the process of locating documents that answer a query
senses.definitionCN: 信息科学指找出回应某一查询的文献的过程
senses.example: The library's retrieval system ranks results by date.
senses.exampleCN: 该馆的检索系统按日期排列结果。
senses.why: Documents are stored, so finding the right ones takes the same word as getting an object back.
senses.whyCN: 文献是被存放的，因此找出合适的那几篇，与取回物件用同一个词。

senses.title: Fetching a record from a database
senses.definition: in computing, the lookup of stored records by a key or a query
senses.definitionCN: 计算领域指按键值或查询取回已存记录
senses.example: Faster retrieval came from indexing the date field.
senses.exampleCN: 更快的取回来自给日期字段建索引。
senses.why: A record is held at a location, and lookup brings it back from that location.
senses.whyCN: 记录被存放在某个位置，查询把它从那里取回。

senses.title: Recovering damaged or deleted data
senses.titleCN: 恢复受损或删除的数据
senses.definition: the recovery of files or data after deletion, damage or failure
senses.definitionCN: 指在删除、损坏或故障之后恢复文件或数据
senses.example: Data retrieval after the crash recovered most of the archive.
senses.exampleCN: 崩溃之后的数据恢复挽回了大部分档案。
senses.why: Deleted data is still somewhere on the medium, so getting it back is retrieval rather than invention.
senses.whyCN: 被删的数据仍在介质某处，所以把它取回是取回，而非凭空造出。

senses.title: Fetching a physical item
senses.definition: the act of going to a shelf, a stack or a storeroom and bringing an item out
senses.definitionCN: 指到书架、书库或储藏室把某物取出来
senses.example: Retrieval from the closed stacks requires a written slip.
senses.exampleCN: 从闭架书库取书需要一张书面申请。
senses.why: A shelf is a store like any other, and the book is brought out of it by hand.
senses.whyCN: 书架与别的仓库无异，书是被手从里面取出来的。

senses.title: Rescue of a person or thing
senses.definition: the recovery of someone or something from danger or loss
senses.definitionCN: 把某人或某物从危险或丧失中救回
senses.example: The retrieval of the climbers took two helicopters.
senses.exampleCN: 把登山者救回来动用了两架直升机。
senses.why: The core sense of getting back extends to lives, where the getting back is a rescue.
senses.whyCN: 核心义「取回」延伸到生命，此时的取回就是营救。

senses.title: Recovery of something abstract
senses.definition: the restoration of a reputation, a meaning or a situation that had been lost
senses.definitionCN: 使名声、意义或局面从失去状态复原
senses.example: The retrieval of his reputation took years of quiet work.
senses.exampleCN: 他名声的挽回花了多年默默的工作。
senses.why: Abstract things are treated like objects in a well: they can be lost, and they can be got back.
senses.whyCN: 抽象之物被当作井中之物：可以失去，也可以取回。

intro.en: Retrieval is the verb retrieve plus the noun suffix -al. Retrieve comes from Old French retrouver 'to find again', built on re- 'again' plus trouver 'to find'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: retrieval 是动词 retrieve 加名词词尾构成。retrieve 出自古法语 retrouver「重新找到」，由表「再次」的前缀加 trouver「找到」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Trouver meant 'to find'. It goes back to a Vulgar Latin verb meaning 'to compose, contrive, find', which is itself a reconstruction and which is usually traced to Greek tropos 'a turn'.
items.cn: trouver 意为「找到」。它上溯一个俗拉丁动词，意为「编排、设法、找到」，该形式本身属重构，通常又被追溯到希腊 tropos「转向」。

items.en: Re- 'again' plus trouver produced retrouver 'to find again, recover', the direct source of the English verb.
items.cn: 表「再次」的前缀加 trouver 构成 retrouver「重新找到、找回」，是英语动词的直接来源。

items.en: English took the verb in the Middle English period, first for recovering something lost and for fetching game in hunting.
items.cn: 英语在中古英语时期借入这个动词，最初指找回失物，也指打猎时把猎物捡回。

items.en: Retrieval is a later noun formed on the English verb with the suffix -al, naming the act rather than the agent.
items.cn: retrieval 是后起的名词，在英语动词后加名词词尾构成，指动作而非施事者。

items.en: Memory retrieval became a psychological term in the late nineteenth century, and information retrieval named a field in the mid-twentieth.
items.cn: 记忆提取在十九世纪晚期成为心理学术语；信息检索在二十世纪中期成为一个领域名称。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper origin): the Vulgar Latin verb behind trouver is a reconstruction, the path from Greek tropos is a hypothesis, and no exact first citation is recorded for the noun.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：trouver 背后的俗拉丁动词属重构形式，从希腊 tropos 来的路径属假说；名词没有确切的最早书证。

note.en: Group one holds forms of the same French verb of finding again; group two holds nouns of getting something back.
note.cn: 第一组是同出法语「重新找到」这一动词的词形；第二组是表示「取回」的近义名词。

entries.definition: The verb for getting something back; the noun names the act as a thing that can be timed and measured.
entries.definitionCN: 指取回的动词；名词把该动作当作可计时、可测量之事。

entries.definition: An adjective for what can still be recovered; it describes a possibility, not an operation.
entries.definitionCN: 指仍可被取回的形容词；描述可能性，而非操作。

entries.definition: A dog bred to fetch game, or a person who recovers things; it names the agent, not the act.
entries.definitionCN: 指被培育来捡回猎物的犬，或负责找回物件的人；指施事者，而非动作。

entries.definition: From re- plus a Latin verb meaning 'to draw', so it means drawing back; the sound is close but the root is trahere, not trouver.
entries.definitionCN: 由表「返回」的前缀加一个意为「拉」的拉丁动词构成，意为后撤；读音相近，但词根是「拉」，不是「找到」。

entries.definition: The act of getting something back or returning to health; it is broader and often implies restoring a state.
entries.definitionCN: 指取回某物或恢复健康的行为；更宽泛，常含「恢复原状」之意。

entries.definition: Bringing something back to mind or summoning it back; it is the mental side, while retrieval also covers stores and files.
entries.definitionCN: 指把某物带回意识或叫回；偏心理一侧，而 retrieval 还包括仓库与文件。

entries.definition: The act of drawing something out of where it is fixed, as a tooth or data from a file; it stresses removal, not return.
entries.definitionCN: 指把固定在某处的东西拔出，如牙齿或文件中的数据；强调取出，而非返回。

entries.definition: The everyday verb for going and bringing something back; retrieval is its formal noun, used for systems and memories.
entries.definitionCN: 指去把某物拿回来的日常动词；retrieval 是它正式的名词形式，多用于系统与记忆。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: A prefix of 'again' on a verb of finding: to find again what had been lost.
normal.cn: 表「再次」的前缀加表「找到」的动词：把失去的东西再找回来。

normal.en: The family runs retrieve, retrievable, retriever and irretrievable, all from one French verb.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 retrieve、retrievable、retriever、irretrievable，全出同一个法语动词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the fields: information retrieval, memory retrieval, data retrieval, beyond retrieval.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：信息检索、记忆提取、数据检索、无法挽回。

normal.en: Memory is treated as a well: something is lowered in, and later drawn up.
normal.cn: 记忆被当作一口井：东西放下去，之后再提上来。

normal.en: The noun is the act, the agent is the dog: a retriever does the retrieval.
normal.cn: 名词是动作，施事者是狗：寻回犬做的就是 retrieval。

abstract.en: Picture a bucket on a rope coming up out of dark water with a box inside.
abstract.cn: 想象一只系绳的桶从黑水里上来，桶底有只盒子。

abstract.en: Picture a hand reaching into the deepest shelf for a book long overdue.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手伸进最深的一格书架，抽出那本久借未还的书。

abstract.en: Picture a rope thrown to two climbers on a ledge.
abstract.cn: 想象一根绳子抛向岩台上的两名登山者。

examples.en: Retrieval of the file failed because the index was corrupt.
examples.cn: 取回该文件失败，因为索引已经损坏。

examples.en: Each retrieval from memory alters what is stored.
examples.cn: 每一次从记忆中提取都会改变所存的内容。

examples.en: The archive charges a fee for retrieval from the closed stacks.
examples.cn: 该档案馆对从闭架书库取书收取费用。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「再次」+「找到」——再找回来：从井里、从书架、从记忆、从磁盘，都是同一次提拉。

root: 古法语 retrouver「重新找到」= 表「再次」的前缀 + trouver「找到」；trouver 上溯一个俗拉丁动词（属重构形式），通常再追溯到希腊 tropos「转向」，该路径属假说。英语 retrieval 由动词加名词词尾构成。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one gesture: something is drawn back out. Out of a well it is a box; out of memory an item; out of a collection a document; out of a database a record; out of a broken disk a file; out of closed stacks a book; out of danger a climber; and out of disgrace a reputation.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：把某物重新提出来。从井里提出的是盒子，从记忆里提出的是条目，从文献集合里提出的是文档，从数据库里提出的是记录，从损坏的磁盘里提出的是文件，从闭架书库提出的是书，从危险中提出的是登山者，从耻辱中提出的是名声。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bucket on a rope rising out of dark water, and a hand pulling a long-overdue book from the deepest shelf.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只系绳的桶从黑水里升起，一只手从最深的一格书架抽出久借未还的书。

branches.en: THE PHYSICAL AND THE URGENT: a dropped box hauled up, and climbers roped off a ledge.
branches.cn: 实物与急难：被拉上来的落水盒子，与用绳索救离岩台的登山者。

branches.en: THE MIND'S STORE: an item located and brought into awareness, sometimes failing at the tip of the tongue.
branches.cn: 心里的仓库：被定位并带入意识的条目，有时就卡在「话到嘴边」。

branches.en: TWO INDEXED STORES: documents ranked for a query, and records fetched by a key.
branches.cn: 两种带索引的仓库：为查询排序的文献，与按键值取回的记录。

branches.en: THE BROKEN DISK: files recovered after deletion or failure.
branches.cn: 损坏的磁盘：在删除或故障之后被恢复的文件。

branches.en: OUT OF THE STACKS, OUT OF DISGRACE: a book fetched by slip, and a reputation got back by years of work.
branches.cn: 出书库、出耻辱：凭条取出的书，与靠多年工作挽回的名声。

intro.en: Retrieval is a French verb of finding again, with two prefixes and a noun suffix around one root of finding.
intro.cn: retrieval 是一个表「重新找到」的法语动词的后代，围绕一个表「找到」的词根，带两个前缀与一个名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: The verb's second element, trouver, is not Latin in form; it goes back to a reconstructed Vulgar Latin verb and, by a hypothesis, to Greek tropos. Latin re- supplies the prefix.
latinIntro.cn: 这个动词的第二个成分 trouver 在形式上不属拉丁语；它上溯一个重构的俗拉丁动词，并按一种假说上溯希腊 tropos。拉丁语只提供了表「再次」的前缀。

items.example: The prefix adds the second attempt.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀加上「第二次」。

items.example: The verb named the finding, not the search.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指「找到」，而非「寻找」。

items.example: The compound named recovering what had been lost.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词指把失去之物找回来。

items.example: The dog retrieved the stick from the pond.
items.exampleCN: 狗从池塘里把木棍捡回来。

items.example: Retrieval from the archive needs a pass.
items.exampleCN: 从档案馆取件需要通行证。

items.example: The deleted mail is still retrievable.
items.exampleCN: 已删除的邮件仍可取回。

items.example: The retriever waited at the water's edge.
items.exampleCN: 寻回犬在水边等着。

items.example: The loss was irretrievable.
items.exampleCN: 这次损失无法挽回。

definition_zh: 取回过程；检索过程；提取过程
definition_en: the sequence of steps by which something stored is located and brought back
core_image: 柜台后的人接过一张索书条，先查目录，再走向书库深处的某一格，最后把书放到台面上；每一格动作都留下一个时间点。
scene: 图书馆的柜台后，馆员接过索书条，先查目录，再走向书库深处的一格，最后把书放到台面上，每个动作都记下了时间。The retrieval process took eleven minutes from slip to counter.
sceneCN: 这里指从提出请求到把书交到手上的整套步骤（第 4 个义项：实物取件的流程）；句意为从递条到交到柜台，取件过程用了十一分钟。

pos.zh: 取回过程；检索过程；提取过程（可数，指一套步骤）

collocations.phrase: the retrieval process of a database
each step in the retrieval process

derivatives.zh: 取回；检索（古法语 retrouver「重新找到」，由「再次」加「找到」构成，由「找回」转指「取回」）
取回；检索（在动词后加名词词尾，由动作转指该行为本身）
寻回犬；取回者（加表施事者的词尾，由「找回」转指「替人捡回者」）
过程；加工（拉丁 processus「向前行进」，由「行进」转指「有阶段的历程」，再转指「按步骤处理」）

senses.title: The steps that bring a memory out
senses.titleCN: 把记忆提出来的一组步骤
senses.definition: the sequence by which a stored memory is located, checked and brought into awareness
senses.definitionCN: 把已存记忆定位、核对并带入意识的一系列步骤
senses.example: The memory retrieval process begins with a cue and ends with an answer.
senses.exampleCN: 记忆提取过程以线索开始，以答案结束。
senses.why: Memory is treated as a store, so bringing an item out has to be described as a sequence of steps.
senses.whyCN: 记忆被当作仓库，因此把条目取出必须描述为一串步骤。

senses.title: The steps that find documents
senses.definition: the sequence by which a query is matched against a collection and results are returned
senses.definitionCN: 把查询与文献集合匹配并返回结果的一系列步骤
senses.example: The information retrieval process ranks documents before the user sees them.
senses.exampleCN: 信息检索过程在用户看到之前先给文献排序。
senses.why: A query must be matched, scored and returned, and the word process names that ordered run.
senses.whyCN: 查询必须被匹配、打分并返回，过程一词命名这条有序流程。

senses.title: The steps inside a database
senses.definition: the sequence by which a key is hashed, an index is walked and a record is returned
senses.definitionCN: 按键值散列、走索引、返回记录的一系列步骤
senses.example: Indexing cut the retrieval process from seconds to milliseconds.
senses.exampleCN: 建索引把取回过程从几秒缩到几毫秒。
senses.why: An index turns a key into a location, and the sequence from key to record is the process.
senses.whyCN: 索引把键值变成位置，从键值到记录的这一串就是过程。

senses.title: The steps of fetching a physical item
senses.definition: the sequence from a request slip to the item being placed in the requester's hands
senses.definitionCN: 从递出索书条到物件交到请求者手上的一系列步骤
senses.example: The retrieval process took eleven minutes from slip to counter.
senses.exampleCN: 从递条到交到柜台，取件过程用了十一分钟。
senses.why: A slip, a shelf and a counter are three stages, and the noun process makes the stages explicit.
senses.whyCN: 索书条、书架与柜台是三个阶段，过程一词把这些阶段说出来。

senses.title: The steps of recovering lost data
senses.titleCN: 恢复丢失数据的一组步骤
senses.definition: the sequence by which deleted or damaged files are located and rebuilt
senses.definitionCN: 把已删除或损坏的文件定位并重建的一系列步骤
senses.example: The recovery team documented the retrieval process step by step.
senses.exampleCN: 恢复小组逐步记录了取回过程。
senses.why: Recovery is not one act but a chain, from scanning the medium to rebuilding the file.
senses.whyCN: 恢复不是一个动作，而是一条链，从扫描介质到重建文件。

senses.title: The steps that rank results
senses.titleCN: 给结果排序的一组步骤
senses.definition: the sequence by which a search system scores and orders what it found
senses.definitionCN: 搜索系统给命中项打分并排序的一系列步骤
senses.example: The retrieval process weights recency more than length.
senses.exampleCN: 该取回过程给新近程度的权重高于篇幅。
senses.why: Ranking happens after matching, so the run has an order that can be described and tuned.
senses.whyCN: 排序发生在匹配之后，因此这条流程有可描述、可调优的次序。

senses.title: Cue, search, output
senses.definition: the cognitive sequence of receiving a cue, searching the store and producing an answer
senses.definitionCN: 收到线索、搜索存储、产出答案的认知序列
senses.example: A breakdown in the retrieval process explains the tip-of-the-tongue state.
senses.exampleCN: 取回过程中的中断解释了「话到嘴边」的状态。
senses.why: A cue, a search and an answer are the three moments psychology separates inside one act.
senses.whyCN: 线索、搜索与答案是心理学在同一次动作里分出的三个时刻。

senses.title: The steps that restore meaning
senses.titleCN: 使意义复原的一组步骤
senses.definition: the sequence by which an obscured meaning is recovered from context, archive or memory
senses.definitionCN: 从语境、档案或记忆中把被遮蔽的意义复原的一系列步骤
senses.example: The scholar described the retrieval process behind a corrupt line.
senses.exampleCN: 这位学者描述了一行讹文背后的意义复原过程。
senses.why: Restoring a meaning takes several moves, from locating the passage to testing a reading.
senses.whyCN: 复原意义要走几步，从定位段落，到检验一种读法。

intro.en: Retrieval process joins the noun retrieval, from Old French retrouver 'to find again', with process, from Latin processus 'a going forward'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: retrieval process 把名词 retrieval 与 process 接在一起：前者出自古法语 retrouver「重新找到」，后者出自拉丁 processus「向前行进」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Trouver meant 'to find'; it goes back to a reconstructed Vulgar Latin verb meaning 'to find, contrive', usually traced to Greek tropos 'a turn' by a hypothesis.
items.cn: trouver 意为「找到」；它上溯一个重构的俗拉丁动词，意为「找到、设法」，通常按一种假说追溯到希腊 tropos「转向」。

items.en: Re- 'again' plus trouver gave retrouver 'to find again, recover', which English took as retrieve.
items.cn: 表「再次」的前缀加 trouver 构成 retrouver「重新找到、找回」，英语借入为 retrieve。

items.en: Processus came from procedere, pro- 'forward' plus cedere 'to go'; the deeper root of cedere is a reconstruction.
items.cn: processus 出自 procedere，即表「向前」的前缀加 cedere「走」；cedere 的更早词根属重构形式。

items.en: Retrieval is an English noun built on the verb with a suffix of action, and process entered English from Latin in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: retrieval 是在英语动词上加表动作的词尾构成的名词；process 在十四世纪由拉丁语进入英语。

items.en: The compound became common with information science and cognitive psychology, where a procedure had to be described step by step.
items.cn: 这个词组随信息科学与认知心理学而通行，因为那里的程序必须逐步描述。

items.en: Source uncertain (first citation and deeper origin): no exact first citation is recorded for the compound, the Vulgar Latin verb behind trouver is a reconstruction, and cedere's deeper root is also reconstructed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：这个词组没有确切的最早书证；trouver 背后的俗拉丁动词属重构形式，cedere 的更早词根同样属重构。

note.en: Group one holds forms of the same verb of finding again; group two holds near neighbours for the steps of getting something back.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「重新找到」动词的词形；第二组是表示「取回步骤」的近义说法。

entries.definition: Names the act of getting something back; adding process turns the act into an ordered sequence that can be timed.
entries.definitionCN: 指取回的行为；加上过程一词后，这个行为变成可计时的有序序列。

entries.definition: The verb for getting something back; the compound never uses it as a verb and always names the procedure.
entries.definitionCN: 指取回的动词；这个词组从不把它当动词用，始终指那套程序。

entries.definition: A dog or a person that fetches; it is the doer of the act, not the act's stages.
entries.definitionCN: 指捡回东西的犬或人；是动作的施事者，而非动作的各阶段。

entries.definition: From a Latin verb of drawing back; the sound overlaps but the root is not the one that gives retrieval.
entries.definitionCN: 出自一个表「后撤」的拉丁动词；读音部分重叠，但词根并非给出 retrieval 的那一个。

entries.definition: The activity of looking for something; retrieval adds that the thing is found and brought back.
entries.definitionCN: 指寻找某物的活动；retrieval 还加上「找到并带回」这一层。

entries.definition: A single act of checking a table or an index, usually fast; it is one step inside a retrieval process.
entries.definitionCN: 指查表或查索引的一次动作，通常很快；它是取回过程中的一步。

entries.definition: The sequence by which something is brought back to a working state, as after a crash; retrieval returns an item, recovery restores a condition.
entries.definitionCN: 指把某物恢复到可用状态的一系列步骤，如崩溃之后；取回是拿回一个物件，恢复是复原一种状态。

entries.definition: The request put to a system; it is the input that sets the retrieval process going.
entries.definitionCN: 指向系统提出的请求；是启动取回过程的输入。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The first half means finding again, the second half means a course of stages: a finding-again run step by step.
normal.cn: 前半是「再找到」，后半是「有阶段的历程」：一次分成步骤的「再找到」。

normal.en: The family runs retrieve, retrieval, retriever and irretrievable, all from one French verb of finding.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 retrieve、retrieval、retriever、irretrievable，全出同一个表「找到」的法语动词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the stores: the memory retrieval process, the information retrieval process, the retrieval process of a database.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各类仓库：记忆提取过程、信息检索过程、数据库的取回过程。

normal.en: The head noun is process, so the phrase always implies stages, a beginning and an end that can be timed.
normal.cn: 中心词是「过程」，因此这个词组始终含「有阶段、可计时、有始有终」之意。

normal.en: Every use names the whole run, never one step: a lookup is a step, not a process.
normal.cn: 每一处用法都指整段流程，而非某一步：查表是一步，不是过程。

abstract.en: Picture a slip handed over a counter and a book arriving at that counter eleven minutes later.
abstract.cn: 想象一张索书条递过柜台，十一分钟后书回到同一张柜台。

abstract.en: Picture a key turned in a locked drawer, the drawer sliding out, the paper already inside.
abstract.cn: 想象钥匙转动，抽屉滑出，纸已在里面。

abstract.en: Picture a word on the tip of the tongue: the search runs, the answer does not arrive.
abstract.cn: 想象话到嘴边的一个词：搜索在跑，答案就是不来。

examples.en: The retrieval process starts with a cue and ends with a report.
examples.cn: 取回过程以线索开始，以报告结束。

examples.en: Compressing the index shortened the retrieval process by half.
examples.cn: 压缩索引把取回过程缩短了一半。

examples.en: A failure at any step in the retrieval process can produce a wrong answer with full confidence.
examples.cn: 取回过程中任何一步失灵，都可能产出一个自信却错误的答案。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「再找到」+「有阶段的历程」——把「找回来」拆成一条流水线：线索进去，条目出来。

root: retrieval：古法语 retrouver「重新找到」= 表「再次」的前缀 + trouver「找到」，trouver 上溯重构的俗拉丁动词，并据假说追溯到希腊 tropos；process：拉丁 processus「向前行进」= 表「向前」的前缀 + cedere「走」，cedere 更深词根属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one run: a request goes in and an item comes out. The run may be through memory, through a document collection, through a database index, through a closed stack, through a broken disk, through a ranking engine, through a cue-and-search loop in the mind, or through a corrupt text on the way to its meaning.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一条流程展开：请求进去，物件出来。这条流程可以走记忆，走文献集合，走数据库索引，走闭架书库，走损坏的磁盘，走排序引擎，走心里「线索—搜索」的回路，也可以走一段讹文以抵达其意义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a slip handed across a counter and a book arriving at that counter minutes later, every move time-stamped.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张索书条递过柜台，几分钟后书回到同一张柜台，每个动作都记着时间。

branches.en: THE MIND'S RUN AND ITS BREAK: a cue that finds an answer, and the same run stalling at the tip of the tongue.
branches.cn: 心里的流程与它的中断：找到答案的线索，与卡在「话到嘴边」的同一条流程。

branches.en: DOCUMENTS AND ORDER: matching a query against a collection, then scoring what came back.
branches.cn: 文献与次序：把查询与集合匹配，再给回来的结果打分。

branches.en: THE INDEX WALK: a key, an index and a record, measured in milliseconds.
branches.cn: 走索引：键值、索引与记录，以毫秒计。

branches.en: THE COUNTER AND THE STACKS: a slip, a shelf and a book placed on the counter.
branches.cn: 柜台与书库：索书条、书架，与放上柜台的书。

branches.en: REBUILDING WHAT WAS LOST: files recovered from a broken disk, and meaning recovered from a corrupt line.
branches.cn: 重建失去之物：从坏盘恢复的文件，与从讹文复原的意义。

intro.en: The phrase joins a noun of getting back to a noun of going forward, so both halves are readable as morphemes.
intro.cn: 这个词组把「取回」的名词与「向前行进」的名词接在一起，两半都可按语素读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin re- and the reconstructed Vulgar Latin ancestor of trouver stand behind retrieval; Latin procedere and cedere stand behind process.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁前缀 re- 与 trouver 那个重构的俗拉丁祖先构成 retrieval 的背景；拉丁 procedere 与 cedere 构成 process 的背景。

items.example: The prefix marks the second finding.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标记「第二次找到」。

items.example: The verb names the result, not the effort.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指结果，而非费力。

items.example: Retrouver is the source of the English verb.
items.exampleCN: retrouver 是英语动词的来源。

items.example: Retrieval is timed from request to answer.
items.exampleCN: 取回从请求到答案计时。

items.example: The verb described movement through stages.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词描述穿过各阶段的行进。

items.example: Processus named the run before it named the method.
items.exampleCN: processus 先指行进，后指方法。

items.example: The process has a start and an end.
items.exampleCN: 这个过程有起点与终点。

items.meaning: the handling of material step by step
items.example: Processing the query takes four steps.
items.exampleCN: 处理这条查询要四步。

definition_en: the focusing of the mind on something, or the notice and care given to it
core_image: 一束灯从舞台顶部落下，只照亮台中央的一小块，其余都在暗处；台上的人却只觉得那一小块就是全部世界。
scene: 剧场里一束灯从舞台顶部落下，只照亮台中央的一小块，其余都沉在暗处，台下的人却只觉得那一小块就是全部世界。Her attention narrowed to the single lit circle.
sceneCN: 这里指意识集中到某一点上（第 1 个义项：注意的集中）；句意为她的注意力收窄到那一小圈亮处。

pos.zh: 注意；注意力；关注；照料（多不可数，作「关注」时可加不定冠词）

derivatives.zh: 出席；注意（拉丁 attendere「朝……伸展」，由「把心伸向」转指「留意」与「到场」）
专注的；殷勤的（加拉丁形容词词尾，由「注意」转指「正在注意的」）
专注地（加副词词尾，由形容词转指动作方式）
专注；殷勤（加表性质的名词词尾，由形容词转指该性质）
不注意；疏忽（加表否定的前缀，由「注意」转指「未加注意」）

senses.title: The mind fixed on one thing
senses.definition: the state in which mental effort is concentrated on a single object or task
senses.definitionCN: 心智努力集中于某一对象或任务的状态
senses.example: Her attention narrowed to the single lit circle.
senses.exampleCN: 她的注意力收窄到那一小圈亮处。
senses.why: The verb behind the noun means 'to stretch toward', so attention is the mind reaching out and holding on.
senses.whyCN: 名词背后的动词意为「朝……伸展」，所以注意就是心向外伸出并抓住不放。

senses.title: The measurable capacity
senses.definition: in psychology, the limited capacity to select and hold stimuli, often measured in tests
senses.definitionCN: 心理学指选择并保持刺激的有限能力，常在实验中被测量
senses.example: The dual-task test measures how attention divides between two streams.
senses.exampleCN: 双任务测验测量注意力如何在两路信息之间分配。
senses.why: Experimental work turned the everyday state into a quantity with a span and a limit.
senses.whyCN: 实验工作把日常状态变成一个带广度与上限的量。

senses.title: Care given to a need
senses.definition: the practical care shown to a person or a need, as in attending to a wound
senses.definitionCN: 对人及其需要的实际照料，如处理伤口
senses.example: The child needed attention that the ward could not give.
senses.exampleCN: 这孩子需要的照护，那个病房给不了。
senses.why: The verb also means to look after someone, so the noun carries practical care as well as mental notice.
senses.whyCN: 动词另有「照料」义，名词因此兼有实际的护理，而不只是心里的留意。

senses.title: Notice from other people
senses.definition: the interest or notice that a person or thing receives from others
senses.definitionCN: 某人或某物从他人那里得到的兴趣与注目
senses.example: The mural drew attention from every passer-by.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅壁画引来每个路人的注目。
senses.why: The same word covers giving and receiving: one pays attention, and a thing attracts it.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词也能指流向某人的东西，而不只是某人向外投出的注意。

senses.title: The military stance
senses.definition: the stiff upright position of a soldier awaiting an order
senses.definitionCN: 士兵等待命令时挺直的站姿
senses.example: The squad stood at attention while the flag was raised.
senses.exampleCN: 升旗时全队列立正。
senses.why: A soldier standing ready is literally held at attention, so the abstract noun freezes into a command.
senses.whyCN: 士兵挺立待命，字面上就是「被保持在注意状态」，抽象名词遂凝固为口令。

senses.title: Formal notice to a person
senses.definition: the directing of a document or a request to a particular person for action
senses.definitionCN: 把文件或请求交由某人处理
senses.example: Send the file to the attention of the registrar.
senses.exampleCN: 把这份文件交由登记主管处理。
senses.why: Bureaucratic use treats attention as a channel: the paper goes where the mind is asked to go.
senses.whyCN: 把文件递交某人，重复了拉丁动词「转向」的动作，只是改在书面上。

senses.title: Medical care
senses.definition: treatment given by a medical service, as in needing medical attention
senses.definitionCN: 由医疗服务给予的处理，如需要医疗照护
senses.example: Two passengers required medical attention at the scene.
senses.exampleCN: 两名乘客在现场需要医疗处理。
senses.why: Medical use keeps the older sense of tending: the attention is what is done for the patient, not what the patient gives.
senses.whyCN: 医学用法保留较早的「照料」义：注意是替病人做的事，不是病人给出的注意。

senses.title: A weighting scheme in a model
senses.titleCN: 模型中给输入分配的权重
senses.definition: in computing, the mechanism by which a model weights parts of its input
senses.definitionCN: 计算领域指模型对输入各部分赋权的机制
senses.example: The attention layer learned to weight the verb more than the article.
senses.exampleCN: 注意力层学会给动词比冠词更高的权重。
senses.why: The machine sense is a metaphor made technical: the model decides where to look, and how hard.
senses.whyCN: 机器义是把比喻技术化：模型决定看向哪里，以及看得多重。

senses.title: A scarce resource
senses.definition: the limited human capacity treated as something that can be bought, sold and competed for
senses.definitionCN: 把有限的人力关注当作可买卖、可争夺之物
senses.example: Advertising competes for the same pool of attention.
senses.exampleCN: 广告争夺的是同一池注意力。
senses.why: When capacity is scarce, it becomes a market, and the noun starts to name a commodity.
senses.whyCN: 经济学把留意当作有限的货物，于是这个名词可以被耗费、购买与争夺。

intro.en: Attention comes from Latin attentio, from attendere 'to stretch toward, give heed', built on ad- 'to' plus tendere 'to stretch'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: attention 出自拉丁 attentio，来自 attendere「朝……伸展、留意」，由表「朝向」的前缀加 tendere「伸展」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Tendere meant 'to stretch, extend'. Its deeper root is reconstructed as a form meaning 'to stretch', and that form is a reconstruction rather than a recorded word.
items.cn: tendere 意为「伸展、拉长」。其更早词根被重构为一个意为「伸展」的形式，那只是重构形式，并非有记录的词。

items.en: Ad- 'to, toward' plus tendere gave attendere 'to stretch toward', hence to give heed to or to wait upon. The physical image is a mind reaching out.
items.cn: 表「朝向」的前缀加 tendere 构成 attendere「朝……伸展」，因此指留意或侍奉。其形象是心向外伸出。

items.en: Attentio named the act of heeding, and it is the direct source of the English noun.
items.cn: attentio 指留意的行为，是英语名词的直接来源。

items.en: The noun entered English in the fourteenth century through Old French, first in the sense of heeding or of courtesy shown to a person.
items.cn: 这个名词在十四世纪经古法语进入英语，最初指留意，或指对人所表示的殷勤。

items.en: Psychology made attention a measurable capacity in the late nineteenth century; the military stance, the medical sense and the computing mechanism are later specializations.
items.cn: 心理学在十九世纪晚期把注意变成可测量的能力；军姿义、医疗义与计算机制义都是后起的专门用法。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper origin): no exact first citation is fixed, and the pre-Latin root of tendere is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：没有确切的最早书证；tendere 在拉丁语之前的词根属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds forms of the same verb of stretching toward; group two holds nouns of focusing and noticing.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「朝……伸展」这一动词的词形；第二组是表示集中与留意之意的名词。

entries.definition: The verb for being present or for giving heed; the noun names the state that the verb produces.
entries.definitionCN: 指出席或留意的动词；名词指该动词所产生的状态。

entries.definition: Describes a person who is giving heed; it is the quality, while attention is the thing given.
entries.definitionCN: 形容正在留意的人；它是性质，而 attention 是被给出的东西。

entries.definition: The fact or number of people present; the same verb, but the sense has moved from heed to turnout.
entries.definitionCN: 指到场这一事实或到场人数；同一个动词，但词义已从「留意」移向「到场」。

entries.definition: From in- plus tendere, so it means a stretching toward a purpose; it shares the root but names a plan, not a focus.
entries.definitionCN: 由表「向内」的前缀加 tendere 构成，意为朝某个目的伸展；词根相同，却指计划而非专注。

entries.definition: The point on which effort is concentrated, or the act of concentrating it; it is often sharper and more deliberate than attention.
entries.definitionCN: 指努力集中的那一点，或使之集中的动作；常比 attention 更锐利、更有意。

entries.definition: The sustained application of mental effort to one task; attention may be brief and involuntary, concentration usually is not.
entries.definitionCN: 指把心力持续用于一项任务；attention 可以短暂且非自愿，concentration 通常不是。

entries.definition: Careful notice given to advice or a warning; it is narrower and more formal than attention.
entries.definitionCN: 指对建议或警告的留心；比 attention 更窄也更正式。

entries.definition: The act of becoming aware of something; it is the start, while attention is the holding that follows.
entries.definitionCN: 指察觉到某物的动作；它是开端，attention 是随后的持续。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: A verb of stretching toward plus a noun of action: the mind reaches out and stays there.
normal.cn: 表「朝……伸展」的动词加动作名词：心伸出去，并且停在那里。

normal.en: The family runs attend, attentive, attentively, attentiveness and inattention.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 attend、attentive、attentively、attentiveness、inattention。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: pay attention to, attract attention, medical attention, stand at attention.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义：注意某事、引起注意、医疗照护、立正。

normal.en: Psychology supplies the measurements: attention span, divided attention, selective attention.
normal.cn: 心理学提供测量语：注意广度、分配性注意、选择性注意。

normal.en: The computing sense keeps the metaphor visible: a model decides where to look and how hard.
normal.cn: 计算义让比喻保持可见：模型决定看向哪里、看得多重。

abstract.en: Picture a single spotlight on a stage while the rest of the house goes dark.
abstract.cn: 想象舞台上一束唯一的追光，观众席其余部分陷入黑暗。

abstract.en: Picture a hand stretched toward a shelf and holding one book while the others stay put.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手伸向书架，只拿住一本书，其余都不动。

abstract.en: Picture a queue of advertisements all bidding for the same pair of eyes.
abstract.cn: 想象一队广告都在竞价争抢同一双眼睛。

examples.en: The problem held his attention for the whole afternoon.
examples.cn: 这个问题抓住了他整个下午的注意力。

examples.en: Send the report to the attention of the finance director.
examples.cn: 把这份报告交由财务主管处理。

examples.en: The injured walker needed medical attention before nightfall.
examples.cn: 受伤的徒步者在入夜前需要医疗处理。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「朝向」+「伸展」——心朝某处伸出去并停住，就是注意；伸向伤口是照护，伸向舞台是专注。

root: 拉丁 attentio，来自 attendere「朝……伸展、留意」= 表「朝向」的前缀 + tendere「伸展」；tendere 在拉丁语之前的词根属重构形式。英语 attention 经古法语。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one gesture: the mind stretches toward something and holds. Holding one object is focus; holding it under test is a measured capacity; holding a person's need is care; being held by others is notice; holding the body still is the military stance; directing a paper is formal notice; directing a wound is treatment; directing a model is a weighting; and the whole capacity, once scarce, becomes a market.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿同一个动作展开：心朝某处伸出并停住。停在一个对象上是专注；在测验中停住是可测的能力；停在人的需要上是照护；被别人停住是受人注目；把身体停直是军姿；把文件指向某人是正式知会；把处理指向伤口是医疗；把权重指向输入是模型机制；而当这种能力稀缺，它就成了市场。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one spotlight on a stage, the rest of the house dark, and a mind that treats the lit circle as the whole world.
core.cn: 核心意象：舞台上的一束追光，观众席其余皆暗，而一颗心把那一圈亮处当成整个世界。

branches.en: THE STATE AND ITS MEASURE: focus as lived, and focus as a span with a limit.
branches.cn: 状态与它的度量：被体验到的专注，与带广度与上限的专注。

branches.en: CARE IN TWO SETTINGS: attention to a person's need, and attention given by a medical service.
branches.cn: 两种场合的照护：对人的需要的照料，与由医疗服务给出的处理。

branches.en: NOTICE AS A PRIZE: being looked at, and looking as a scarce thing to be bought.
branches.cn: 作为奖赏的注目：被人看见，以及把「看见」当作可购买的稀缺物。

branches.en: THE BODY HELD STILL: the same holding, applied to posture and command.
branches.cn: 把身体停住：同一种「停住」，用在姿态与命令上。

branches.en: DIRECTING WHERE THE MIND GOES: a paper sent to a person, and a model weighting its input.
branches.cn: 指引心思的去处：交给某人的文件，与给输入赋权的模型。

intro.en: Attention is a Latin verb of stretching toward, with a prefix of direction and a suffix of action.
intro.cn: attention 是一个表「朝……伸展」的拉丁动词的后代，带表方向的前缀与表动作的后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin tendere gives tension, tense and extend; ad- plus tendere gives attend, attention and attentive.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 tendere 衍生 tension、tense、extend；表「朝向」的前缀加 tendere 衍生 attend、attention、attentive。

items.example: The verb supplied the image of a reaching mind.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供了「心向外伸」的形象。

items.example: The compound turned direction into heed.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词把方向变成留意。

items.example: The noun named the state of reaching out.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指「伸出并停住」的状态。

items.example: She attends the clinic on Mondays.
items.exampleCN: 她每周一到诊所。

items.example: Attention drifted during the third hour.
items.exampleCN: 到第三个小时，注意力开始飘走。

items.example: The audience was unusually attentive.
items.exampleCN: 听众异常专注。

items.example: He listened attentively to the objections.
items.exampleCN: 他专注地听完反对意见。

items.example: Inattention caused the misprint.
items.exampleCN: 疏忽造成了这处误印。

definition_en: giving close heed to someone or something, and quick to notice what they need
core_image: 一张矮桌旁，主人不声不响地把客人面前的杯子续满，又把窗缝关上，客人还没觉得冷。
scene: 矮桌旁，主人不声不响地把客人面前的杯子续满，又起身把窗缝合上，客人还没觉得冷。The attentive host noticed the draught before anyone mentioned it.
sceneCN: 这里指留心照料他人需要、抢先察觉的（第 2 个义项：体贴周到的）；句意为这位殷勤的主人在任何人开口之前就察觉了穿堂风。

pos.zh: 专注的；留心的；殷勤周到的

derivatives.zh: 注意；注意力（由形容词回到拉丁动作名词，指被给出的那份留意）
留意；出席（同族动词，由「朝……伸展」转指「留意」与「到场」）
专注地（加副词词尾，由形容词转指动作方式）
专注；殷勤（加表性质的名词词尾，由形容词转指该性质）
不注意的；漫不经心的（加表否定的前缀，由「专注」转指「缺乏专注」）

senses.title: Listening or watching closely
senses.definition: paying close heed to what is being said, shown or performed
senses.definitionCN: 对正在说出、展示或表演的内容保持密切留意
senses.example: The audience was attentive through the whole second act.
senses.exampleCN: 整个第二幕，观众都很专注。
senses.why: The core of the word is the mind stretched toward an object, so the first sense is simply that stretch maintained.
senses.whyCN: 形容词把留意说成持续的状态，于是听与看成了守着的姿态。

senses.title: Considerate of others' needs
senses.definition: quick to notice and serve what another person wants or lacks
senses.definitionCN: 敏锐察觉并照料他人所缺所需的
senses.example: The attentive host noticed the draught before anyone mentioned it.
senses.exampleCN: 这位殷勤的主人在任何人开口之前就察觉了穿堂风。
senses.why: The same heed is turned on a person rather than a task, and the result is described as courtesy.
senses.whyCN: 把「转向」用在他人所需上，同一种姿态便由留意变成服侍。

senses.title: Careful about detail
senses.definition: taking care over small points that others might pass over
senses.definitionCN: 对他人可能略过的小处也认真处理
senses.example: The proofreader was attentive to every comma.
senses.exampleCN: 这位校对者对每个逗号都很留心。
senses.why: Small points are what heed catches first, so the adjective extends from people to details.
senses.whyCN: 小处正是留意最先捕捉的东西，形容词便由人延伸到细节。

senses.title: Alert to danger
senses.definition: watchful for a threat that may appear without warning
senses.definitionCN: 对可能毫无预警出现的威胁保持警戒
senses.example: The lookout stayed attentive to the horizon.
senses.exampleCN: 瞭望者一直留意着海平线。
senses.why: Watchfulness for a threat is the same reaching out, with the object changed from a task to a risk.
senses.whyCN: 警戒是把留意对准未来的威胁，姿态相同，对象换成危险。

senses.title: High in attentiveness as a trait
senses.definition: in psychology, describing a person whose default level of heed is high across situations
senses.definitionCN: 心理学指在各种情境下留意水平都偏高的人
senses.example: Attentive children in the study also slept more regularly.
senses.exampleCN: 研究中的专注儿童睡眠也更规律。
senses.why: Psychology moves the word from an act to a disposition, so it can be measured across time.
senses.whyCN: 心理学把形容词变成可测量的特质，一时之举便成了稳定水平。

senses.title: Assiduous in duty
senses.definition: formal use for steady diligence in service, office or ritual
senses.definitionCN: 正式用法中指在服务、职务或礼仪上持续勤谨
senses.example: The attendant was attentive to every rule of the ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 这位侍从对仪式的每一条规矩都谨守不怠。
senses.why: Formal service is heed sustained over time, which is why the word appears in oaths and rituals.
senses.whyCN: 正式的职务是把留意拉长成时间，所以这个词出现在誓言与礼仪里。

senses.title: Heeding advice
senses.definition: giving serious heed to advice, warning or instruction
senses.definitionCN: 对劝告、警告或指示给予认真留意
senses.example: She was attentive to her tutor's corrections.
senses.exampleCN: 她对导师的指正很留心。
senses.why: Advice is heard before it is followed, so heeding words is the same act as watching a scene.
senses.whyCN: 劝告先被听见才被遵从，所以听进话与看住场面是同一个动作。

senses.title: Responsive service
senses.definition: describing service that answers a need promptly and without being asked
senses.definitionCN: 形容无需索求便及时回应需要的服务
senses.example: The hotel is known for attentive service rather than for size.
senses.exampleCN: 这家旅馆出名的是殷勤的照应，而非规模。
senses.why: The word can be applied to an organization, where the heed is a policy rather than a mood.
senses.whyCN: 未经索求便回应的服务，是把留意向外变成行动。

intro.en: Attentive is Medieval Latin attentivus, from attendere 'to stretch toward, heed', plus the adjective suffix -ive. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: attentive 出自中世纪拉丁 attentivus，来自 attendere「朝……伸展、留意」，加形容词词尾构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Tendere meant 'to stretch'. Its deeper root is reconstructed as a form meaning 'to stretch', and that form is a reconstruction.
items.cn: tendere 意为「伸展」。其更早词根被重构为一个意为「伸展」的形式，属重构形式。

items.en: Ad- 'toward' plus tendere gave attendere 'to stretch toward', hence to heed or to wait upon.
items.cn: 表「朝向」的前缀加 tendere 构成 attendere「朝……伸展」，因此指留意或侍奉。

items.en: Medieval Latin formed attentivus 'giving heed', adding the adjective suffix of tendency to the verb's participle stem.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁构成 attentivus「留意的」，在动词分词词干上加表倾向的形容词词尾。

items.en: The adjective entered English in the fifteenth century, first describing a person given to heeding, then a person courteous in service.
items.cn: 这个形容词在十五世纪进入英语，先形容惯于留意的人，再形容在服侍上殷勤的人。

items.en: Psychology and service writing gave the word its current range, from a measurable trait to the quality of a hotel's staff.
items.cn: 心理学与服务行业的写作给出它今天的范围：从一个可测量的特质，到旅馆员工的水准。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper origin): no exact first citation is fixed, and the pre-Latin root of tendere is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：没有确切的最早书证；tendere 在拉丁语之前的词根属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds forms of the same verb of stretching toward; group two holds adjectives of watchfulness and courtesy.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「朝……伸展」这一动词的词形；第二组是表示警觉与殷勤的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun for the heed itself; the adjective describes the one who gives it.
entries.definitionCN: 指所给出的留意本身；形容词描述给出它的人。

entries.definition: The verb for heeding or being present; the adjective is the resulting quality of a person.
entries.definitionCN: 指留意或出席的动词；形容词是人由此呈现的性质。

entries.definition: The noun for the quality of being attentive; it names what the adjective describes.
entries.definitionCN: 指「专注、殷勤」这一性质的名词；它命名形容词所描述者。

entries.definition: Describes a person who fails to heed; it is the direct opposite and is common in school reports.
entries.definitionCN: 形容未能留意的人；是直接的反义，常用于学校评语。

entries.definition: Quick to notice what is there, especially details others miss; it stresses perception rather than service.
entries.definitionCN: 指敏锐察觉眼前之物，尤其是他人忽略的细节；强调知觉，而非服侍。

entries.definition: Careful not to inconvenience others; it stresses avoiding harm, while attentive stresses noticing needs.
entries.definitionCN: 指小心不使他人不便；强调避免造成困扰，而 attentive 强调察觉需要。

entries.definition: Watchful and ready to react, usually to a risk; it is sharper and more defensive than attentive.
entries.definitionCN: 指警觉并准备反应，通常针对风险；比 attentive 更锐利、更偏防备。

entries.definition: Persistently careful in work; it concerns sustained effort rather than the direction of heed.
entries.definitionCN: 指在工作中持续用心；关心的是持久的努力，而非留意所向。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: A verb of stretching toward plus a suffix of tendency: a person inclined to reach out and hold.
normal.cn: 表「朝……伸展」的动词加表倾向的词尾：一个倾向于伸出去并停住的人。

normal.en: The family runs attend, attention, attentively and inattentive, all from one Latin verb.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 attend、attention、attentively、inattentive，全出同一个拉丁动词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the two directions: attentive to detail, attentive to someone's needs.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出两个方向：注重细节、留意某人的需要。

normal.en: A host and a lookout share the word: one watches for comfort, the other for danger.
normal.cn: 主人与瞭望者共用这个词：一个留意舒适，一个留意危险。

normal.en: Service writing uses the adjective for staff, where heed becomes policy rather than mood.
normal.cn: 服务行业的文字用它形容员工，此处的留意成了制度，而非心情。

abstract.en: Picture a cup refilled before the guest notices it is empty.
abstract.cn: 想象杯子在客人察觉空之前就被续满。

abstract.en: Picture a hand closing a window before anyone feels the draught.
abstract.cn: 想象在任何人觉得有风之前，一只手已把窗关上。

abstract.en: Picture a lookout who keeps the horizon in view while others talk below.
abstract.cn: 想象瞭望者一直看着海平线，而其他人在下面说话。

examples.en: An attentive reader notices what the paragraph does not say.
examples.cn: 专注的读者会注意到段落没有说出的部分。

examples.en: The staff were attentive without being intrusive.
examples.cn: 员工殷勤而不打扰。

examples.en: He remained attentive to every objection during the hearing.
examples.cn: 听证过程中他对每个反对意见都保持留意。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「朝……伸展」+ 表倾向的词尾——心常常伸出去的人：对事是专注，对人是殷勤。

root: 中世纪拉丁 attentivus，来自 attendere「朝……伸展、留意」= 表「朝向」的前缀 + tendere「伸展」；tendere 在拉丁语之前的词根属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one disposition: heed that reaches out and stays. Staying on a performance is close listening; staying on a person is courtesy; staying on small points is care over detail; staying on a horizon is vigilance; staying on everything is a trait; staying on a duty is assiduity; staying on advice is obedience to correction; and staying on a guest is service.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种倾向展开：伸出去并停住的留意。停在演出上是专注倾听；停在人身上是殷勤；停在小处是注重细节；停在海平线上是警觉；停在一切之上是稳定特质；停在职守上是勤谨；停在劝告上是听从指正；停在客人身上是照应。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cup refilled before the guest notices, and a window closed before anyone feels the draught.
core.cn: 核心意象：杯子在客人察觉之前被续满，窗在任何人觉得有风之前被关上。

branches.en: THE HELD ATTENTION: close listening, and the same care spent on commas.
branches.cn: 被持住的注意：专注地听，与把同样的用心花在逗号上。

branches.en: COURTESY IN PERSON AND IN SERVICE: a host who notices, and a staff trained to notice.
branches.cn: 人身上的与制度里的殷勤：会察觉的主人，与被训练去察觉的员工。

branches.en: THE WATCH ON THE HORIZON: heed turned toward a risk that may come without warning.
branches.cn: 盯住海平线：留意转向可能毫无预警到来的风险。

branches.en: DUTY AND CORRECTION: steady diligence in office, and serious heed to advice.
branches.cn: 职守与指正：在职务上持续勤谨，与对劝告的认真留意。

branches.en: THE TRAIT BEHIND ALL OF THEM: a default level of heed that holds across situations.
branches.cn: 所有义项背后的特质：在各种情境下都偏高的留意水平。

intro.en: The adjective is one Latin verb of stretching with a prefix of direction and a suffix of tendency.
intro.cn: 这个形容词由一个表「伸展」的拉丁动词、一个表方向的前缀与一个表倾向的后缀组成。

latinIntro.en: Latin attendere and its participle give attend, attention and attentive; the suffix -ivus gives the tendency adjectives.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 attendere 及其分词衍生 attend、attention、attentive；后缀 -ivus 构成表倾向的形容词。

items.example: The verb gave the family its image of reaching.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词给整个词族「伸出」的形象。

items.example: The compound made direction into heed.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词把方向变成留意。

items.example: Medieval Latin formed the adjective on the participle stem.
items.exampleCN: 中世纪拉丁在分词词干上构成这个形容词。

items.example: He attends to the smallest change.
items.exampleCN: 他留意最细微的变化。

items.example: She was attentive to the visitor's comfort.
items.exampleCN: 她留意客人的舒适。

items.example: They listened attentively.
items.exampleCN: 他们专注地听。

items.example: Attentiveness is part of the job.
items.exampleCN: 殷勤是这份工作的一部分。

items.example: An inattentive driver missed the sign.
items.exampleCN: 一个不留神的司机错过了标牌。

definition_zh: 分心；使人分心之物；消遣；心烦意乱
definition_en: something that pulls attention away, or the state of having one's attention pulled away
core_image: 一张书桌被从中间掰开，两半朝相反方向滑走，桌上的纸页散在两边；走廊里另有一群人正举着花花绿绿的东西走过。
scene: 书桌被从中间掰成两半，朝相反方向滑走，纸页散在两边，写字的人手里还握着笔，却已不知道下一句要写什么。Every small distraction cost him a whole sentence.
sceneCN: 这里指把注意力从正在做的事上拉走的事物（第 1 个义项：使人分心之物）；句意为每一个小小的干扰都让他损失一整句话。

pos.zh: 分心；使人分心之物；消遣；心烦意乱（可数指具体干扰，不可数指状态）

derivatives.zh: 使分心；使转向（拉丁 distrahere「拉开」，由「拉开」转指「把心思拉走」）
分心的；心不在焉的（加表被动的分词词尾，由「被拉开」转指「心神被拉散」）
使人分心的（加表主动的分词词尾，由「拉开」转指「正在拉走注意」）
易分心的（加表「易于」的形容词词尾，由「被拉开」转指「容易被拉走」）

senses.title: Something that pulls attention away
senses.definition: a thing or event that draws the mind off the task in hand
senses.definitionCN: 把心思从手头任务上引开的事物或事件
senses.example: Every small distraction cost him a whole sentence.
senses.exampleCN: 每一个小小的干扰都让他损失一整句话。
senses.why: The noun names the pulling thing itself, which is why one speaks of a distraction rather than of distractedness.
senses.whyCN: 先把心思引走的是外在之物，所以名词先指「那个拉走注意的东西」。

senses.title: The state of divided attention
senses.definition: the condition of having one's heed split or drawn off, so that the task suffers
senses.definitionCN: 留意被分开或引走、以致任务受损的状态
senses.example: He worked in a state of constant distraction after the news.
senses.exampleCN: 听到那个消息后，他一直在分心的状态里工作。
senses.why: The same word covers the cause and the condition, so context alone tells whether a thing or a mind is meant.
senses.whyCN: 状态义说出拉扯的结果：留意被分开，手头的任务因此受损。

senses.title: A distractor in an experiment
senses.definition: in psychology, a stimulus deliberately included to compete with the target
senses.definitionCN: 心理学指为与目标竞争而有意加入的刺激
senses.example: The task added a coloured distractor beside each target word.
senses.exampleCN: 任务在每个目标词旁加了一个彩色干扰项。
senses.why: Laboratory design turns distraction into a controlled variable that can be subtracted.
senses.whyCN: 实验需要一个可控的干扰源，于是日常的烦扰被设计成刺激。

senses.title: An amusement
senses.definition: something that turns the mind away from worry or boredom in a pleasant way
senses.definitionCN: 以愉快的方式把心思从忧虑或无聊中引开的东西
senses.example: The concert was a welcome distraction after a week of bad news.
senses.exampleCN: 在经历一周坏消息之后，这场音乐会是一种受欢迎的消遣。
senses.why: Pleasure is the same pulling away, with the object changed from a task to a mood.
senses.whyCN: 消遣同样把心思引开，只是方向从任务换成忧虑或无聊。

senses.title: Near-madness
senses.definition: an extreme state of agitation in which the mind cannot settle
senses.definitionCN: 心神无法安定、极度烦躁的状态
senses.example: The noise drove her to distraction.
senses.exampleCN: 那噪声把她烦得几乎发狂。
senses.why: The older medical flavour survives in this phrase: being pulled apart is close to losing one's mind.
senses.whyCN: 心神被来回拉扯到无法安定，夸张用法便把它说成近乎疯狂。

senses.title: A feint that misleads
senses.definition: a movement or action designed to draw an opponent's forces away from the real point
senses.definitionCN: 为把对方力量引离真正目标而作出的行动
senses.example: The raid was a distraction while the main column crossed upstream.
senses.exampleCN: 那次突袭是佯动，主力此时从上游渡河。
senses.why: A feint works by pulling the opponent's force to the wrong place, the literal pull made tactical.
senses.whyCN: 佯动靠把对方力量拉到错误地点奏效，字面的「拉开」由此变成战术。

senses.title: A tearing apart
senses.definition: the archaic literal sense of being pulled apart or separated by force
senses.definitionCN: 被强行拉开或分离的古老字面义
senses.example: In the old text, distraction names the splitting of a whole into pieces.
senses.exampleCN: 在古老的文本里，这个词指把整体分裂成碎片。
senses.why: The physical sense is the root of all the others: whatever is distracted is first pulled in two directions.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的字面义留在解剖与力学语境里：被拉开的身体或部件。

senses.title: Fragmentation of attention
senses.definition: the abstract condition in which heed is scattered across many claims at once
senses.definitionCN: 留意同时被分散到许多诉求上的抽象状态
senses.example: The report describes the distraction of a working day cut into four-minute pieces.
senses.exampleCN: 报告描述了一个被切成四分钟一段的工作日所带来的注意力碎片化。
senses.why: Modern writing uses the noun for a collective condition, not for a single interruption.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义把「拉开」用在留意本身：一束注意被扯成许多股。

intro.en: Distraction comes from Latin distractio, from distrahere 'to pull apart', built on dis- 'apart' plus trahere 'to draw, drag'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: distraction 出自拉丁 distractio，来自 distrahere「拉开」，由表「分开」的前缀加 trahere「拉、拖」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Trahere meant 'to draw, drag, pull'. Its deeper origin is not established; any older root offered for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: trahere 意为「拉、拖、拽」。其更深来源未得到证明；凡为其给出的更早词根都是重构形式。

items.en: Dis- 'apart' plus trahere gave distrahere 'to pull apart, draw in different directions, divide'. The physical image is a body torn between two pulls.
items.cn: 表「分开」的前缀加 trahere 构成 distrahere「拉开、朝不同方向拉、分裂」。其形象是一个身体被两股力扯开。

items.en: Distractio named a pulling apart, and in later use a state of being torn in mind. It is the direct source of the English noun.
items.cn: distractio 指拉开的动作，后亦指心神被扯散的状态。它是英语名词的直接来源。

items.en: The noun entered English in the fourteenth century through French, first naming a division or a mental agitation.
items.cn: 这个名词在十四世纪经法语进入英语，最初指分裂或心神的激动。

items.en: From the eighteenth century the word covered amusement as well as disturbance, and modern psychology added the controlled distractor.
items.cn: 从十八世纪起，这个词既指打扰，也指消遣；现代心理学又增添了受控干扰项这一用法。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper origin): no exact first citation is fixed, and the pre-Latin root of trahere is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：没有确切的最早书证；trahere 在拉丁语之前的词根属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds forms of the same verb of pulling apart; group two holds nouns of interruption and of amusement.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「拉开」这一动词的词形；第二组是表示打断与消遣的名词。

entries.definition: The verb for pulling attention away; the noun names either the pulling thing or the pulled state.
entries.definitionCN: 指把注意力拉走的动词；名词指拉走之物或被拉散的状态。

entries.definition: An adjective for a person whose heed has been drawn off; it describes the result, not the cause.
entries.definitionCN: 形容留意已被引走的人；描述结果，而非原因。

entries.definition: An adjective for what pulls attention away; it is close to the first sense of the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 形容把注意力拉走之物；接近名词的第一个义项。

entries.definition: From Latin distringere 'to press apart, hamper', built on a verb of tightening, so it means hardship or pain rather than divided attention.
entries.definitionCN: 出自拉丁 distringere「压开、阻碍」，其词根意为「拉紧」，因此指困苦或痛苦，而非注意力被分散。

entries.definition: The act of breaking in on something already under way; it names the break, while distraction names the pulling of the mind.
entries.definitionCN: 指打断正在进行之事的行为；它指那次中断，而 distraction 指心思被拉走。

entries.definition: Something that turns a course or a mind aside, often deliberately; it is the planned counterpart of distraction.
entries.definitionCN: 指把路线或心思引开之物，常为有意；是 distraction 中带计划的一面对应词。

entries.definition: A breaking of calm or order, often noisy; it concerns the setting rather than the mind's focus.
entries.definitionCN: 指平静或秩序的破坏，常伴噪声；关心的是环境，而非心思的焦点。

entries.definition: The pleasure of having one's mind turned lightly away; it is the fourth sense of distraction without the guilt.
entries.definitionCN: 指心思被轻轻引开所带来的愉悦；是 distraction 第四义不带愧疚的版本。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: A prefix of apartness on a verb of pulling: to be pulled in two directions at once.
normal.cn: 表「分开」的前缀加表「拉」的动词：同时被两边拉扯。

normal.en: The family runs distract, distracted, distracting and distractible, all from one verb of pulling apart.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 distract、distracted、distracting、distractible，全出同一个表「拉开」的动词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the range: a distraction from work, constant distractions, driven to distraction.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出范围：使人从工作中分心之物、不断的干扰、被烦得发狂。

normal.en: The noun covers cause and state, which is why the same word can name a noise and a mind.
normal.cn: 这个名词兼指原因与状态，所以同一个词既能指噪声，也能指心境。

normal.en: The pleasant sense is visible in welcome distraction, where the pulling away is wanted.
normal.cn: 愉快的义项见于「受欢迎的消遣」，那里的「被引开」是求之不得的。

abstract.en: Picture a desk split down the middle and sliding apart in two directions.
abstract.cn: 想象书桌从中间裂开，朝两边滑走。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd with bright things walking past a window where someone is trying to write.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人举着花花绿绿的东西，从有人正想写字的窗前走过。

abstract.en: Picture a raid far from the river while the real crossing happens elsewhere.
abstract.cn: 想象远处一次突袭，而真正的渡河发生在别处。

examples.en: The phone on the desk was the worst distraction of the morning.
examples.cn: 桌上的手机是那天上午最糟的干扰。

examples.en: She welcomes any distraction that keeps her from checking the news.
examples.cn: 任何能让她不去刷消息的消遣，她都欢迎。

examples.en: The drill was a distraction meant to draw the defenders east.
examples.cn: 那次演练是佯动，意在把守军引向东面。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「分开」+「拉」——被两边同时拉扯：心被拉散是分心，人被拉着玩是消遣，队伍被引开是佯动。

root: 拉丁 distractio，来自 distrahere「拉开」= 表「分开」的前缀 + trahere「拉、拖」；trahere 更深来源未得到证明，其更早词根属重构形式。英语 distraction 经法语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one gesture: something is pulled in two directions. Pulled apart physically it is the old literal sense; pulled off a task it is a distractor; the resulting split is a state; arranged for an experiment it is a controlled variable; arranged for pleasure it is amusement; pushed too far it is near-madness; arranged for an enemy it is a feint; and spread across a whole day it is fragmentation.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：某物被朝两个方向拉扯。被物理拉开是古老的字面义；被从任务上拉开是干扰项；造成的分裂是一种状态；被安排进实验是受控变量；被安排成愉悦是消遣；被推到极处是近乎发狂；被用来对付敌人是佯动；被铺满一整天是碎片化。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a desk split down the middle and sliding apart, its papers scattered on both sides.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张书桌从中间裂开、朝两边滑走，纸页散在两侧。

branches.en: THE PULLING THING: an everyday distractor, and the same thing inserted on purpose in a test.
branches.cn: 拉走注意之物：日常的干扰，与同一物被有意放进测验。

branches.en: SPLIT AND SCATTERED: a mind drawn off one task, and heed spread thin across a whole day.
branches.cn: 被分裂与被撒开：从一项任务上被引走的心，与被摊薄到一整天的留意。

branches.en: THE PLEASANT PULL: the mind turned away on purpose, with no task to lose.
branches.cn: 愉快的拉扯：有意把心思引开，且没有任务可失。

branches.en: THE PULL TOO FAR: agitation so strong that the mind cannot settle at all.
branches.cn: 拉得太过：烦躁强到心神完全无法安定。

branches.en: THE OLD AND THE STRATEGIC: a body torn apart in the archaic sense, and an enemy drawn off the real point.
branches.cn: 古老义与战术义：字面意义上被扯开的身体，与被引离真正要点的敌军。

intro.en: Distraction is a Latin verb of pulling apart, with a prefix of separation and two suffixes of action and result.
intro.cn: distraction 是一个表「拉开」的拉丁动词的后代，带表分离的前缀与表动作、结果的后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin trahere gives tractor, traction, extract and contract; dis- plus trahere gives distract and distraction.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 trahere 衍生 tractor、traction、extract、contract；表「分开」的前缀加 trahere 衍生 distract、distraction。

items.example: The verb is the oldest layer of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是词族中最老的一层。

items.example: The compound described a body torn between two pulls.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词描述被两股力扯开的身体。

items.example: The noun named both the split and the mental state.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词兼指分裂与心神状态。

items.example: The noise distracted the whole row.
items.exampleCN: 噪声让整排人都分了心。

items.meaning: the pulling away or the thing that pulls
items.example: Distraction came from every direction.
items.exampleCN: 干扰从四面八方来。

items.example: He seemed distracted all morning.
items.exampleCN: 他一上午都心不在焉。

items.example: The ticking clock was distracting.
items.exampleCN: 滴答作响的钟很让人分心。

items.example: Young children are highly distractible.
items.exampleCN: 幼儿极易分心。

definition_zh: 使分心；使转向；使不安；引开
definition_en: to draw someone's attention away from what they are doing or thinking
core_image: 一个人正低头系鞋带，一只手从旁边伸来把线头轻轻一扯，结散了；那只手没有碰人，只碰了那根线。
scene: 他正低头把鞋带系成一个结，旁边有人轻轻一扯线头，结散了，低头的人还在原地，手上的活却已经断了。A single question distracted him from the knot.
sceneCN: 这里指把注意力从正在做的事上引开（第 1 个义项：使分心）；句意为一个问题就让他的注意力离开了那个结。

pos.zh: 使分心；使转向；使不安；引开（注意力）

derivatives.zh: 分心；使人分心之物（在动词后加拉丁动作名词词尾，由动作转指该行为或造成该行为之物）
心不在焉的（加表被动的分词词尾，由「被引开」转指「心神已散」）
使人分心的（加表主动的分词词尾，由「引开」转指「正在引走注意」）
易分心的（加表「易于」的形容词词尾，由「被引开」转指「容易被引走」）

senses.title: Draw attention away
senses.definition: to make someone stop attending to one thing and attend to another
senses.definitionCN: 使某人停止留意一事而转向另一事
senses.example: A single question distracted him from the knot.
senses.exampleCN: 一个问题就让他的注意力离开了那个结。
senses.why: The prefix of apartness plus a verb of pulling gives the core: heed is pulled off its object.
senses.whyCN: 动词把某人的留意从一处挪到另一处，这一挪的核心就是「拉开」。

senses.title: Sidetrack someone from a purpose
senses.definition: to turn a person away from the aim they were pursuing, often delaying them
senses.definitionCN: 把某人从正在追求的目标上引开，常致其延误
senses.example: The dispute distracted the committee from the budget for a month.
senses.exampleCN: 这场争执让委员会一个月没能处理预算。
senses.why: A purpose can be pulled aside as a body can: the same verb, the object changed from attention to aim.
senses.whyCN: 把留意引离目标，就是把人从路上引开，因此常带延误的后果。

senses.title: Amuse a person
senses.definition: to occupy someone pleasantly so that a worry or a wait is forgotten
senses.definitionCN: 以愉快的方式占住某人，使其忘掉忧虑或等待
senses.example: He distracted the child with a paper bird while the doctor finished.
senses.exampleCN: 医生处理完之前，他用一只纸鸟哄开了孩子的注意。
senses.why: The pleasant sense keeps the structure and drops the harm: heed is moved, but nothing is lost.
senses.whyCN: 让人愉快地分神，等于用别的东西占住他的心思，仍是同一种拉扯。

senses.title: Unsettle the mind
senses.definition: to disturb someone's composure so that thought becomes difficult
senses.definitionCN: 扰乱某人的镇定，使思考变得困难
senses.example: The letter distracted her for the rest of the day.
senses.exampleCN: 那封信让她一整天都心神不宁。
senses.why: Here what is pulled away is not attention but composure, the object being the person's whole state.
senses.whyCN: 心神被扰乱也是被拉开，只是被扯开的是镇定而非留意。

senses.title: Tear apart
