senses.definition: the archaic literal sense of pulling something into pieces or in different directions
senses.definitionCN: 把某物拉成碎片或朝不同方向拉开的古老字面义
senses.example: In the older legal language, to distract a thing meant to divide it by force.
senses.exampleCN: 在较早的法律用语里，「拉开」某物指以强力把它分开。
senses.why: The literal sense is the root of the family: every later meaning keeps the image of two opposed pulls.
senses.whyCN: 古义仍是物理的：把物体拉成碎片，或拉向不同方向。

senses.title: Draw off an enemy
senses.definition: to cause an opponent's force to move away from the real point of action
senses.definitionCN: 使对方力量离开真正的行动要点
senses.example: Two companies distracted the garrison while the bridge was taken.
senses.exampleCN: 两个连引开守军，同时桥被拿下。
senses.why: Military use keeps the literal pull: a force is drawn off the point it should hold.
senses.whyCN: 军事用法保留字面的拉：一支部队被从应守之处拉开。

senses.title: Draw a defender away
senses.definition: in sport, to pull a marker out of position so that space opens elsewhere
senses.definitionCN: 体育中指把盯防者引离位置，从而在别处露出空当
senses.example: The winger distracted the full-back and the centre ran through.
senses.exampleCN: 边锋引开边后卫，中锋从中间穿了过去。
senses.why: Sport borrows the military pattern in miniature: a pull that creates room rather than a fight.
senses.whyCN: 体育里被拉开的是盯防位置，空当因此出现在别处。

senses.title: Split one's own focus
senses.definition: to divide one's own heed deliberately between two things, usually to the loss of both
senses.definitionCN: 有意把自己的留意分给两处，通常两处都受损
senses.example: He distracted himself with the radio and missed the turn.
senses.exampleCN: 他用收音机分了自己的心，结果错过了转弯。
senses.why: The verb can take the self as both actor and object, which shows how easily the pull becomes internal.
senses.whyCN: 把自己分成两处，仍是拉开，只是施动者与受动者同为一人。

intro.en: Distract comes from Latin distractus, the participle of distrahere 'to pull apart', built on dis- 'apart' plus trahere 'to draw, drag'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: distract 出自拉丁 distractus，即 distrahere「拉开」的分词，由表「分开」的前缀加 trahere「拉、拖」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Trahere meant 'to draw, drag, pull'. Its deeper origin is not established; any older root proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: trahere 意为「拉、拖、拽」。其更深来源未得到证明；凡为其提出的更早词根都是重构形式。

items.en: Dis- 'apart' plus trahere gave distrahere 'to pull apart, draw off in different directions'.
items.cn: 表「分开」的前缀加 trahere 构成 distrahere「拉开、朝不同方向引开」。

items.en: The participle distractus described what had been pulled apart, and English took the verb form from it.
items.cn: 分词 distractus 描述已被拉开之物，英语由此取得动词形式。

items.en: Distract is recorded in English in the sixteenth century, first for pulling the mind away and for dividing by force.
items.cn: distract 在十六世纪的英语中已有记录，最初指把心思引开，也指以强力分开。

items.en: Sport, military writing and child care each took the verb for their own kind of deliberate pulling away.
items.cn: 体育、军事写作与育儿各自取用这个动词，指自己那一类有意的引开。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper origin): no exact first citation is fixed, and the pre-Latin root of trahere is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：没有确切的最早书证；trahere 在拉丁语之前的词根属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds forms of the same verb of pulling apart; group two holds verbs of turning something aside.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「拉开」这一动词的词形；第二组是把某物引向别处的动词。

entries.definition: Names the pulling away or the thing that causes it; the verb names the act done to a person.
entries.definitionCN: 指引开的动作或造成它的事物；动词指对人所做的那个动作。

entries.definition: An adjective for the person after the pull has worked; it is the state, not the act.
entries.definitionCN: 形容被引开之后的人；是状态，而非动作。

entries.definition: An adjective for what does the pulling; it describes a thing or an event, not a person.
entries.definitionCN: 形容做出「拉」的那一方；描述事物或事件，而非人。

entries.definition: From a Latin verb of pressing tight or hampering; it means to cause pain or hardship, not to divide attention.
entries.definitionCN: 出自一个表「压紧、阻碍」的拉丁动词；意为造成痛苦或困苦，而非分散注意。

entries.definition: To turn something aside from its course, as traffic or funds; it names the redirection but not the loss of heed.
entries.definitionCN: 指把某物的路线引开，如交通或资金；指改变方向，却不含留意受损之意。

entries.definition: To move a person or a discussion onto a secondary matter; it is the second sense of distract in everyday words.
entries.definitionCN: 指把人或讨论引到次要的事情上；是 distract 第二义的日常说法。

entries.definition: To make someone uneasy or uncertain; it matches the fourth sense and says nothing about attention.
entries.definitionCN: 指使人不安或把握不定；对应第四义，且完全不说注意力。

entries.definition: To hold someone's interest pleasantly; it is the third sense of distract without the idea of a task abandoned.
entries.definitionCN: 指以愉快的方式占住某人的兴趣；是 distract 第三义去掉「任务被弃」的版本。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: A prefix of apartness on a verb of pulling: to pull a mind off what it was holding.
normal.cn: 表「分开」的前缀加表「拉」的动词：把心从它握着东西上拉开。

normal.en: The family runs distraction, distracted, distracting and distractible, all from one verb of pulling apart.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 distraction、distracted、distracting、distractible，全出同一个表「拉开」的动词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the directions: distract someone from work, distract attention, distract the defender.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出方向：使人从工作中分心、引开注意力、引开防守者。

normal.en: The verb can take the self as its object, which is how the pull becomes internal.
normal.cn: 这个动词可以把自己当作对象，拉扯于是变成内在的。

normal.en: The archaic sense is tearing apart, and every modern sense keeps that image of two opposed pulls.
normal.cn: 古老义是撕裂，而每个现代义都保留「两股相反的力」这一形象。

abstract.en: Picture a finger pulling one loose end of a knot while the hands stay still.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指扯住绳结的一头，而双手还停在原处。

abstract.en: Picture a paper bird held up so a child forgets the needle.
abstract.cn: 想象一只纸鸟被举起，孩子于是忘了针。

abstract.en: Picture a winger running wide so the middle opens.
abstract.cn: 想象边锋跑向边路，中路于是空出来。

examples.en: The ringing phone distracted her from the sentence she was writing.
examples.cn: 响起的电话让她从正在写的那句话上分了心。

examples.en: He distracted the child with a story while the nurse prepared the syringe.
examples.cn: 护士准备针管时，他讲了个故事哄开孩子的注意。

examples.en: The decoy force distracted the garrison long enough to cross the river.
examples.cn: 佯动部队引开守军，争取到渡河的时间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「分开」+「拉」——把心从原处拉开：拉去别的事是分心，拉去玩是哄，拉去别处是引开。

root: 拉丁 distractus，为 distrahere「拉开」的分词 = 表「分开」的前缀 + trahere「拉、拖」；trahere 更深来源未得到证明，其更早词根属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one act: something is pulled off what it was holding. Pulled off a task it is distraction; pulled off a purpose it delays a committee; pulled off a worry it amuses a child; pulled off composure it unsettles; pulled apart in the old sense it divides by force; pulled off a position it draws off a garrison or a defender; and pulled by oneself it splits one's own focus.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：把某物从它所握的东西上拉开。从任务上拉开是分心；从目的上拉开是延误委员会；从忧虑上拉开是哄孩子；从镇定上拉开是使不安；按旧义拉开是以强力分裂；从阵位上拉开是引开守军或防守者；被自己拉开则是自拆注意力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger pulling one loose end of a knot while the hands themselves stay still.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根手指扯住绳结的一头，而双手本身仍停在原处。

branches.en: OFF THE TASK, OFF THE AIM: heed moved to another object, and a whole committee delayed.
branches.cn: 离开任务、离开目标：留意被移到另一物，与整个委员会被延误。

branches.en: THE HARMLESS PULL: a child occupied so that a worry or a wait is forgotten.
branches.cn: 无害的拉扯：孩子的注意被占住，忧虑或等待于是被忘掉。

branches.en: THE INNER PULL: composure shaken from outside, and focus split from inside.
branches.cn: 内在的拉扯：镇定被外面撼动，与焦点被自己拆开。

branches.en: THE OLD TEARING: the literal sense of dividing a thing by force.
branches.cn: 古老的撕裂：以强力把事物分开的字面义。

branches.en: DRAWN OFF A POSITION: a garrison moved from the bridge, and a defender moved from the middle.
branches.cn: 被引离阵位：从桥边被调开的守军，与从中路被引开的防守者。

intro.en: Distract is a Latin participle used as an English verb, with a prefix of separation and a root of pulling.
intro.cn: distract 是拉丁分词用作英语动词，带表分离的前缀与表「拉」的词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin trahere gives traction, tractor, extract and subtract; dis- plus trahere gives distract, distraction and distractible.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 trahere 衍生 traction、tractor、extract、subtract；表「分开」的前缀加 trahere 衍生 distract、distraction、distractible。

items.example: The root carries the image of force applied sideways.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根带着「从侧面施力」的形象。

items.example: The compound added opposition to the pull.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词给「拉」加上了相反的方向。

items.example: The participle became the English verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词成为英语动词。

items.example: Nothing distracted him from the proof.
items.exampleCN: 没有什么让他从证明上分心。

items.example: The traffic outside was a constant distraction.
items.exampleCN: 外面的车流是持续的干扰。

items.example: He gave a distracted answer.
items.exampleCN: 他心不在焉地答了一句。

items.example: The bright screen was distracting.
items.exampleCN: 发亮的屏幕很让人分心。

items.example: The class was young and distractible.
items.exampleCN: 这个班年纪小，容易分心。

definition_en: the state of knowing that something exists or is happening, or of noticing it
core_image: 夜里走过一条熟悉的街，忽然注意到墙根有一盏从未亮过的小灯；灯一直在那里，只是今天才被看见。
scene: 夜里走过一条熟悉的街，他忽然注意到墙根有一盏从未亮过的小灯，灯一直在那里，只是今天才被看见。The awareness of the small lamp changed the whole street.
sceneCN: 这里指对某事物的存在有所察觉（第 1 个义项：觉察到某事存在）；句意为对这盏小灯的觉察改变了整条街的样子。

pos.zh: 意识；觉察；认识；警觉（不可数，偶尔可数指具体的认识）

derivatives.zh: 觉察到的；知道的（古英语 gewær「警觉的」，由「警觉」转指「知道」）
未觉察的（加表否定的前缀，由「知道」转指「不知道」）
未觉察（在 unaware 后加表性质的名词词尾，由形容词转指该状态）
谨慎；戒心（同出古英语表「警觉」的形容词，由「警觉」转指「防备」）
谨慎地（由 wary 加副词词尾，由「警觉」转指行事方式）

senses.title: Knowing that something exists
senses.definition: the state of having knowledge that something is there or is the case
senses.definitionCN: 知道某物在那里或某事属实的状况
senses.example: The awareness of the small lamp changed the whole street.
senses.exampleCN: 对这盏小灯的觉察改变了整条街的样子。
senses.why: The word is built on an old adjective of watchfulness, so its core is not knowledge in the abstract but a mind that is switched on.
senses.whyCN: 名词把「知道有这回事」说成一种状态，而不指具体的知识内容。

senses.title: Conscious awareness
senses.definition: in psychology, the state in which a stimulus is registered by a conscious mind
senses.definitionCN: 心理学指刺激被有意识的心智登记到的状态
senses.example: Awareness of the light dimmed as the drug took effect.
senses.exampleCN: 随着药效起来，对光亮的觉察变弱了。
senses.why: The laboratory narrows the everyday state to what can be reported by a subject.
senses.whyCN: 心理学把状态收窄：刺激必须被有意识的心智登记，才算进入察觉。

senses.title: Public consciousness of an issue
senses.definition: the degree to which a society as a whole knows about a problem or a cause
senses.definitionCN: 整个社会对某一问题或事业的知晓程度
senses.example: The campaign raised awareness of the river's pollution.
senses.exampleCN: 这场运动提高了人们对那条河污染的认识。
senses.why: The noun is used for a collective state, which is why it can be raised, measured and campaigned for.
senses.whyCN: 把个人的知道放大到社会，这种状态便成了公共议题的指标。

senses.title: Awareness of oneself
senses.definition: the ability to notice one's own states, habits and effects on others
senses.definitionCN: 察觉自身状态、习惯及对他人影响的能力
senses.example: Years of criticism left him with little self-awareness.
senses.exampleCN: 多年的批评让他几乎没有自我觉察。
senses.why: Turning the noticing back on the noticer is the reflexive use of the same noun.
senses.whyCN: 把察觉转回察觉者自身，就是同一个名词的反身用法。

senses.title: Vigilance about a situation
senses.definition: the readiness to notice changes or hazards in one's surroundings
senses.definitionCN: 对周围变化或危险的注意准备
senses.example: The pilot's situational awareness kept the crew out of the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 飞行员的情境警觉让机组避开了风暴。
senses.why: Awareness here is not a state but a skill kept up under load.
senses.whyCN: 警觉是把察觉对准周围，对象从自身换成环境。

senses.title: Awareness of one's own learning
senses.definition: the learner's knowledge of what they understand and what they do not
senses.definitionCN: 学习者对自己懂什么、不懂什么的了解
senses.example: Metacognitive awareness lets a student stop and reread.
senses.exampleCN: 元认知觉察使学生停下来重读。
senses.why: The learner is both the one who knows and the thing known, so the noun turns reflexive again.
senses.whyCN: 学习者既是知道的人，也是被知道的对象，名词再次反身。

senses.title: Mindfulness
senses.definition: the practiced attention to one's present experience, cultivated on purpose
senses.definitionCN: 有意培养的对当下体验的持续注意
senses.example: The retreat taught awareness of breath and posture.
senses.exampleCN: 这次静修教人觉照呼吸与姿态。
senses.why: Contemplative practice uses the word for attention deliberately kept open and unhurried.
senses.whyCN: 正念是把察觉有意停在此刻，并当作可练习的功夫。

senses.title: A noticer's eye
senses.definition: the quality of noticing what others pass over, as in a writer's or an artist's work
senses.definitionCN: 察觉他人忽略之处的品质，如作家或艺术家作品中的
senses.example: The novel has an awareness of small gestures that most readers miss.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说对细小手势有觉察，而多数读者会忽略它们。
senses.why: The noun can describe a body of work, where awareness is a style of seeing rather than a mental state.
senses.whyCN: 作家与艺术家捕捉他人略过之处，末一个义项便指这种捕捉的品质。

intro.en: Awareness is the adjective aware plus the noun suffix -ness. Aware goes back to Old English gewær 'watchful, vigilant'. There is no Latin element in the word. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: awareness 是形容词 aware 加表性质的名词词尾构成。aware 上溯古英语 gewær「警觉的、警醒的」。词中不含拉丁成分。年代均为约数。

items.en: Gewær meant 'watchful, vigilant, cautious'. Its deeper origin is not established; the Germanic adjective behind it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: gewær 意为「警觉的、警醒的、谨慎的」。其更深来源未得到证明；其背后的日耳曼语形容词属重构形式。

items.en: The adjective is reconstructed as a Germanic word meaning 'wary, watchful', and it is related to the verb that gives English warn.
items.cn: 这个形容词被重构为一个意为「戒备、警觉」的日耳曼语词，与给出英语 warn 的那个动词相关。

items.en: The modern form aware developed in Middle English, where it meant 'watchful' before it meant 'informed'.
items.cn: 现代形式 aware 在中古英语中形成，先指「警觉」，后指「知情」。

items.en: Awareness is a later noun formed on the adjective with the suffix -ness, naming the state rather than the person.
items.cn: awareness 是后起名词，在形容词后加表性质的名词词尾，指状态而非人。

items.en: Psychology, public campaigning and contemplative practice each gave the noun a distinct modern use in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries.
items.cn: 心理学、公共倡导与静修实践在十九至二十世纪各自赋予这个名词一种现代用法。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Germanic source of the adjective is not established, and the reconstructed Germanic form is a reconstruction, not a recorded word.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：这个形容词在日耳曼语之前的来源未得到证明，所重构的日耳曼语形式属重构，并非有记录的词。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Old English stock of watchfulness; group two holds nouns of knowing and noticing.
note.cn: 第一组是同出古英语「警觉」词干的词；第二组是表示知晓与察觉的名词。

entries.definition: Describes someone who knows or notices; the noun names that state as a thing.
entries.definitionCN: 形容知道或察觉的人；名词把该状态当作一个事物来命名。

entries.definition: Describes someone who does not know; it is the direct opposite and very common in warnings.
entries.definitionCN: 形容不知道的人；是直接反义，常见于警示语。

entries.definition: The state of being cautious about a possible harm; it shares the old root but keeps the defensive sense.
entries.definitionCN: 指对可能之害保持谨慎的状态；共用古老词根，却保留防备义。

entries.definition: To tell someone of a danger so that they become aware of it; it is the act that produces the state.
entries.definitionCN: 指告知某人危险以使其察觉；是产生该状态的动作。

entries.definition: The general capacity to be awake and experience; awareness is one strand of it, often directed at an object.
entries.definitionCN: 指清醒并能体验的整体能力；awareness 是其中一股，常指向某个对象。

entries.definition: The state of being watchful and ready to respond, usually to a risk; it is awareness under pressure.
entries.definitionCN: 指警觉并准备反应的状态，通常针对风险；是在压力下的 awareness。

entries.definition: The deliberate, non-judgemental attention to the present; it is awareness as a practice rather than a state.
entries.definitionCN: 指对当下有意且不加评判的注意；是作为修习而非状态的 awareness。

entries.definition: The process of sensing and interpreting what is there; awareness is the knowing that follows perception.
entries.definitionCN: 指感知并解释眼前之物的过程；awareness 是感知之后的「知道」。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: An old adjective of watchfulness plus a suffix of state: the condition of being switched on.
normal.cn: 一个表「警觉」的古老形容词加表状态的后缀：处于「开着」的状况。

normal.en: The family runs aware, unaware, wariness and warn, all from one Germanic stock of watching.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 aware、unaware、wariness、warn，全出同一个表「看守」的日耳曼词干。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the fields: raise awareness of, public awareness, self-awareness, situational awareness.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：提高对……的认识、公众意识、自我觉察、情境警觉。

normal.en: The noun is collective as well as personal: a campaign raises it, a pilot keeps it.
normal.cn: 这个名词既指个人状态，也指集体状态：运动提高它，飞行员保持它。

normal.en: The word has no Latin layer, so every attempt to read it as a Latin derivative is a false lead.
normal.cn: 这个词没有拉丁层，凡把它读作拉丁派生词的做法都是歧路。

abstract.en: Picture a small lamp on a familiar wall that only becomes visible tonight.
abstract.cn: 想象熟悉墙根上的一盏小灯，只在今夜才变得可见。

abstract.en: Picture a switched-on radio in a room everyone had thought silent.
abstract.cn: 想象一间人人以为安静的屋里，其实有台开着的收音机。

abstract.en: Picture a hand noticing the grain of a table it has used for years.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手忽然注意到用了多年那张桌子的木纹。

examples.en: The film raised awareness of the conditions in the mills.
examples.cn: 这部影片提高了人们对工厂里劳动条件的认识。

examples.en: A pilot's situational awareness matters more than reaction speed.
examples.cn: 飞行员的情境警觉比反应速度更重要。

examples.en: Regular practice gradually increases awareness of one's own habits.
examples.cn: 持续的练习会逐渐提高对自己习惯的觉察。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「警觉」+ 表状态的名词词尾——心是开着的：知道某事在，是觉察；知道自己在，是自察；知道四周在变，是警觉。

root: 古英语 gewær「警觉的、谨慎的」加表性质的名词词尾；gewær 更深来源未得到证明，其背后的日耳曼语形容词属重构形式。词中无拉丁成分。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one state: a mind switched on to something. Switched on to a thing it is awareness of it; to a stimulus under test it is conscious registration; to an issue across a society it is public consciousness; to oneself it is self-awareness; to a situation it is vigilance; to one's own learning it is metacognition; to the present moment it is mindfulness; and as a body of work it is a noticer's eye.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种状态展开：心对某物是开着的。对某物开着是对它的觉察；对测验中的刺激开着是有意识的登记；对整个社会的一个议题开着是公众意识；对自己开着是自我觉察；对处境开着是警觉；对自己的学习开着是元认知；对当下开着是觉照；若表现在一整部作品里，则是善察的眼光。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small lamp on a familiar wall that has been there all along and is seen for the first time tonight.
core.cn: 核心意象：熟悉墙根上的一盏小灯，一直在那里，今夜才第一次被看见。

branches.en: THE STATE AND ITS LAB FORM: knowing that something is there, and the same knowing recorded by a subject.
branches.cn: 状态与它的实验形式：知道某物在那里，与同一份知道被试者报告出来。

branches.en: THE COLLECTIVE FORM: a whole society's knowledge of an issue, which can be raised like a level.
branches.cn: 集体形态：整个社会对某议题的知晓，可以像水位一样被提高。

branches.en: TURNED INWARD: noticing one's own habits and their effects.
branches.cn: 转向自身：察觉自己的习惯及其影响。

branches.en: UNDER LOAD: watchfulness kept up in a situation that can change without warning.
branches.cn: 在负荷之下：在随时可能变化的处境里保持警觉。

branches.en: THREE CULTIVATED FORMS: knowing one's own understanding, attending to the present, and a noticer's eye in a body of work.
branches.cn: 三种被培养的形态：知道自己懂什么、注意当下，以及作品里那双善察的眼。

intro.en: Awareness is native English: an old adjective of watchfulness and a suffix of state, with no Latin layer.
intro.cn: awareness 是纯英语本族词：一个表「警觉」的古老形容词加表状态的后缀，没有拉丁层。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin element here, so the Latin list is left empty; the older strata are Germanic only.
latinIntro.cn: 此处不含拉丁成分，因此拉丁条目留空；更早的层次纯属日耳曼语。

items.example: The adjective described a mind on guard.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述一颗戒备着的心。

items.example: She was aware of the risk before anyone spoke.
items.exampleCN: 在任何人开口之前，她就察觉到了风险。

items.meaning: the state of knowing or noticing
items.example: Awareness of the rule spread slowly.
items.exampleCN: 对这条规则的认识传播得很慢。

items.example: He was unaware that the room had emptied.
items.exampleCN: 他没察觉屋里已经空了。

items.example: Unawareness of the deadline caused the delay.
items.exampleCN: 没意识到截止日期，导致了延误。

items.example: She was wary of the offer.
items.exampleCN: 她对这份提议抱有戒心。

items.example: His wariness kept him from signing.
items.exampleCN: 他的戒心让他没有签字。

items.example: They warned the village about the flood.
items.exampleCN: 他们提醒村庄注意洪水。
